epigraph.quote: Every southern child's first chore is the Cluckmaw coop. Every southern child's first bite is from a Cluckmaw.

title: Quillhen
subtitle: Pirrak · Table tradition
summary: A small feathered saurian kept for eggs, meat, and useful quills.

sections.title: Form and character
paragraphs: Quillhen plumes supply writing quills, fletching, and adornment. Eggs and meat also make the birdlike saurian valuable to southern households.

sections.title: In southern life
paragraphs: Pirrak is the older Kalvatari name for this feathered hen of the Southern Wilds.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A Jakupur scribe swears his quillhen's quills only write the truth.” (heard in Jakupur)

source: Bible Complete · Volume XIII, Part Two: The Breeds

illustration.label: Quillhen: Pirrak
illustration.alt: A feathered Quillhen stands beside collected plumes and an adult keeper’s basket.
illustration.caption: A feathered Quillhen stands beside collected plumes and an adult keeper’s basket.

epigraph.quote: Eggs for breakfast, quills for the letter you write after it.

title: Gloamhide
subtitle: Xolca · Dusk tradition
summary: A stealthy nocturnal hunter whose color-shifting hide vanishes into jungle light.

sections.title: Form and character
paragraphs: Almost impossible to tame, the Gloamhide is a quiet danger of the deep paths. The rare trained Xolca is a remarkable hunting-beast.

sections.title: In southern life
paragraphs: Its shifting coloration makes it difficult to distinguish from dappled foliage and shadow. The Kalvatari name is Xolca.

sections.title: In the stables and the wild
paragraphs: The twilight stalker: a stealthy, color-shifting nocturnal predator, near-invisible in dappled jungle light. Almost impossible to tame; the rare trained Xolca is a peerless hunting-beast, and the wild ones are a quiet terror of the deep paths.

sections.title: What the handlers say
paragraphs: The twilight stalker, so rare and so deadly that some doubt it exists. The White Flame keeps a standing bounty on wild ones; a trained one is a peerless hunting-beast.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The White Flame's bounty on wild gloamhides was paid twice last year, both times for the same animal.” (heard in Jakupur)

source: Bible Complete · Volume XIII, Part Two: The Breeds

illustration.label: Gloamhide: Xolca
illustration.alt: A wild Gloamhide’s color-shifting outline emerges from the dusk jungle.
illustration.caption: A wild Gloamhide’s color-shifting outline emerges from the dusk jungle.

epigraph.quote: If you can see it, it's already decided you're not worth the trouble.

title: The Cycle
subtitle: Ten days. One turn.
summary: The ten-day week. It runs straight through the months and the Still Days without ever starting over.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The week is the Cycle: ten days, named in order. The Cycle runs straight through the months and the Still Days without ever starting over, so you name a day by its Cycle-name and its date.

rows: Sailing and trade: the day to weigh anchor
The dead and the ancestors; never set sail on a Graveday
Market day; debts paid; Pocchin caravans roll into town
The islands' day off: temple, tidecall, and the long meal

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Cindren of Everfall say the Glass Forest chimed thirteen times last Graveday, and it has only ever chimed in twelves.” (an Ash Warden)

title: The Two Moons and the Tides
subtitle: Two moons pull the road.
summary: Valtaire turns in 36 days and makes the month; Ciel turns in 57. When they pull together the tides run high.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Ors is the sun. You rise with Ors, swear by Ors, and squint against Ors at noon.
Valtaire, the great near silver moon, turns in 36 days. Its turn is the month.
Ciel, small, pale, and far, turns in 57 days.
When the moons pull together the tides run high; when they pull apart the tides go slack.

Liora's lovers. The harbors say both moons love Liora. Valtaire comes full on Liora 18th to court her; Ciel wanders off and comes back. When both call on her at once, the King Tide rises with the quarrel.
Harbor children learn the moons by chalking the morning's high-water line on the harbor steps: the Chalk Tide.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Pale moons. New Tides ring dull, say the scale-men of Fairweather, and they have started weighing them. The Mint says nothing.” (common talk)

title: Coins and Prices
subtitle: What a day is worth.
summary: Bit, Tide, Anchor, Orsal: each worth ten of the one before. Three Bits are a laborer's day; an Anchor a month; an Orsal a year.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The coins of the Council:
Bit: copper, with a hole in the middle for stringing. Thirty on a cord make a string, a laborer's Cycle.
Tide: silver, stamped with the two moons over a wave. Worth 10 Bits.
Anchor: gold, stamped with a ship's anchor over a wave. Worth 10 Tides, or 100 Bits. A counterfeit is a drowned Anchor.

Orsal: a heavy square of gold stamped with the face of Ors, and numbered; worth 10 Anchors. It pays for ships, dowries, land, and ransoms, and most people never hold one. Old folk still call it a sun.
Regional names. The Orsal is the Orsal everywhere, but the three common coins go by local names:

sections.title: At a glance
paragraphs: What money means:
A Bit buys a fishbread, a mug of ale, or a cup of brightleaf.
Three Bits are a laborer's day. An Anchor is a laborer's month. An Orsal is a laborer's year.
Wages, by the month:
Laborer: 1 Anchor.
Journeyman: 2 Anchors.
Clerk: 3 Anchors.
Master craftsman: 4 to 6 Anchors.
Physician: 10 to 15 Anchors.
Merchant captain: 15 to 30 Anchors.
Fleetlord: 100 Anchors.

sections.title: At a glance
paragraphs: Magic is never a catalog. A market town has one or two worked pieces for sale, if any. Goldwind has dozens. Every legal sale pays the Registry's tenth.
Two makes: everything ordinary comes in harbor make, local and cheap, and proof make, guild-stamped and about ten times the price.
Debts freeze in the Still Days. Coinsday is settling day everywhere.
Off the coin-roads, people barter:
Salt and iron nails on the outer Frontier.
University scrip among Goldwind's scholars.
Cacao beans, jade beads, saurian teeth, and worked feathers in the deep Wilds.
Whale-oil, dried fish, and furs on the ice.
Pressed leaf-bricks of brightleaf aboard ship.

rows: A meal at a tavern's common table
A night in a private room at a decent inn
Deck passage from Goldwind to Southhaven
1 Anchor (a harbor-made one costs a tenth)
A good sword, good armor, or a rare firearm
A monster contract for a Gold
50 Anchors: five years of a laborer's pay

title: Sayings You'll Hear
subtitle: The islands have a word for it.
summary: Hold or drown. Coin remembers. The jungle keeps its own. The ice forgives nothing. Be kind to the water.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: "Hold or drown." The Frontier.
"Coin remembers." The Heartland.
"A smile in Goldwind has two faces." The Heartland.
"The jungle keeps its own." The south.
"Paper burns, skin remembers." The south.
"The ice forgives nothing." The ice.
"Be kind to the water." Everywhere.
"The tide calls it." It's settled.
"Playing last water." The desperate end of anything.
"Tie your knot." Get your affairs in order.
"By the Three Nights!" and "By Ors!"
"Drown me."
"Tide's with you." Good luck.
"Someone kept the fire on that one." Quiet, unthanked work.
"The sill provides."
"We still have salt between us." This isn't over.
"Still carrying iron." A rookie holding an iron who has not yet sat the Trials.
"The chant remembers what the page forgets."
"Salt and kin!" answered by "Fair tide home!" The toast.

title: The Talk of 175 EC
subtitle: What the ports are saying.
summary: The King Tide is due in 177, the Charterhouse has won the salt monopoly, and the Legion is pushing north.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The headlines:
The King Tide is due in 177. Coastal land is quietly changing hands.
The Charterhouse Company won the southern salt monopoly. Two ports rioted; the brass-collars "restored order."
Crimson Legion raids are pushing north of Golgarma. The Emerald Wrath has asked for another squadron; the Council is "reviewing."
A new island has surfaced off the southern lanes. Three claims are filed, and the first survey crew is a week overdue.
Returned Crown pamphlets, calling to invite the Imperium back "on honorable terms," keep appearing in Ironfort. Nobody has found the printers.
Names on everyone's lips:
The Last Smile, pirate queen of the Free Tide.
Harrow Mane, the reaver-lord too brutal even for her.
The Crimson Legion and the Scarlet Mother.
The Midnight Patron of Karn Sorroch.
The Registrar, hunting unlicensed casters in Goldwind's fog.
Mother Kess of Varan Port.
The Returned Crown and the Tollmen, in the north.
The Southern Rebels, the Reclaimers, and the Chainbreakers, in the south.

title: Assios and the Wider World
subtitle: A region of the charted sea
summary: North across the strait lies Assios and the Korvan Imperium. West lies Khard Muur, and cursed Xathnatraz. Most of the world is only rumor.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Assios lies north of the Frontier across the strait, and only its southern coast is in view from the Ironfort quay on a clear day.

It is the seat of the Korvan Imperium under Emperor Theomar Vol Sunessi and his Inquisition: the militant creed of human inheritance, which roots out heresy, polices magic, and burns what it cannot convert.

The Imperium is the empire the Exodus fled. It still fights the Thousand-Year War against the Alliance of Baronies and the Free Cities, and it presses Kalvatar with coin and cult rather than open fleets.
Refugees and spies wash south constantly. Steel, wine, and books come through the gate; Free City firearms are carried south by smugglers; registered Krysta goes north.
The archipelago's dragonborn came from Assios, as refugees, exiles, and traders of the long war.
Khard Muur is a wild continent beyond the western ocean, of ruined kingdoms and unsettled wilds. Off its southwest coast lies Xathnatraz.
The wider world holds other continents, known to the archipelago only by rumor and the occasional wreck.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Nobody has ever painted the Imperium's Grand Inquisitor. The Frontier spies who claim to have seen him won't say what he looked like.” (an Ironfort customs clerk)
“Sailors back from Khard Muur say Valengrad crowned King Rune last year. They crowned him the year before too, and he was buried in between.” (a sailor back from the west)

facts: the Baronies and the Free Cities

title: The Wrong Coast
subtitle: Plague waters. Closed horizon.
summary: The quarantined waters of the far south, closed since 148 EC. The Council calls them plague waters. Sailors tell of grey ships and the Hum.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Sealed Waters of the far south, where the Wilds fray into the ice, have been closed by Council order since 148 EC as "plague waters."
Southern sailors call them the Wrong Coast.
They tell stories of grey ships with no names that sail without lanterns.
They tell of the Hum, a note under hearing that you feel in the hull on calm nights. Never hum along.
Southern custom: carry a silver Tide in your boot when you sail south, and lay a silver Tide on the tongue of the dead.
Compasses behave there, the stars behave, the sea behaves, and that, the sailors say, is what is wrong with it: it behaves as if it is holding its breath.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Wrong Coast. The quarantined waters of the far south are "plague waters," the Council says. Southern sailors tell stories of grey ships with no names that sail without lanterns, and of the Hum: a note under hearing that you feel in the hull on calm nights. Never hum along.” (common talk)

title: Aurelion
subtitle: A place of the Central Heartland
summary: Aurelion is the forge-city of the north coast, and the seat of the Sunforge house.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Aurelion is the forge-city of the north coast, and the seat of the Sunforge house. Its smoke is visible from Goldwind on a clear day, and its metalwork, firearms, and goldsmithery fill the Congress's warehouses. The Sunforge house is the master-smith house of the Heartland, fabulously wealthy and deeply tied to the Congress. Its forges, the Sunforge works, are the only place in the Heartland where a firearm can be made to proof standard, and the Aurelion smiths guard the secret of that proof as closely as the Council guards its seats.

title: Bastion
subtitle: A place of the Northern Frontier
summary: Bastion is the seat of House Faust, the gate-fortress of the north.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Bastion is the seat of House Faust, the gate-fortress of the north. It stands on a fortified island at the mouth of the eastern sea-road, with a curtain wall that has held off every fleet that tested it. The Faust garrison is the largest standing force in the archipelago outside the Armada, and the house's remount farms supply horses to half the Frontier. The Bastion tourneys in the summer are the great martial spectacle of the north, and the winners carry the Faust sigil home with them as a mark of standing. Johann Faust, the captain of the Jubilant and a celebrated Hunter, is the house's most famous son, and his divided loyalty between blood and oath is the house's most discussed private trouble.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Kastan Vol Kaern is buying Bastion's debts through the Zane house. He will own the Frontier's gate before the Council knows he has begun.” (heard in the Central Heartland)

title: Black Harbor
subtitle: A place of the Northern Frontier
summary: Black Harbor is the smugglers' capital of the Frontier, a warren of wharves and sea-caves in the fog below Greyhaven.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Black Harbor is the smugglers' capital of the Frontier, a warren of wharves and sea-caves in the fog below Greyhaven. It is the home of the Fogrunners, who carry untaxed cargo through the Murk by bell-codes so exact they can thread the Widow's Teeth blind. Its leader, Wenna Hollis, the Bellmistress, has never been caught, because no officer of the Gate-Tithe has ever been able to hear what she is saying. The Gullet, a tide-cave that leads down into the Below, opens at the harbor's north end, and the Fogrunners use it when the Council's patrols are thickest on the surface.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The dry road. The roads Below run island to island, and a smuggler who knew them could walk a cargo from Black Harbor to Goldwind without paying a single harbor due.” (common talk)

illustration.alt: Sailors unload a boat on the fog-bound wharves of Black Harbor beneath Greyhaven.
illustration.caption: Fog and bell-codes shelter the Frontier’s untaxed trade.

title: Briarcrown
subtitle: A place of the Central Heartland
summary: Briarcrown is the seat of House Silverthorn, a fortified town on a hill above the eastern shore.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Briarcrown is the seat of House Silverthorn, a fortified town on a hill above the eastern shore. It is quiet, prosperous, and watchful, with a reputation for discretion that is nearly a crime in itself. Its houses have high walls and silent gardens, and the Silverthorn spies keep a register of every visitor to the Heartland's shadow markets. The house's rivalry with House Alastor is cold and deep. Neither trusts the other, and both trade in secrets for a living.

title: Crystalhaven
subtitle: A place of the Icy Expanse
summary: Crystalhaven is a wrecking-town on the blue-ice coast.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Crystalhaven is a wrecking-town on the blue-ice coast. Its harbor is a half-moon of frozen water, and its streets are lined with the hulls of ships that came in with a light in their eyes and never went out. The False Lights are the town's wreckers, who hang false lanterns on the cliffs to lure ships onto the ice, and then strip the wreck. Granny Ylva Skerrow is the wreckers' matriarch, a tiny woman with a voice like a foghorn and a memory for every ship she has ever lured. Southern captains say "not every kind coast is kind" when they pass the blue-ice cliffs, and they make the sign of the Answering Light as they sail on.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Mira has been seen at Crystalhaven with Granny Skerrow's grandson. A smuggler's heir is never seen with a wrecker's grandson unless one of them means to take the other's chair.” (heard in the Icy Expanse)

title: Duskmire Haven
subtitle: A place of the Central Heartland
summary: Duskmire Haven is a misty fen near Goldwind, a town of stilt-houses and reed-boats where the Registry's writ grows thin.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Duskmire Haven is a misty fen near Goldwind, a town of stilt-houses and reed-boats where the Registry's writ grows thin. It is the home of the Mint-in-the-Mire, the coiners whose drowned Anchors are so good that the Council's mint has twice bought them back by mistake. The master engraver is Ottar Glimm, a gnome of terrible genius and worse temper. The Knot, the market below Duskmire kept by goblins, opens in the fen's deepest reed-beds, and the goblins permit no names, no blades, and no light brighter than a candle.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Goldspire's heir was seen at a pawnbroker's on the Duskmire road, in a borrowed cloak.” (a Duskmire pawnbroker's boy)

title: Easthold, Westwatch, and Pearl Groove
subtitle: A place of the Central Heartland
summary: Easthold is the fishing port of the east coast, with its fleets, herb-gardens, and seafood markets.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Easthold is the fishing port of the east coast, with its fleets, herb-gardens, and seafood markets. Westwatch is the mining town of the western heights, its quarries and coal-pits supplying the Heartland's stone and fuel. Pearl Groove is a shallow lagoon of pearl-clans, where the divers work the beds under the watchful eyes of the Belmaris house and its bell-mistress. The pearls and the murex-dyed reefpurple are the region's most exclusive exports, and the Coral Kingdoms' sound-trade passes through the Groove on the way to the Congress.

title: Elyria
subtitle: A place of the Central Heartland
summary: Elyria is the elven hold of House Caelvaron, the only major seat ruled by the deathless.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Elyria is the elven hold of House Caelvaron, the only major seat ruled by the deathless. Its towers are white and pale green, set among ancient trees on the eastern hills. The Caelvaron rulers rotate on the Hundred-Year Cycle, and the Elyria court is the most patient and least hurried in the Heartland. The elves of Elyria remember grudges older than the Charter, and the court keeps records that the Council would give much to read.

title: Frosthold
subtitle: A place of the Icy Expanse
summary: Frosthold is the capital of the whaling coast and the strongest seat of the Brine Brotherhood, the fishers and whalers who keep the Expanse alive.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Frosthold is the capital of the whaling coast and the strongest seat of the Brine Brotherhood, the fishers and whalers who keep the Expanse alive. The fortress-walls are built of ice-stone and whale-bone, and the oil-houses along the bay burn the whale-fat that every lamp in the Heartland burns. The Brennvar house holds the oil-houses, and its Lamp-Mistress, Astri, rules the bay with a fairness that the Brotherhood respects and the Combine resents. The Tidecallers of the Concord keep a small temple on the harbor wall, and their sea-blessing is the first thing every whaling fleet receives before it goes out. Frosthold is the last place in the Expanse where a stranger can buy a warm room for a silver Tide.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Goldwind's lamps burn cleaner since Frosthold changed its oil. The lamplighters say the smoke smells faintly of coins.” (a Goldwind lamplighter)

title: Golgarma
subtitle: A place of the Southern Wilds
summary: Golgarma is a city of Orka ruins, vast monuments of stone that loom over the jungle like the bones of a dead god.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Golgarma is a city of Orka ruins, vast monuments of stone that loom over the jungle like the bones of a dead god. The Crimson Legion holds the ruins, and the Legion's banners fly from the great stair that the Orka cut to reach the deeps. The stair is called Golgarma's Throat, and it leads down into the Orka undercity of Nadhûr, which the Legion has held since 175 EC. The Legion's raids push north of Golgarma each season, and the Emerald Wrath has requested a second squadron to hold the river-ports against them. The Council reviews the request. The ruins are still beautiful, and a visitor who walks the great avenues at dusk can feel the Orka's pride in the stone.

illustration.alt: The Crimson Legion guards Golgarma’s great stone stair to Nadhûr amid colossal Orka ruins.
illustration.caption: The Legion holds the Throat.

title: Greyhaven
subtitle: A place of the Northern Frontier
summary: Greyhaven is a grey, hard port that lives inside the fog.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Greyhaven is a grey, hard port that lives inside the fog. Its harbor is the richest salt-fish harbor in the Frontier, and its bells never stop during the Murk. The Stormweaver house, a Marchlord line of storm-sorcerers, keeps the Greyhaven lights burning through the fog, and the house's mages are paid by the Brine Brotherhood's fishing fleets to keep the fishing boats off the rocks. The Widow's Teeth lie just off the harbor mouth, and every Greyhaven child learns the bell-codes before they learn their letters, because a boat that cannot read the bells cannot find the harbor. The old quarter has a chapel on the cliff where the widows of the lost light lamps for the boats that have not come home.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Johann Faust has been seen in a Greyhaven tavern with a man who wears the Last Psalm's badge. Nobody knows which side he means to take.” (heard in the Northern Frontier)

title: Hollowkey
subtitle: A place of the Southern Wilds
summary: Hollowkey is a hidden lagoon in the uncharted south, the greatest of the Pirate Freeholds: a drift-market of lashed-together hulks where the Remnants of Blackheart, the Free Tide crews, and every outlaw captain in the south…

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Hollowkey is a hidden lagoon in the uncharted south, the greatest of the Pirate Freeholds: a drift-market of lashed-together hulks where the Remnants of Blackheart, the Free Tide crews, and every outlaw captain in the south trade, refit, and drink. Its rules are the Free Tide's rules. No Council flag flies there, no Council coin is accepted, and every deal is sealed by the sea. The Hollowkey harbor-master is a retired Armada Blade-Ensign who lost an arm to the Drowning Star, and who will tell anyone who buys him a tot exactly how the Star was fired.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Reinhardt Holst buys a drink for every old pirate in Hollowkey and asks each of them the same question: whose colors sank the Sea Seraph?” (a Hollowkey barkeep)

illustration.alt: A hidden southern pirate lagoon is filled with lashed-together hulls, wooden walkways, boats and market stalls.
illustration.caption: Trade and repairs carry on in Hollowkey’s floating market.

title: Kaldmark
subtitle: A place of the Icy Expanse
summary: Kaldmark is the hold of House Kaldmark, the one true noble house of the Expanse.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Kaldmark is the hold of House Kaldmark, the one true noble house of the Expanse. It is a fortified stronghold in the hills, with a black stone keep and a gate of whale-bone, and its banners carry the white bear-skull on a black field rimmed in ice-blue. The House holds a march of whaling-towns and ice against a frontier that kills the careless. Its Marchlord, Sten Kaldmark, governs with the hold's grim law, and he has learned exactly what his house's motto means. The Kaldmark icebrand stillhouses supply the house's warriors, and the house's blood-feud with the Varan Lodge is older than any living Kaldmark.

title: Karn Sorroch
subtitle: A place of the Southern Wilds
summary: Karn Sorroch is the domain of Velemnos, the Midnight Patron, a dark and jungled land of infamous Krysta-mines worked by the unfree.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Karn Sorroch is the domain of Velemnos, the Midnight Patron, a dark and jungled land of infamous Krysta-mines worked by the unfree. The town of Karn Sorroch is a fortified mining-camp on a river-bend, its gates kept by the thralls of the House of Vossreth, and its streets are lit by low-grade Krysta lamps whose stored workings glow blue within the stones. The Krysta comes out of the deep mines in carts under the Vossreth seal, and the mines are the richest source of dark glass in the south. No visitor is allowed to see the Patron, and most visitors who try do not come back out.

title: The Kraken's Maw
subtitle: A place of the open sea
summary: A passage between two reefs, where the great battle of 165 EC was fought.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: A passage between two reefs, where the great battle of 165 EC was fought. The wrecks of the Armada and the Blackheart fleets lie on the reef's bottom, and divers say the wrecks still hum at dusk.

facts: The Sea and the Coral Kingdoms

illustration.alt: Two adult salvagers row among weed-covered wooden wrecks in the Kraken's Maw in 175 EC, ten years after the battle, with the reefs fading into evening fog.
illustration.caption: Ten years on, the sea keeps its tally.

title: Northreach
subtitle: A place of the Northern Frontier
summary: Northreach is the horse country of the Frontier, a country of gorse, heather, stud-farms, and long grey roads.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Northreach is the horse country of the Frontier, a country of gorse, heather, stud-farms, and long grey roads. The Faust remounts breed here, and the Northreach studs produce the finest horses in the islands, which fetch twice their weight in Anchors in Goldwind. The Tarvan clans graze their own herds on the high moors, and the Tarvan Gathering is held here in the year when all the scattered clans come down together. The Gathering is a market, a moot, a festival, and a proving at once. The trapper towns of Northreach supply the furs that line every Frontier hood, and the logging camps supply the timber the Expanse cannot grow.

title: Saltreach
subtitle: A place of the Northern Frontier
summary: Saltreach is a flat coast of pans, sluices, and salt-sheds, held by the Hallorn trading house, whose Lord-Mistress holds the Frontier's salt monopoly.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Saltreach is a flat coast of pans, sluices, and salt-sheds, held by the Hallorn trading house, whose Lord-Mistress holds the Frontier's salt monopoly. The salt-workers are the most organized labor in the north, and they have struck four times in living memory. The pans are the source of the salt that the Charterhouse Company buys to hold its southern monopoly, and the trade between the Hallorn sheds and the Company's agents in Southhaven is one of the most profitable and least discussed secrets of the Frontier.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A hush owl went quiet at a wedding in Saltreach last Storm Water, and the groom has not been seen since.” (a Frontier tavern)

title: Silverport
subtitle: A place of the Central Heartland
summary: Silverport is the eastern silk-port, a city of pale stone and fragrant gardens.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Silverport is the eastern silk-port, a city of pale stone and fragrant gardens. Its silk-farms and incense-houses supply the Heartland's silk, perfume, and fine oils. The Perfumers of Silverport are at open war with the Pocchin families, who refuse to join the guild, undersell everyone, and steal recipes for sport. The Saffrane house holds the silk trade. The city's markets sell the finest perfumes in the islands, and the rarest of them contain ambergris from Frosthold.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Tobbin pride say Saffrane's famous Black Rose was theirs first, and that they still have the bill of sale.” (a Pocchin, loudly)

title: Snowvah
subtitle: A place of the Icy Expanse
summary: Snowvah is the northernmost settled town of the Expanse, a cluster of stone houses on a black-rock promontory above the ice.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Snowvah is the northernmost settled town of the Expanse, a cluster of stone houses on a black-rock promontory above the ice. It is the last place where a stranger can buy a warm meal before the silent country begins. The Snowvah folk are hard, quiet, and proud. They keep a watch on the sky beyond the last posts, and they do not talk about what they see there.

title: Southhaven
subtitle: A place of the Southern Wilds
summary: Southhaven is the colonial port of the southern coast and the commercial heart of the Wilds.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Southhaven is the colonial port of the southern coast and the commercial heart of the Wilds. Its harbor is lined with the warehouses of the great plantation houses, and its hills grow the coffee, southleaf, cane-sugar, and cotton that every Heartland salon consumes. The Charterhouse Company keeps its southern offices here, and its writ-men, the brass-collars, patrol the warehouse streets. The plantations are divided between the fair estates of House Greymoor and the unfree estates of House Vossreth, and the southern boycott is simple: "Greymoor coffee or none." The Blackleaf Runners smuggle southleaf in and indentured workers out through the river-ports. The Southhaven markets are the best place in the south to learn anything about anyone, and the worst place to be seen learning it.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A Scarlet Mother's priest was seen in Southhaven buying the Fennick factors' coffee in bulk. Nobody says what he wants with so much of it.” (heard in the Southern Wilds)
“Damyel's ship made Mumit from Southhaven in five days, against the wind. The fastest Justicar in the Emerald Wrath needs two weeks.” (heard in the Southern Wilds)
“Every tide anemone in Southhaven closed at noon on the same day last year, out of turn, for exactly as long as it takes to say a prayer.” (a Southhaven harbor-widow)

title: Stormreach
subtitle: A place of the Northern Frontier
summary: Stormreach is the seat of House Vanris and the largest shipbuilding yard in the north.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Stormreach is the seat of House Vanris and the largest shipbuilding yard in the north. The Stormguard Hold is a fortress on a rock above the strait, and the house's yards build the best storm-hulls in the islands and charge a premium for them. The Ninth Fleet, the Standing Storm, keeps its base here, and the Galven crews of the great Juggernaut storm-runners sleep in the lower wards. The town is named for the weather and lives by it. Its spring water fizzes naturally from the rock, and the Galven call it stormwater, shaking it into their kellum and swearing that lightning tastes the same. Mortimer Vanris holds the seat, and his brother Rodrick and the spymaster Cassandra Dosslas hold the house together around him.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Stormwater from the Stormreach spring tastes of the sea where it used to taste of rock.” (heard in the Northern Frontier)
“Fishers off Stormreach netted a brass hatch the size of a door, with a wheel on it.” (a Stormreach fishwife)

title: Sunhold
subtitle: A place of the Central Heartland
summary: Sunhold is the brightest city in the Heartland, a town of terraces and white walls above the western coast.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Sunhold is the brightest city in the Heartland, a town of terraces and white walls above the western coast. Its hills grow the brightleaf that the Terrace Guild presses into leaf-bricks, and its vines produce the Sunhold wines that the Goldwind banks judge by taste. The Sunhold Accord, signed on Veriden 6th, is a treaty of the Concord and the Council that the town hosts every year. The Terrace Guild feuds with the coffee-houses of Goldwind as a matter of identity, and the feud is the subject of a hundred songs.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Dio Emberheart has been seen walking in the Sunhold gardens. The people who saw him say he was not quite the same man who walked there last year.” (heard in the Central Heartland)
“The Sunhold terraces grow a brightleaf that the Registry buys every leaf of, and nobody has ever been allowed to taste it.” (a Terrace Guild picker)

title: Xathnatraz
subtitle: A place of the open sea
summary: A cursed black isle off the southwest coast of Khard Muur, where the dark of the old Eon was sealed. Ships that go looking come back with fewer people, or not at all.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Xathnatraz is a black isle off the southwest coast of Khard Muur, the wild continent beyond the western ocean.
Every child learns that long ago a sunless Eon of Darkness swallowed the world, and that its dark was sealed inside Xathnatraz.
Its lost kingdom of Alcyor fell long ago. Only the last bastion, Valengrad, still holds, under King Rune Vermillion.
No ship has landed there in living memory without the crew falling to a fever that burns in the blood.
"Don't sail west," the sailors say. Ships that go looking for it come back with fewer people, or not at all.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Don't sail west. Out past the edge of the charts lies cursed Xathnatraz, the isle where the dark of the old Eon was sealed. Ships that go looking for it come back with fewer people, or not at all.” (common talk)
“Sailors back from Khard Muur say Valengrad crowned King Rune last year. They crowned him the year before too, and he was buried in between.” (a sailor back from the west)

facts: off the southwest coast of Khard Muur

title: Zal'Kareth
subtitle: A place of the Southern Wilds
summary: Zal'Kareth is the last Council town on the southwestern edge of the Wilds, a fortified river-port beyond which the Council's maps go blank.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Zal'Kareth is the last Council town on the southwestern edge of the Wilds, a fortified river-port beyond which the Council's maps go blank. It is the home of the Ninth Shovel, the grave-robbers and ruin-looters who feed the Quiet Auction with Orka relics and native sacred things. The Ninth Shovel is at war with the Reclaimers, the Sacred Flame, and anyone else who stands in the way of the next treasure. The town's walls are high, and its guard is paid well to look away from what comes up the river at night.

title: The Cistern Door
subtitle: A wonder of the Central Heartland
summary: A dwarven wall under Goldwind's oldest cistern, whose mortar was worked from the far side.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: A dwarven wall under Goldwind's oldest cistern, whose mortar was worked from the far side. Any visitor who lays a hand on the wall feels a faint warmth, and the dwarves of the Goldwind holds say the warmth is the debt being paid, one load at a time.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Cistern Door. At the bottom of Goldwind's oldest cistern is a dwarven wall, and someone has been working its mortar from the other side.” (common talk)

title: The Giant's Table
subtitle: A wonder of the Northern Frontier
summary: A flat stone platform on the high Tarvan moor, set on the shoulder of the Sleeping Giant, the land-spirit that lies beneath the Northreach heath.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: A flat stone platform on the high Tarvan moor, set on the shoulder of the Sleeping Giant, the land-spirit that lies beneath the Northreach heath. The Tarvan walk their herds around the Table on the first morning of spring, and the herd-father Ulmach is said to tread the stones before them. A Tarvan who sits on the Table at dusk hears the Giant breathe.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A Tarvan on the Giant's Table heard the Sleeping Giant turn over in its sleep. She went home and sold every horse she had.” (heard in the Northern Frontier)

title: The Knot
subtitle: A wonder of the Central Heartland
summary: A market below Duskmire, reached through the reed-beds and kept by goblins.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: A market below Duskmire, reached through the reed-beds and kept by goblins. It is the only trading place in the Below that the surface folk use by choice. Its rules are short: no names, no blades, and no light brighter than a candle.

illustration.alt: A goblin merchant bargains with visitors by candlelight in The Knot under Duskmire.
illustration.caption: No names, no blades, no light brighter than a candle.

title: The Maw-Pit
subtitle: A wonder of the Southern Wilds
summary: An arena cut into the rock of Jakupur's southern hill, where saurians fight one another and the condemned.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: An arena cut into the rock of Jakupur's southern hill, where saurians fight one another and the condemned. It is not a wonder of nature, but it is a wonder of the south, and visitors who have seen the Maw-Pit's sand after a fight never tell the same story twice.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Maw-Pit is holding a fight this month that does not have a condemned man in it. It has a child.” (heard in the Southern Wilds)

illustration.alt: Handlers lead a giant feathered saurian into the rock-cut arena of Jakupur before a waiting crowd.
illustration.caption: The Maw-Pit fills before the contest begins.

title: The Rime Ways
subtitle: A wonder of the Icy Expanse
summary: A network of channels under the winter sea-ice, opened by the dwarves of the Expanse's deep holds and used by the smugglers when the ice is too thick for ships.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: A network of channels under the winter sea-ice, opened by the dwarves of the Expanse's deep holds and used by the smugglers when the ice is too thick for ships. The Rime Ways connect the Expanse to the Below, and the dwarves say a tally-mark is cut at every turning, and that the marks go down further than any man has dived.

illustration.alt: A dwarven guide points to tally marks inside the ice channels of the Rime Ways beside a skiff.
illustration.caption: At every turning, another tally in the ice.

title: The Serpent's Coil
subtitle: A wonder of the Northern Frontier
summary: A ring of reefs in the Stormreach strait, shaped like a serpent coiled about a tower.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: A ring of reefs in the Stormreach strait, shaped like a serpent coiled about a tower. The Vanris house took its founding from the sea serpent that led Valdar Vanris to the fortress-site, and the Coil is the serpent's body in stone. Captains who run the Coil in a storm say the reef moves at the King Tide, and the house has never been able to prove otherwise, or to prove it wrong.

title: The Sun's Grave
subtitle: A wonder of the open sea
summary: A patch of open sea south of the Goldwind gulf that the oldest charts name and no chart explains.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: A patch of open sea south of the Goldwind gulf that the oldest charts name and no chart explains. Fishermen say the water there is warm in winter and that nets come up with gold leaf caught in them. Nobody fishes it twice.

facts: The Sea and the Coral Kingdoms

title: The Veil of Shadows
subtitle: The curtain rises again.
summary: A shadow-theater in Goldwind's old quarter, halfway up the city's rings, where a single play has run every night for about a hundred and forty years without a dark night.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: A shadow-theater in Goldwind's old quarter, halfway up the city's rings, where a single play has run every night for about a hundred and forty years without a dark night. The actors perform behind a great veil of white silk. Goldwind's nobility never miss a season.

illustration.alt: An audience watches performers cast silhouettes behind a great white silk veil in a Goldwind theater.
illustration.caption: The same play fills the Veil of Shadows each night.

title: Abyssara, the Black Below
subtitle: Beneath the waves
summary: Abyssara is the trench beneath the trenches, where the dark has never been broken.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Abyssara is the trench beneath the trenches, where the dark has never been broken. It is the lair of Thalgorath, and of something vast and ancient that the sea-peoples call by a name they do not say near the water. Even the deep courts will not go there. Abyssara is the place they fear.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Abyssara: what falls into the southwestern trench does not come back; what comes back is changed.” (common talk)

facts: The Sea and the Coral Kingdoms

title: The Glass Gardens
subtitle: Beneath the waves
summary: The Glass Gardens are the fair merfolk's realm in the Sunlit shallows, a city of living reef-architecture where the coral grows in shapes the sea-folk choose.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Glass Gardens are the fair merfolk's realm in the Sunlit shallows, a city of living reef-architecture where the coral grows in shapes the sea-folk choose. Its towers are clear, and its streets are lit by bioluminescent fish. The Glass Gardens are the sea's most welcoming court, and the sea-folk trade memory-pearls there to surface visitors who come to them with a kind word and a clean hand.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Pelagar has been buying the Starfall coral in bulk. The Glass Gardens have stopped trading with Pelagar in return.” (heard in the Sea and the Coral Kingdoms)

facts: The Sea and the Coral Kingdoms

illustration.alt: Two merfolk with fin-frills extend both hands toward a memory pearl amid the coral arches of the fully submerged Glass Gardens.
illustration.caption: A memory pearl changes hands in the Sunlit shallows.

title: The Grey Fathoms
subtitle: Beneath the waves
summary: The Grey Fathoms are the realm of the kept drowned, a deep court whose sea-folk gather the dead of the surface and keep them in silver-lit caves.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Grey Fathoms are the realm of the kept drowned, a deep court whose sea-folk gather the dead of the surface and keep them in silver-lit caves. Their ransom is fair: a family that comes to the Grey Fathoms with a pearl and a song may take a drowned relative home for a day. The Fathoms refuse the dead of the Wrong Coast, and their keepers have never said why.

facts: The Sea and the Coral Kingdoms

title: The Old Shells
subtitle: Beneath the waves
summary: The Old Shells are the realm of the leviathan sage-turtles, great ancient creatures whose shells are the size of islands.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Old Shells are the realm of the leviathan sage-turtles, great ancient creatures whose shells are the size of islands. They answer three questions a generation, to any who come to them with a gift of sound and a true question. The Old Shells surface at the Stillwater, and their answers have shaped the Armada's naval doctrine twice in living memory.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Old Shells answered a question last month that no one had asked. The answer was the name of a ship, and the ship has not been seen since.” (heard in the Sea and the Coral Kingdoms)
“The Old Shells have surfaced at the Stillwater three times this year. They used to come up once in a generation.” (a Last Psalm Tidecaller)

facts: The Sea and the Coral Kingdoms

illustration.alt: A sage-turtle as large as an island surfaces beside a tiny sailing boat at Stillwater.
illustration.caption: A gift of sound and a true question approach an Old Shell.

title: Pearl Groove and the Pelagar Isle
subtitle: Beneath the waves
summary: Pearl Groove is the surface's pearl-port, a shallow lagoon of pearl-clans on the Heartland's coast, under the watch of the Belmaris house and its bell-mistress Orlaine.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Pearl Groove is the surface's pearl-port, a shallow lagoon of pearl-clans on the Heartland's coast, under the watch of the Belmaris house and its bell-mistress Orlaine. The Pelagar isle lies on the Coral edge, a small island of pearl-houses and sea-gardens, where the Pelagar house keeps its pacts and its secrets. Both ports are the surface's gateway to the courts, and both are watched by every faction in the Heartland.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Someone is buying every reefpurple dye that comes through Pearl Groove. The Council cannot find the buyer, and the Pelagar house will not say.” (heard in the Central Heartland)
“Pelagar has been buying the Starfall coral in bulk. The Glass Gardens have stopped trading with Pelagar in return.” (heard in the Sea and the Coral Kingdoms)
“A memory-pearl sold in Pearl Groove shows a woman's face on the Sunken Thrones. She is looking up, and she is smiling.” (heard in the Sea and the Coral Kingdoms)

facts: The Sea and the Coral Kingdoms

title: The Red Choir
subtitle: Beneath the waves
summary: The Red Choir is the sahuagin blood-faith, a deep and savage court whose hymns rise when blood is in the water.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Red Choir is the sahuagin blood-faith, a deep and savage court whose hymns rise when blood is in the water. Its choirmaster is Thalgorath, the Tide-Tyrant, and its priests sing him up from the depths on the King Tide. The Red Choir does not trade with the surface, and the Pelagar house has never been able to make it an offer it would accept.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Red Choir has started singing on a quiet night, when there is no blood in the water. The Tidecallers say the song is coming up the Starfall Reef.” (heard in the Sea and the Coral Kingdoms)

facts: The Sea and the Coral Kingdoms

title: The Sunken Thrones
subtitle: Beneath the waves
summary: The Sunken Thrones are the deep courts, a midnight abyss of ancient sovereigns whose politics do not map onto anything a land-mind can hold.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Sunken Thrones are the deep courts, a midnight abyss of ancient sovereigns whose politics do not map onto anything a land-mind can hold. What little is known of them comes thirdhand through the Pelagar house, and the Pelagar house does not share it, because some of it cannot be told without changing the teller.

sections.title: Rumors

title: The Whispering Current
subtitle: Beneath the waves
summary: The Whispering Current is the twilight secret-traders' realm, a court of currents that carry every word spoken over water.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Whispering Current is the twilight secret-traders' realm, a court of currents that carry every word spoken over water. Its keepers buy and sell the secrets of the surface's harbors, and the Skein, the great Heartland information-broker, has a standing contract with them. Speak carelessly over water in a Current port and the Current will remember, and the words will be sold at the next full moon.

title: The Charterhouse Company
subtitle: A power of the islands
summary: A Council-chartered trading company that bypasses the guilds: monopolies, company towns, and enforcers called brass-collars.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Outside the guilds stands the Charterhouse Company, a Council-chartered trading company with monopolies, company towns, and enforcers the docks call brass-collars.
Governor: Imelda Roque, "the Lady of Writs."
Holdings: the southern salt monopoly (won in 175 EC; two ports rioted), the Verdayan jade concession, and indenture contracts in the south.
Its southern offices are in Southhaven.
Everyone knows it wants the thirteenth flag-socket on the Spire Floor very badly.

title: The Reckoners' Hall
subtitle: A power of the islands
summary: The Congress's bank, under First Reckoner Maera Blackstrand, who holds half the islands' debts.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Everyone knows the real power of the Mercantile Congress is its bank, the Reckoners' Hall, the marble hall in Goldwind under First Reckoner Maera Blackstrand, who holds half the islands' debts.
Credit: the Reckoners lend at 1 in 20 to the Five great houses, and as high as 1 in 5 to a tradesman.
Bottomry (a loan on a ship and its cargo) runs from 1 in 50 on the coast to 1 in 5 on the ice, and three times that in a King Tide year.
A reckoning, a letter of credit, costs 2 in 100.
The Still Days freeze every debt.
Three Coinsdays unpaid put a name in the Ledger.
Under salvage law, the Reckoners register claims on named wrecks, and they pay the Council's bounties on proof.

title: The Twelve Flags
subtitle: A power of the islands
summary: The great merchant families who hold the twelve flag-posts of the Spire Floor in Goldwind and call the Coinsday board-price.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Twelve Flags are the great merchant families. Each holds one of the twelve flag-posts on the Spire Floor, the trading hall of the Goldspire Exchange in Goldwind, where every Coinsday they call the board-price of coffee, salt, oil, grain, and the rest. A post takes a bond of 1,000 Orsals and twenty years on the floor, and it passes only by family.
Goldspire, who own the Exchange: Merchant Lord Horace, heir Celestine.
The Corvane Line, the great shipping house that carries the Council's post: Matthias, "the Old Crow."
Saffrane of Silverport, silk and perfume: Madame Ilsabet.
Vantrey, the licensed Krysta brokers: Lord-Broker Edmar.
Belmaris of Pearl Groove, bells and the sea-folk's sound-trade: Bell-Mistress Orlaine.
Ostrel of Ironfort, farmers of the Gate-Tithe: Tithe-Mistress Maren.
Hallorn of Saltreach, salt and herring: Aldric.
Fennick of Southhaven, coffee and sugar factors: Ondine, a half-elf.
The Oruma, a native river-clan of the Nine Mouths: Grandmother Veyani. They took House Darrowen's post when it fell in 171 EC.
Sukuun of Jakupur, saurians: Teoma, brother of the great tamer Tana.
Brennvar of Frosthold, whale-oil: Lamp-Mistress Astri.
The Tobbin pride, a Pocchin family, to everyone's continuing astonishment: Mother Tatta and Pobbo.
Bannermen are the sworn houses, flag-captains, and bought bannerets of each flag, bound by the Flag-Oath. A broken oath gets the flag struck.
The center socket. The Spire Floor has a thirteenth flag-socket at its center that has never held a flag.

title: The Great Hunter Crews
subtitle: The Order of Hunters
summary: The crews every islander can name, from the Crimson Tide to the Karnivool, and the rival crews of the Board.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Famous crews:
Crimson Tide: Captain Bramgard, who breached and sank the Gaze of Abyss at the Kraken's Maw, and his First Mate Albion Tempest.
Rolling Thunder: co-captains Uther and Gunther Banestorm.
Jubilant: Captain Johann Faust of House Faust.
The Last Word: Captain Khaz'Aimar Maa'iq.
Zephyr: Sandros Magnus.
Karnivool: a Hunters' ship and a traveling show at once, under captain and ringmaster Avalan Grant.
Retribution's Wrath: Reinhardt Holst, disinherited by House Holst; the youngest Gold, seventeenth in the Ranking.
Iron Swan: Titania, who struck through the pirate line again and again at the Maw.
The rival crews everyone has heard of:
The Gilded Wake: Capt. Odessa Braith's house-sponsored darlings, who arrive second and claim credit first.
The Saltborn Nine: Warden Rhona Cravoch's exactly nine cold professionals, all Tarvan steel.
The Second Sons: Capt. Lucan Alastor's disgraced nobles, reckless, lovable, and broke.
The Flensers: "Old Knife" Petra Sallow's badge-stripped poachers no decent Lodge will name.

title: The Iron
subtitle: The Order of Hunters
summary: Not a rank: the iron coin a candidate needs to sit the Trials of Ascension. Only 300 are struck each year.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: There is no Iron rank. To sit the yearly Trials of Ascension you need a Hunter's endorsement, which is usually an iron: an iron coin struck with the Hunters' shield.
Only 300 irons are struck each year.
Whoever presents an iron sits the Trials. Lose yours, and someone else uses it, and that is your problem.
A candidate carrying one is called an iron, and "still carrying iron" means a rookie who has not yet sat the Trials.
Hunters buy irons at the Crucible in Ironfort, up to two a year at 10 Orsals each, or earn them on important contracts. Some contracts pay in an iron, and a Hunter may ask for one as part of the fee.
Most candidates work under the Hunter who gave them their iron. It is only a duty if the iron was given on that condition; an iron given without strings binds nothing.
Every year's irons are struck to a new die, so last year's is worthless. You can sit the Trials as many times as you like, if you survive them, but each attempt needs a new iron.

The iron market is seasonal. The Crucible mints the year's irons one to two months after the Trials, so the market shuts for that window and reopens for the rest of the year, peaking as the next Trials approach. In the Undertow an iron fetches 150 to 300 Anchors in that last season.

facts: 10 Orsals, two a year at most

title: The Sigil
subtitle: The Order of Hunters
summary: A Hunter's rank badge, forged at the Goldwind Lodge. It is bearer-bound: anyone else who holds it suffers, worse the higher the rank.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Every Hunter's Sigil is made in one place: the Sigil-Forge of the Goldwind Lodge, by the Sigilwrights under the Master Sigilwright, one of the most prestigious titles in the guild.
The curse is forged in. A Sigil carried by anyone but its rightful bearer works on them, and the longer it is held, the worse it gets. None of it kills.
Bronze: a mild headache, and a numbness in the hand that spreads with time.
Silver: nausea and vomiting, fainting spells, and a slow drain of strength.
Gold: like a deadly poison taking hold: fever, weakness, and pain that build by the hour.
Rank protects. A Silver Hunter is immune to a Bronze Sigil, and a Gold Hunter to Silver and Bronze.
Branches. Every Hunter belongs to a branch, and the branch is worked into the Sigil:
Mage: arcane motifs, crystals, and glyphs.
Scout: feathers, arrows, and predators.
Diplomat: scrolls, olive branches, and symbols of union.
Warrior: shields, weapons, and bold lines.
Design by rank:
Bronze: a simple single piece of bronze, with the iron of the Hunter who vouched for it set into the back.
Silver: engraved, often inlaid with gems or fine detail.
Gold: ornate and made of several materials, showing the bearer's deeds. A Gold Sigil may carry two branches.
Platinum: enchanted platinum of a craft no one else can match.
Awakened Sigils. Rarely, a Sigil awakens: it becomes a sentient thing with a personality of its own and bonds with its bearer like a partner.

title: The Trials of Ascension
subtitle: The Order of Hunters
summary: The Hunters' yearly exam, held in the month of Ezra. Its last leg is the Vow, where the candidate's iron is set into a new Bronze Sigil.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Trials of Ascension are the Hunters' exam, held once a year, in Ezra, the month of Mast and Sail.
You need an iron to sit them.
Those who pass swear the Oath and are made Bronze.
A candidate who fails is encouraged to sit them again; a few are offered support roles instead: clerks, quartermasters, Lodge staff, and the hands that keep the Hunters' ships at sea.
Shedding iron. The last leg of the Trials is the Vow, where the candidate swears the Oath before the hall. The iron they carried is set into the back of their new Bronze Sigil while the hall watches.
Turn any Hunter's Sigil over and that year's die shows.
Every Bronze Sigil therefore carries the iron of the Hunter who vouched for it.
The iron is spent in the Sigil, so it cannot be sold, pawned, or presented again.

title: The Coats and Ranks of the Armada
subtitle: Earn a color. Learn the chain.
summary: A coat identifies a branch, a rank a place in command, and a shipboard post a job that must be done. Together they make the Armada legible.

sections.title: Earning your coat
paragraphs: Every recruit begins as a Grey Coat. Earning a color is the first rite, after which the sailor is sorted into a branch. The colors cut across the rank ladder; knowing that someone is a White Coat does not by itself tell you which ship or squadron they command.

Blue Coats belong to the Cerulean Vanguard, the fighting line led by Brigid Thane. They pass the Cerulean Trials and keep the creed “In Valor, We Stand.” White Coats belong to Serane Marr’s Ivory Command, the largely noble strategic and diplomatic branch, entered through the Ivory Investiture: “Wisdom Guides, Power Follows.”

Black Coats are the Ebon Blade, entered through its own rite and bound to no fleet. Their work includes espionage and infiltration; their creed is “Might Makes Right.” A Black Coat normally ranks below a White Coat, but a sanctioned mission permits an override of contrary orders.

rows: Supreme command of the nine fleets
A fleet; Battle-Admiral when commanding a joint line
Squadron assignment: standard / independent offensive / convoy, rear guard and logistics
A sea flotilla / fortress or station / port defenses and harbor watch
Flagships and capital ships; squadron second
A warship’s captain, addressed by their hull
Crew; known together as the Blooded after first action
table.caption: From the Admiralty to the deck

sections.title: The work inside the rank
paragraphs: An Oathwarden keeps the crew to the Charter and its oath; a Sword-Warden is master-at-arms and senior marine. The Ship’s Tidecaller is the Concord chaplain who blesses the sailing. The Master of Thunder is chief gunner; the Chartmaster is a Chartwright-certified navigator.

The Rook is the chief lookout, living high in the top: the name carries both tower and crow. These posts tell a visitor whom to seek for a particular kind of knowledge or responsibility aboard. A ship needs all of them long before an admiral gives the order to fight.

facts: Cerulean Vanguard, Ivory Command, Ebon Blade

title: The Nine Fleets
subtitle: Nine names sailors know by heart
summary: A Fleetlord, a ship and a duty for each part of the sea: the Armada’s nine fleets form a map of what the islands ask their navy to protect.

sections.title: Reading the fleet roll
paragraphs: Each fleet has a number, a name, a Fleetlord and a ship from which that commander flies a flag. Its station or charge explains the rest. Some watch a particular approach; others follow a kind of work wherever it leads.

The First and Second are the Twin Irons. Kalivos Durant’s Iron Wall shields Goldwind and the Heartland, while Dastan Graylock’s Iron Blockade holds the northern strait against the Imperium. One protects the center; the other guards its northern approach.

rows: Goldwind and the Heartland; the capital's shield
The northern strait, against the Imperium
The Concord's fleet; sea-pacts and the Coral Kingdoms
Expeditionary; offense wherever the Council points
Rescue, crisis, and what rises from the deep
Exploration and charting with the Chartwrights
Southern rivers and coasts; gunboats in the green
The Icy Expanse; stretched thin, unbroken
table.caption: The Armada in 175 EC

sections.title: Duties that cross the map
paragraphs: The Last Psalm carries Tidecallers on every hull and deals with the sea-pacts and Coral Kingdoms. The Spearfall takes the offensive wherever the Council directs it. The Killing Tide responds to crisis, rescue, evacuation and dangers rising from the deep. The Far Watch explores and charts with the Chartwrights.

The last three commands give the regional chart its harder edges: gunboats in the Southern Wilds, a thin watch across the Icy Expanse, and heavy-weather operations out of Stormreach. “The Vow does not thaw” is the Eighth’s promise to itself.

sections.title: The ship beneath the flag
paragraphs: A flagship is the ship carrying a commander’s flag. Nine Executioners were built, but the fleet roll is not a list of nine such hulls. Brightsight keeps the Falkoner, the ship he captained at the Kraken’s Maw; Smiling Uha commands from the Seeker and flies no Executioner.
A Fleetlord takes the style Battle-Admiral when commanding a joint line. The title describes that combined command without erasing the fleets’ separate identities.

title: Ship Classes of the Armada
subtitle: Read the hull before the flag
summary: Courier, pursuer, river gunboat or fortress-breaker: an Armada ship’s class tells an islander what work has arrived offshore.

sections.title: Duties with teeth
paragraphs: The Armada names its classes for the work they carry into the world. A Harbinger is a courier cutter, and sailors say its arrival means news, rarely good. A Vindicator sloop gives chase. A Justicar gunboat can work a river where the great battle hulls have no business going.

Warden frigates are the backbone of the fleets. Juggernaut heavy frigates are storm-runners, crewed by Galven; Interdictor cruisers make the Iron Blockade’s fist. A ship’s importance follows the waters and duty it is built to serve.

sections.title: The great battle hulls
paragraphs: The Dreadnought is the ship of the line, said to fear nothing. The Enforcer is a bombard built to deliver the Council’s verdict to fortresses. Above them stand the Executioners: nine men-of-war ever built, including Conqueror, Charter’s Oath, Stormcrown and Deepward.

A Fleetlord’s flagship need not be an Executioner. Falken Brightsight keeps the Falkoner that carried him through the Kraken’s Maw, and the Far Watch flies none. A familiar hull and a commander’s history can remain bound together across a promotion.

sections.title: The cost of crystal
paragraphs: Krysta armament is rare and ruinously expensive. The pirate cannon called the Drowning Star has given the Admiralty a weapon to reckon with, but it has not made crystal guns ordinary equipment. Most of the fleet roll is still best understood through a ship’s intended duty.

Sigil: a coiled sea-serpent about a tower, on storm-grey and deep green.
Motto: "Unyielding as the Storm."
Head: Lord Mortimer Vanris.
The family, as the salons name them:
Sir Rodrick Vanris
Lady Cassandra Dosslas
Mortis
Gideon
Lord Mortimer himself

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Mortimer Vanris will sell the Stormguard to the Heartland before the year is out. His brother has already written to the Council about it.” (heard in the Northern Frontier)

facts: a coiled sea-serpent about a tower, on storm-grey and deep green
aliases: a coiled sea-serpent about a tower, on storm-grey and deep green

title: House Varselis
subtitle: The Even Hand
summary: The Even Hand: an Archlord house whose motto is “Weighed, Not Wagered.”

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: House Varselis, the Even Hand.
Rank: Archlord.
Seat: the Hall of Scales, Central Heartland.
Sigil: a set of silver scales over an open book, on grey-blue.
Motto: "Weighed, Not Wagered."
Head: Lord Linus Varhall Varselis.
Heir: Halsof Varselis, who holds the Nobles' seat on the Council of the Charted Isles.
The family, as the salons name them:
Lady Octavia Varselis
Julius Varselis
Calista Varselis
Aelius Varselis

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Halsof Varselis has been asked to take the Five's chair, and he has said no three times. The fourth time he may say yes.” (heard in the Central Heartland)

facts: the Hall of Scales, Central Heartland
a set of silver scales over an open book, on grey-blue
Halsof Varselis, who holds the Nobles' seat on the Council of the Charted Isles

title: House Veldane
subtitle: The Marriage-Web
summary: The Marriage-Web: a Highlord house of the Central Heartland whose motto is “Kin to All, Kept by None.”

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: House Veldane, the Marriage-Web.
Rank: Highlord.
Region: Central Heartland.

facts: two clasped hands ringed in laurel, on cream and rose-gold

title: House Vol Kaern
subtitle: The Crown That Isn't
summary: The Crown That Isn't: an Archlord house of the Central Heartland whose motto is “One Hand, One Helm.”

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: House Vol Kaern, the Crown That Isn't.
Rank: Archlord.
Seat: the castle-heights above Goldwind.
Region: Central Heartland.
Sigil: a black tower crowned with a silver flame, on deep violet.
Motto: "One Hand, One Helm."
Head: Lord Kastan Vol Kaern.
The family, as the salons name them:
Lady Vaela Vol Kaern
Nyssara Vol Kaern
Lord Arkos Vol Kaern
Draven Vol Kaern

“Tana Sukuun has sold a Dreadmaw to the Heartland. The buyer is a Vol Kaern agent, and the saurian is named after the Vol Kaern tower.” (heard in the Southern Wilds)

title: House Vossreth
subtitle: The Hollow Crown of the South
summary: The Hollow Crown of the South: a Marchlord house whose motto is “What Is Mine, I Keep.”

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: House Vossreth, the Hollow Crown of the South.
Rank: Marchlord.
Seat: a Krysta-rich southern mining holding within the domain of Karn Sorroch.
Sigil: a red gem in a black hand, on bruise-purple.
Motto: "What Is Mine, I Keep."
Head: Lord Caldren Vossreth.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Sissix-the-Comet has lost a heat for the first time in two seasons. The jockey who beat her has a Vossreth brand on his wrist and no memory of the race.” (heard in the Southern Wilds)

facts: the Hollow Crown of the South

title: The Noble Houses
subtitle: A noble house
summary: The twenty Major Houses, the Five among them, and the hundreds of lesser houses beneath them.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: There are twenty Major Houses. Five are first among them:
Vol Kaern: the Crown That Isn't, whose castle looms over Goldwind.
Varselis: the Even Hand; holds the Nobles' seat on the Council.
Faust: the Gate of the North, at Bastion.
Vanris: Unyielding as the Storm, at Stormreach.
Alastor: the Rose House.

The Highlords: Caelvaron, the Hundred-Year Throne of the high elves; Emberheart, the Fire Beneath; Silverthorn, the Quiet Knife of Briarcrown; Sunforge, the Golden Hammer; Starborn, the Watchers of Heaven; Holst, Order Before Mercy, keepers of the customs-codes; Blackstrand, the Ledger's Lord; Pelagar, the Deep Trade; Veldane, the Marriage-Web; and Solenne, the Faithful Seat.
The Marchlords: Stormweaver, Kaldmark, Greymoor (the Fair Hand of the South), and Vossreth.
The Warden: Quillane, the Coin-Made Lords, who sell bannerets to anyone with coin.
The bannermen: beneath the Twenty swarm more than two hundred minor houses, each granted land or title by a greater lord.
Knightly orders: the Knights of the Pale Rose (sworn to Alastor), the Sapphire Guard, the Shieldmaidens, and the Knights of Dawn.
Grand Dame Ottilie Veldane arranges half the weddings in the Heartland.

title: Abysm
subtitle: Domination, strength, slavery.
summary: Slavers and despots

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Abysm: domination, strength, slavery.
Slavers and despots

Abysm’s slavers and despots see strength as a claim on the lives of others. In his worship, the chain is the logical end of that belief: those who can impose their will expect obedience to outlast the moment of force.

title: Aoifel, the Green Laugh
subtitle: the Green Laugh.
summary: Archfey of the Faewild. Spring, the First Bloom. Renewal, youth, games; the gentlest, by fae standards.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Aoifel, the Green Laugh is one of the Archfey, the divine-tier rulers of the Faewild.
Court: Spring, the First Bloom.
Holds: Renewal, youth, games; the gentlest, by fae standards.

Aoifel’s gentleness has the measure of the Faewild. The ruler of the First Bloom delights in youth and games, and a mortal at play in the Spring Court may discover how differently the fae understand a fresh start.

epigraph.quote: Laugh at the frost, child. It cannot understand a joke, so it will simply go away.
epigraph.by: A Florian child of the Spring Court's edge, at the Laughing Thaw, to a grandfather who had been afraid of the late frost

title: Asmodul
subtitle: Necromancy, pestilence, decay.
summary: Plague as deliberate cruelty

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Asmodul: necromancy, pestilence, decay.
Plague as deliberate cruelty

Asmodul brings necromancy, pestilence and decay together through intent. His name belongs to the deliberate spread of sickness, when someone takes a harm that could be contained and cultivates it as an instrument of cruelty.

title: Athuraz
subtitle: Destruction, chaos, tyranny.
summary: Raiders and warlords

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Athuraz: destruction, chaos, tyranny.
Raiders and warlords

Raiders and warlords turn to Athuraz when destruction itself is a way to rule. A town can remain under a tyrant’s sway long after the raiders have gone if its neighbors still remember what happened to the last place that resisted.

title: Brakkundr, the War-Forge
subtitle: the War-Forge.
summary: The quenched blade and the marching host

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Brakkundr, the War-Forge: war-smithing, the armed host.
The quenched blade and the marching host

Brakkundr’s province stretches from the quenched blade to the marching host. A smith who finishes a weapon and a soldier who relies on it meet in the same act of preparation, long before either sees the outcome of a battle.

epigraph.quote: Quench the blade in the same water you will drink from tomorrow. Then you will know what it is for.
epigraph.by: An armorer of the Frontier garrison, to a young recruit who had broken his first sword

title: The Breath That Wanders
subtitle: A name the islands know.
summary: The Aspect of Sky. It holds: Wind, storm, breath, freedom, the five layers of the heavens

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Breath That Wanders is the Aspect of Sky, one of the Six Aspects that the native peoples pray to directly.
Primal names: Aëthyr-Vol, the Five Skies, the Open Mouth.
Mundane names: the Wind, the High Blue, the Wanderer.
It holds: Wind, storm, breath, freedom, the five layers of the heavens.

facts: Aëthyr-Vol, the Five Skies, the Open Mouth
the Wind, the High Blue, the Wanderer

title: Brother Dog
subtitle: Travel, animals, companionship.
summary: Loyalty and the joy of the road

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Brother Dog: travel, animals, companionship.
Loyalty and the joy of the road

Brother Dog belongs to the shared road: the animal that walks beside a traveler and the companion who waits when the pace slows. Among halflings he is honored alongside Eo, Castellyn and the folk-saint Penny Greenstep.

epigraph.quote: He does not care where you are going. He only wants to know whether you will be coming back, and he will wait by the gate until you do.
epigraph.by: A herder of the Tarvan moors, to a child who had lost the family's dog on the road

title: Cael the Vintner
subtitle: Revelry, wine, joy, festival.
summary: His festivals are sacred riots; an overflowing cup

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Cael the Vintner: revelry, wine, joy, festival.
His festivals are sacred riots; an overflowing cup

The overflowing cup suits a god whose festivals spill past the bounds of an orderly feast. Wine, joy and revelry belong together in Cael’s worship, and a celebration that grows louder as the evening wears on is true to his character.

epigraph.quote: Drink to the living first, then to the dead, and only then to whoever is left. The cup is always fuller than the grief.
epigraph.by: A Heartland vintner at the Riot of Cups, pouring for the widows of the Long Night

title: Castellyn, the Open Hearth
subtitle: the Open Hearth.
summary: To harm one you have fed is among the gravest sins; symbol an open door, bread on the sill

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Castellyn, the Open Hearth: hospitality, guest-right.
To harm one you have fed is among the gravest sins; symbol an open door, bread on the sill

Castellyn’s open door and bread on the sill mark the moment hospitality becomes a duty. Once a host has fed a guest, even an old grievance must reckon with the protection that the shared meal has placed over that person.

epigraph.quote: Feed the stranger at your table, and nobody in the village will ever harm him. It is the only law anyone has ever needed.
epigraph.by: An innkeeper of the Heartland, to a visiting Navy officer who had asked why she never turned away a beggar

title: Chaos
subtitle: A name the islands know.
summary: destruction and madness. The caged first being, prayed to only by the mad and the desperate.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Chaos is one of the five Greater Gods: destruction and madness. The caged first being, prayed to only by the mad and the desperate.

The image of a cage gives the old account its force: the first being still exists, and the pantheon remembers what had to be contained. A prayer to Chaos comes from the far edge of desperation, where someone is willing to call on the very power the story warns against.

title: Daelhir
subtitle: Sand, time, death, destiny.
summary: Destiny written in falling sand

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Daelhir: sand, time, death, destiny.
Destiny written in falling sand

Falling sand gives Daelhir’s domains a common image. Each grain marks time passing, and the whole descent suggests a destiny whose end can be certain even when those living through it cannot see how much time remains.

title: The Drowning Mother
subtitle: A name the islands know.
summary: The Aspect of Water. It holds: Oceans, rain, rivers, blood, birth, dissolution. The most revered Aspect in Kalvatar

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Drowning Mother is the Aspect of Water, one of the Six Aspects that the native peoples pray to directly.
Primal names: Ysra-Deep, the Unending Grey, She-Who-Was-First.
Mundane names: the Tide, the Old Wet, Grandmother Salt.
It holds: Oceans, rain, rivers, blood, birth, dissolution. The most revered Aspect in Kalvatar.

facts: the Tide, the Old Wet, Grandmother Salt

epigraph.quote: She was here before the first boat, and she will be here after the last one sinks. Bring her salt and she will not take the boat.
epigraph.by: A fisher's widow of Goldwind's Lower Harbor, to a son who wanted to sail in Storm Water

title: Elcifer
subtitle: Illusion, trickery, charm, luck, lies.
summary: Rogues, gamblers, illusionists

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Elcifer: illusion, trickery, charm, luck, lies.
Rogues, gamblers, illusionists

Rogues, gamblers and illusionists all deal in the gap between what someone sees and what they decide to believe. Elcifer governs that moment, when a well-timed charm, a convincing lie or an unexpected turn of luck can change the outcome.

title: Eliol
subtitle: Magic, knowledge, spell, time.
summary: Patron of the University. Month: Eliol of Chart and Star

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Eliol: magic, knowledge, spell, time.
Patron of the University. Month: Eliol of Chart and Star

Eliol’s patronage of the University places spellcraft alongside the work of learning. Chart and Star, the name of his month, gives that relationship a fitting image: knowledge has to be recorded and read before it can guide someone else.

title: Elisse
subtitle: Envy, lust, passion, fire.
summary: The desire that consumes, where Liora's frees

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Elisse: envy, lust, passion, fire.
The desire that consumes, where Liora's frees

Elisse’s fire gives passion the power to consume its bearer. Her place beside Liora in accounts of desire draws attention to what happens when the longing to be loved turns into envy and the need to possess.

title: Elros
subtitle: Tyranny, war, law, tempest.
summary: Warlords and dictators

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Elros: tyranny, war, law, tempest.
Warlords and dictators

Elros’s domains bring law and tempest into the service of war. A dictator who invokes him can speak of order while ruling through the sudden violence of a storm, making the right to command depend on the power to punish.

title: Eo
subtitle: Family, earth, healing, community.
summary: Greater God. Month: Eo of Hearth and Home

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Eo: family, earth, healing, community.
Greater God. Month: Eo of Hearth and Home

Eo’s month, Hearth and Home, puts the work of healing inside the life of a community. Tending the earth, caring for a relative and keeping a household fed all express the same responsibility for the lives that depend on it.

title: Ezra
subtitle: Protection, courage, the Shield.
summary: She guards the weak; the Armada's own goddess. Month: Ezra of Mast and Sail

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Ezra: protection, courage, the shield.
She guards the weak; the Armada's own goddess. Month: Ezra of Mast and Sail

Ezra’s shield expresses the duty to stand between danger and someone who cannot meet it alone. That protective courage is central to the Armada’s devotion and gives particular weight to her place in the calendar, in the month of Mast and Sail.

title: Fortura the Fickle
subtitle: Luck, chance, gambling.
summary: She does not love or hate; she rolls

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Fortura the Fickle: luck, chance, gambling.
She does not love or hate; she rolls
A gambler can hope for Fortura’s favor without having any assurance of keeping it. Her fickleness belongs to chance itself: the next throw can undo a winning streak as easily as it began it.

epigraph.quote: I do not love you. I do not hate you. I roll, and you live with what comes up. Pray to me if you like. I will not listen any harder for it.
epigraph.by: A pit-boss of the Heartland's gambling halls, to a sailor who had bet his ship on a single throw

title: The Gods of the Pantheon
subtitle: A name the islands know.
summary: The pantheon of the imperials and the Council's peoples: five Greater Gods over the Named Gods, by alignment, and the ten gods of the months.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The pantheon of the imperials and the Council's peoples, by alignment. Most islanders are practical polytheists: a fisherman thanks Okram, fears Mhavros, respects Lilim, and pours a cup for Cael at festival, and sees no contradiction. Gods marked with a month are the patrons of the Charter calendar (Part Five).

sections.title: The Greater Gods
paragraphs: Eo: family, earth, healing, community. The year opens in her month.
Law the Sun King: law, sun, fire, purification. The First Namer, as the faithful know him.
Skaia: dreams, fate, sky, stars. She touches the oldest sorrow of all, for every star is a dead god.
Chaos: destruction and madness. The caged first being, prayed to only by the mad and the desperate.
Mhavros: the ocean depths, hatred, suffering, the abyss. Lord of the things in Abyssara.

sections.title: The gods of the months
paragraphs: The Charter calendar names each month for a god and the part of life that god keeps (Volume XV).
| Month | God | Keeps | Season | |

title: The Green Fire
subtitle: A name the islands know.
summary: The Aspect of Life. It holds: Plants, beasts, fertility, hunger, the jungle's reach

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Green Fire is the Aspect of Life, one of the Six Aspects that the native peoples pray to directly.
Primal names: Ilavash, the Spreading, the Thousand Mouths.
Mundane names: the Growth, the Green, Mother Leaf.
It holds: Plants, beasts, fertility, hunger, the jungle's reach.

facts: Ilavash, the Spreading, the Thousand Mouths
the Growth, the Green, Mother Leaf

epigraph.quote: Put your dead in the earth and listen. You will hear the green answering.
epigraph.by: A grove-mother of the Liriath, at a planting, to a human settler who wanted to bury his dead in stone

title: The Green Hunter
subtitle: The free hunt, wild beasts.
summary: The Life-Aspect as a wild god; an antlered skull

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Green Hunter: the free hunt, wild beasts.
