The Life-Aspect as a wild god; an antlered skull

As a wild face of the Life-Aspect, the Green Hunter holds both the hunt and the beasts that make it possible. The antlered skull brings those together in one sign, carrying the shape of the living animal into the image of its death.

epigraph.quote: The chase is joy. It is not cruelty and it is not kindness. Run, and let the sky watch you run.
epigraph.by: A free hunter of the Southern Wilds, at the end of a day's chase, to an Ilis druid who had asked him to stop

title: Halvenir, the Reaper of Grain
subtitle: the Reaper of Grain.
summary: Too busy working for stories. Month: Halvenir of Salt and Harvest

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Halvenir, the Reaper of Grain: harvest, seasons, plenty, toil.
Too busy working for stories. Month: Halvenir of Salt and Harvest

Halvenir’s abundance has a season and a cost in work. Salt and Harvest, the month that bears his name, evokes the moment when the labor of many hands has to become provisions that will last after the fields have been cut.

epigraph.quote: Nobody writes stories about the harvest. We are too busy bringing it in.
epigraph.by: A farmer of the Heartland's Storm Water fields, at the last sheaf of the season

title: The Hunger That Warms
subtitle: A name the islands know.
summary: The Aspect of Fire. It holds: Warmth, destruction, the forge, passion, the volcano. The Keeping is its humblest rite

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Hunger That Warms is the Aspect of Fire, one of the Six Aspects that the native peoples pray to directly.
Primal names: Kel-Vorrath, the First Spark, the Ever-Eating.
Mundane names: the Hearth, the Red Tongue, Old Ember.
It holds: Warmth, destruction, the forge, passion, the volcano. The Keeping is its humblest rite.

facts: Kel-Vorrath, the First Spark, the Ever-Eating
the Hearth, the Red Tongue, Old Ember

epigraph.quote: Feed me a little each night and I will keep your children warm. Forget me once and I will remember you.
epigraph.by: A forge-mother of Everfall, to a Heartland apprentice who let his hearth go out

title: Idel
subtitle: Trade, trickery, travel, music.
summary: The honest deal and the clever one. Month: Idel of Coin and Cargo

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Idel: trade, trickery, travel, music.
The honest deal and the clever one. Month: Idel of Coin and Cargo

Idel’s road runs through the port and the marketplace. The same traveler can bargain over cargo, trade a tune for company and listen carefully for the difference between an honest deal and one that is merely clever.

title: Iliriel, the Perfect Form
subtitle: the Perfect Form.
summary: Perfection, indifferent to whether it comforts or wounds

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Iliriel, the Perfect Form: beauty, art, aesthetic glory.
Perfection, indifferent to whether it comforts or wounds

Iliriel’s perfection measures a work by the form it attains. That leaves room for beauty that unsettles its audience: a work may answer every demand of its maker’s art while remaining painful to look at.

epigraph.quote: Perfection does not comfort. It cuts clean, and it leaves you with the cut. Learn to love the edge.
epigraph.by: A sculptor of Goldwind's Mirror Hall, to an apprentice who had wept at the first finished statue

title: Ilis
subtitle: Animals, balance, life, plants.
summary: Druids and keepers of balance

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Ilis: animals, balance, life, plants.
Druids and keepers of balance

For the druids and keepers of balance who turn to Ilis, animal and plant life belong to the same living system. A change that seems small in one part of it, such as losing the cover that shelters an animal, can matter far beyond where it began.

title: Kessa of the Crossroads
subtitle: Travel, choice, chance meetings.
summary: Coins left at crossroads; three roads meeting

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Kessa of the Crossroads: travel, choice, chance meetings.
Coins left at crossroads; three roads meeting

Kessa’s sign is three roads meeting, and the coins left at crossroads belong to her. A junction makes her domains tangible: a traveler has to choose a route, and that choice determines which strangers can cross their path.

epigraph.quote: Every road has three ways out of it. Choose one, and you will meet someone who chose another. Leave a coin for her before you choose.
epigraph.by: A wayside shrine-keeper of the Heartland's southern roads, to a young wanderer who could not decide which road to take

title: Khadras
subtitle: Life, glory, music, magic.
summary: Joy through art and bravery; bards and healers

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Khadras: life, glory, music, magic.
Joy through art and bravery; bards and healers

Khadras gives bards and healers common ground in the joy of life. Music, magic and bravery can restore something to a person even before a wound closes, giving glory a place in acts of care as well as deeds worth singing about.

title: Khagun the Rotmother
subtitle: Plague, famine, the swarm.
summary: Plague as blind nature; a fly upon a skull

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Khagun the Rotmother: plague, famine, the swarm.
Plague as blind nature; a fly upon a skull

Khagun’s plague follows the blind logic of a swarm, moving wherever it finds a way to spread. The fly upon a skull gives her a fitting sign: the life of the swarm can continue even where famine and sickness have ended other lives.

epigraph.quote: Nature does not hate you. It only eats. Learn to be eaten gracefully, and you may yet feed something worth feeding.
epigraph.by: A famine-priest of the Heartland's dry years, at a field of blackened grain, to a farmer who had asked why the swarm had come

title: Korthax the Iron Crown
subtitle: Conquest, empire, dominion.
summary: The whispered truth behind the Empire's Magnus

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Korthax the Iron Crown: conquest, empire, dominion.
The whispered truth behind the Empire's Magnus

Korthax embodies conquest as a claim to dominion over others. The suggestion that he lies behind the Empire’s public devotion to Magnus remains a whisper, and it is worth keeping that uncertainty when reading accounts of imperial religion.

epigraph.quote: The strong civilization rules. The weak civilization is erased. This is not cruelty. It is history, and history is merciful to those who write it.
epigraph.by: A Korvan officer of the imperial frontier, in private, to a native guide who had asked why his village was being burned

title: The Laughing Beast
subtitle: Wild instinct, the untamed self.
summary: Berserkers and the were-touched

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Laughing Beast: wild instinct, the untamed self.
Berserkers and the were-touched

The Laughing Beast appeals to berserkers and the were-touched through the untamed part of the self. Its province is the instant instinct takes charge, when the body has already answered a threat before the mind can give that answer a name.

epigraph.quote: You were born with a tooth and a howl. Civilization made you forget it. Remember it, and run.
epigraph.by: A berserker of the Southern Wilds, after a feast, to a Council soldier who had asked him to sit still

title: Law, the Sun King
subtitle: the Sun King.
summary: Greater God; judges, noble courts, the Navy of the north

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Law, the Sun King: law, sun, fire, purification.
Greater God; judges, noble courts, the Navy of the north

Judges, noble courts and the northern Navy all find something of their authority in the Sun King. His sun and cleansing fire give divine force to the idea that a judgment can expose a wrong and call for its removal.

title: Lilim
subtitle: Tempest, sea, protection, glory.
summary: The sea's lawful wrath; sailors beg her mercy

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Lilim: tempest, sea, protection, glory.
The sea's lawful wrath; sailors beg her mercy
Sailors ask Lilim for mercy because her protection and her tempest belong to the same sea. The force that can carry a crew to glory can just as readily put every person aboard in need of shelter.

title: Liora of the Open Heart
subtitle: Love, desire, union, passion.
summary: Love freely given; both moons are her lovers; symbol two clasped hands. Month: Liora of Heart and Hand

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Liora of the Open Heart: love, desire, union, passion.
Love freely given; both moons are her lovers; symbol two clasped hands. Month: Liora of Heart and Hand

Liora’s two clasped hands make sense as a sign of love freely given: the gesture needs both people. Her love for both moons sets that intimacy on the scale of the sky, and her month bears the name Heart and Hand.

epigraph.quote: Love freely given is the only kind that does not turn into a debt. I have seen the other kind, and I will not pray to it.
epigraph.by: A Liora chaplain of the Heartland ports, at a wedding where the bride's family had demanded a dowry in writing

title: Lunia, the Lady of Light
subtitle: the Lady of Light.
summary: Her clerics root out corruption

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Lunia, the Lady of Light: purity, exorcism, glory, law.
Her clerics root out corruption

Lunia’s clerics put purity and law to work through exorcism and the search for corruption. For her followers, bringing a hidden wrong into the light is part of cleansing it, since secrecy can let it take root again.

epigraph.quote: Light is not kind. It only shows you what you were hiding, and then it lets you decide what to do about it.
epigraph.by: A Lunian exorcist of Goldwind, to a Heartland widow who had brought her a husband's old ring, which the exorcist found to be cursed

title: Maela the Mender
subtitle: Medicine, healing, mercy, childbirth.
summary: Hospices and plague-wards; symbol a green cross of bound reeds

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Maela the Mender: medicine, healing, mercy, childbirth.
Hospices and plague-wards; symbol a green cross of bound reeds

Maela’s green cross of bound reeds belongs in hospices and plague wards as much as beside a birthing bed. Medicine and mercy meet in the daily work of those places, where someone must continue caring for the sick after the immediate crisis passes.

epigraph.quote: Let the enemy sleep in the sickroom too. A fever does not check whose side you are on.
epigraph.by: A Frontier surgeon of the Mercy House, at the bedside of a Navy prisoner

title: Magnus
subtitle: Destiny, civilization, courage, humanity.
summary: Perhaps the divinized Korvan; the Empire's public face

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Magnus: destiny, civilization, courage, humanity.
Perhaps the divinized Korvan; the Empire's public face

Magnus gives the Empire a public language for courage, civilization and human destiny. The possibility that he is Korvan raised to divinity remains unresolved, even where imperial memory brings the two names close together.

title: Memnara, the Unbroken Thread
subtitle: the Unbroken Thread.
summary: Enemy of every forgery and erased name. Month: Memnara of Bell and Remembrance

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Memnara, the Unbroken Thread: memory, history, lineage, the true record.
Enemy of every forgery and erased name. Month: Memnara of Bell and Remembrance

Memnara keeps the connection between a name, the record that preserves it and the people who remember it. A forgery or an erased name can break that connection for generations. Her month is known as Bell and Remembrance.

facts: Memory, history, lineage, the true record

epigraph.quote: A name that is written down and read aloud is never quite dead. Write it, and I will keep it. Erase it, and I will ask why.
epigraph.by: A clerk of the Imperial Archives, copying the lineage of a noble house that had asked for a forgery

title: Mhavros
subtitle: The ocean depths, hatred, suffering, the abyss.
summary: Greater God of evil; the drowned and the things in Abyssara

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Mhavros: the ocean depths, hatred, suffering, the abyss.
Greater God of evil; the drowned and the things in Abyssara

Mhavros holds the suffering and hatred of the depths, and his reach is associated with the drowned and the things of Abyssara. His place in the pantheon gives the sea below the light a divine presence of its own.

facts: The ocean depths, hatred, suffering, the abyss

title: Morthryn, the Pale Empress of Air and Ending
subtitle: the Pale Empress of Air and Ending.
summary: Archfey of the Faewild. Winter, the Long Silence. Cold, cruelty, silence; exiled the Frost Elves; covets Krysta.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Morthryn, the Pale Empress of Air and Ending is one of the Archfey, the divine-tier rulers of the Faewild.
Court: Winter, the Long Silence.
Holds: Cold, cruelty, silence; exiled the Frost Elves; covets Krysta.

title: The Nameless God
subtitle: Hope, purification, meditation.
summary: Hope in the darkest hour; his name lost, his mask faceless

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Nameless God: hope, purification, meditation.
Hope in the darkest hour; his name lost, his mask faceless

The Nameless God’s faceless mask gives a shape to devotion without restoring the name that was lost. His domains of hope, purification and meditation meet in the darkest hour, when the act of holding on may be all that is possible.

epigraph.quote: I do not know my name. The priests who knew it are dead, and the ones who remember it do not say it aloud. But I am still here, and I am still hoping for you.
epigraph.by: A hermit of the Frontier's ice-caves, to a dying soldier who asked whether the god had a name at all

title: Naxithe the Dream-Eater
subtitle: Nightmares, madness, fear.
summary: Dreams that hunt you; a weeping, lidless eye

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Naxithe the Dream-Eater: nightmares, madness, fear.
Dreams that hunt you; a weeping, lidless eye
Naxithe’s weeping, lidless eye gives form to a nightmare that pursues the dreamer. Fear is the center of that domain: the sleeper cannot choose to look away from what the dream keeps bringing back.

epigraph.quote: You did not dream that. Something dreamed it for you, and it is hungry. Stay awake, child, and it will have to find another.
epigraph.by: A dream-reader of Greyhaven, at a bedside in the night, to a child who would not stop screaming in her sleep

title: Nethis, the Sealed Word
subtitle: the Sealed Word.
summary: The pact with teeth; patron of the Marked and of warlocks

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Nethis, the Sealed Word: pacts, bargains, the binding contract, the price.
The pact with teeth; patron of the Marked and of warlocks

Nethis is patron to the Marked and to warlocks, and the price matters as much to him as the promise. His domain begins where an agreement can bind the speaker long after the circumstances that made the bargain attractive have changed.

facts: Pacts, bargains, the binding contract, the price

epigraph.quote: Every bargain has a price, and the price is always written in the margin. Read the margin, or do not sign.
epigraph.by: A notary of the Marked quarters, to a young tiefling who had asked for a bargain that would save her mother

title: Oda
subtitle: Oracle, mystery, shadow, knowledge.
summary: She reveals only what she must

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Oda: oracle, mystery, shadow, knowledge.
She reveals only what she must

Oda’s oracles put knowledge and shadow in the same answer. What she reveals may be enough for a person to act, while what she withholds leaves the person responsible for deciding how far the answer can be trusted.

title: Okram
subtitle: Coast, fishers, survival, protection.
summary: The sea as sustenance. Month: Okram of Harbor and Rest

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Okram: coast, fishers, survival, protection.
The sea as sustenance. Month: Okram of Harbor and Rest

Okram’s coast is the sea as a source of food and a place where people work to survive. His protection belongs to fishers who depend on those waters, and his month, Harbor and Rest, gives the return to shore its place beside the catch.

title: Oorah
subtitle: Cold, community, courage, glory.
summary: The far south's goddess of surviving together

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Oorah: cold, community, courage, glory.
The far south's goddess of surviving together
Oorah’s courage takes the form of people keeping one another alive in the cold. Her worship belongs both to the far south and to the Frost Elves, whose faith also honors Vukharr and Volvieg.

title: Orphanos
subtitle: Gluttony, greed, hunger, envy.
summary: Hoarders consumed by want

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Orphanos: gluttony, greed, hunger, envy.
Hoarders consumed by want

Orphanos joins gluttony, greed, hunger and envy in an appetite that grows as it is fed. The hoarder in his domain can possess more than they could ever use and still experience another person’s good fortune as a loss.

title: The Pale Man
subtitle: Necromancy, knowledge, death, law.
summary: The cold intellect over the passage from life to death

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Pale Man: necromancy, knowledge, death, law.
The cold intellect over the passage from life to death

The Pale Man approaches the passage from life to death through necromancy, law and knowledge. His cold intellect gives that passage the character of something that can be studied, classified and subjected to a rule.

title: Patrons of the Peoples
subtitle: A name the islands know.
summary: Every people honors a patron of its own, or shares one, alongside the wider pantheon and the Concord.

rows: Aelthuvar, the First Light, the Dawnfather, who led the elves out of the Faewild. High Elves honor his Faewild-bound face, Wood Elves his world-rooted face. The Frost Elves have forgotten him and follow Vukharr, Oorah and Volvieg. The drow keep a third face, the Buried Dawn, the light that went down into the dark and stayed

The Forge-Pantheon: Durmakhâim, the All-Anvil (also the Quenching), lord of metal, craft and fate; Khazrûkk, the Debt Below (also the Tally), god of grudges and the unforgiving ledger; Varganthûr, the Deep Hearth, god of the clan-hold
Gorrokar, the Devouring Tusk, the old Orka war-god, kept lean and private by the Remembering Tribes
The Skarn, the Many-Mouthed: the small and clever outlast the great and proud. His fae-warped face is worshipped by the goblinoids trapped in the Faewild
Imperial-descended folk look to Magnus and the memory of Korvan; native peoples pray to the Aspects and honor Yaxqel, the First Walker, eldest ancestor of the south; Council folk keep the Concord
Penny Greenstep, folk-saint of luck and the well-laid table, with Eo, Brother Dog and Castellyn
Tik, the Tinkering Spark, with Rhor and Eliol
Vorthung, the First Crown, the giant progenitor-god; goliaths keep him alongside Khaurun
Khaurun, the Fourfold: discipline, balance, the inner fire; shared with monks of every people
Sszathra, the Cold-Blooded Mother, braided with the Savage Lord Ssvayuk, "her living hand"
Tharuun, the Sworn Breath, the clan-oath god; the kobolds' Vrix is the cousin whose stolen scale broke the oldest oath
Vrix, the Underscale, clever ancestor beneath the true dragons
Aevyr, the Open Wing; the Aethyn also honor the Breath That Wanders, Tramica and Skaia
Eirhal, the Living Lightning, their own god; Badron is their beast-god
Sathrun, the Steady Flame; the Hunger That Warms is their fire
Vaythra, the Coral Sovereign; the Drowning Mother and the courts; in the deeps, Mhavros
Yarrowen, the Rooted Crown; the Green Fire and the Spring Court (Aoifel)
Ulmach, the Herd-Father; the Sleeping Giant beneath the standing-stones; the dead graze in the Endless Pasture, the Maghren
Hyssen, the Turning Loam; the Quiet Door as compost for the next life
Coriell, the Between, the bridge between the two families
A magpie-creed of whichever god seems likeliest to improve the next deal
Fortura and Mishri the Nine-Lived; a stolen-voice face of the Skarn

title: Pyraxis, the Unbowed Flame
subtitle: the Unbowed Flame.
summary: Archfey of the Faewild. Summer, the Burning Crown. Passion, glory, fire, heroic war; the most martial sovereign.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Pyraxis, the Unbowed Flame is one of the Archfey, the divine-tier rulers of the Faewild.
Court: Summer, the Burning Crown.
Holds: Passion, glory, fire, heroic war; the most martial sovereign.

epigraph.quote: I have never once been defeated in a fair war. Fight me in the Burning Crown, and I will show you what it means to be remembered.
epigraph.by: A Faewild knight of the Summer Court, to a Heartland captain who had asked for a truce

title: The Quiet Door
subtitle: A name the islands know.
summary: The Aspect of Death. It holds: Death, decay, memory, ancestors, the passage

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Quiet Door is the Aspect of Death, one of the Six Aspects that the native peoples pray to directly.
Primal names: Morr-Ungal, the Last Cold, the One Who Waits.
Mundane names: the End, the Long Sleep, the Grey Guest.
It holds: Death, decay, memory, ancestors, the passage.

facts: Morr-Ungal, the Last Cold, the One Who Waits
the End, the Long Sleep, the Grey Guest

epigraph.quote: The door opens for everyone, and it closes behind them with a sound like a latch. Do not stand in the frame.
epigraph.by: An old Frost Elf of the Unpainted, at a grave cut in the ice, to a child who wanted to follow a parent through

title: Rhor
subtitle: Craft, luck, artifice, travel.
summary: The luck to make a thing last. Month: Rhor of Net and Anvil

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Rhor: craft, luck, artifice, travel.
The luck to make a thing last. Month: Rhor of Net and Anvil

Rhor’s craft is judged by what lasts in use. A net has to hold when it is hauled in and a tool must survive the work it was made for. Those tests suit the patron of craft and travel whose month is called Net and Anvil.

title: Saelthar the Cold Throne
subtitle: Hierarchy, ambition, bloodline.
summary: Rank as divine right; a throne of frost

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Saelthar the Cold Throne: hierarchy, ambition, bloodline.
Rank as divine right; a throne of frost

Saelthar’s throne of frost embodies hierarchy as a divine right inherited through blood. Ambition in his domain is caught between the desire to rise and the insistence that rank already belongs to those born to it.

epigraph.quote: Rank is the will of the gods. The peasant who forgets it has already forgotten his place in the world, and I will remind him.
epigraph.by: A Heartland noble of an old house, at a feast, to a guest who had asked about the price of bread in the village

title: Sevrin the Chainbreaker
subtitle: Liberty, rebellion, the broken yoke.
summary: Patron of the Southern Rebels; outlawed by the Empire; symbol a snapped iron collar

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Sevrin the Chainbreaker: liberty, rebellion, the broken yoke.
Patron of the Southern Rebels; outlawed by the Empire; symbol a snapped iron collar

Sevrin’s snapped iron collar gives the Southern Rebels a clear image of the freedom they seek. The Empire outlaws his worship, so openly honoring him can carry political weight before a follower has said a word about rebellion.

epigraph.quote: You kneel because they told you that kneeling was the law. I told you to stand. Stand, and see what the law does about it.
epigraph.by: A Southern Rebel, at the breaking of a slave-collar in the marsh, to a freed thrall who was afraid to walk away

title: The Six Aspects
subtitle: A name the islands know.
summary: Older and stranger than the Concord: Water, Fire, Earth, Sky, Life, and Death, prayed to directly by the native peoples.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The natives of Kalvatar never bothered with the gods' masks. They pray to the Primordials directly, as Aspects, by their primal names in the deep places and their mundane names at the hearth.

sections.title: At a glance
paragraphs: The derivative Aspects, lesser children of the six, invoked by shamans for particular work:
Storm: Water and Sky.
Ash: Fire and Death.
Marsh: Water and Earth.
Spirit: Sky and Life.
Ice: Water and Death.
Magma: Fire and Earth.
"You imperials pray to a man with a sword and call him War. We do not pray to War. War is just Fire that learned to walk." A southern elder.

rows: the Tide, the Old Wet, Grandmother Salt
Oceans, rain, rivers, blood, birth, dissolution. The most revered Aspect in Kalvatar
Kel-Vorrath, the First Spark, the Ever-Eating
the Hearth, the Red Tongue, Old Ember
Warmth, destruction, the forge, passion, the volcano. The Keeping is its humblest rite
Durn-Hakka, the Bone Below, the Stone That Dreams
the Ground, the Old Back, Mother Root
Mountains, stone, soil, endurance, the dead beneath, the giants of old
Aëthyr-Vol, the Five Skies, the Open Mouth
the Wind, the High Blue, the Wanderer
Wind, storm, breath, freedom, the five layers of the heavens
Ilavash, the Spreading, the Thousand Mouths
the Growth, the Green, Mother Leaf
Plants, beasts, fertility, hunger, the jungle's reach
Morr-Ungal, the Last Cold, the One Who Waits
the End, the Long Sleep, the Grey Guest
Death, decay, memory, ancestors, the passage

title: Skaia
subtitle: Dreams, fate, sky, stars.
summary: Greater God

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Skaia: dreams, fate, sky, stars.
Greater God

The pantheon teaches that every star is a dead god. Skaia’s dominion over the night sky therefore reaches into one of the oldest sorrows in Kalvatar: the lights by which sailors find their way are also a record of what the world has lost. The Aethyn honor Skaia alongside the Breath That Wanders and Tramica, and the calendar names her as the keeper of Starfall, observed on the thirtieth of Eliol.

title: The Sleeping Giant
subtitle: A name the islands know.
summary: The Aspect of Earth. It holds: Mountains, stone, soil, endurance, the dead beneath, the giants of old

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Sleeping Giant is the Aspect of Earth, one of the Six Aspects that the native peoples pray to directly.
Primal names: Durn-Hakka, the Bone Below, the Stone That Dreams.
Mundane names: the Ground, the Old Back, Mother Root.
It holds: Mountains, stone, soil, endurance, the dead beneath, the giants of old.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A Tarvan on the Giant's Table heard the Sleeping Giant turn over in its sleep. She went home and sold every horse she had.” (heard in the Northern Frontier)

facts: Durn-Hakka, the Bone Below, the Stone That Dreams
the Ground, the Old Back, Mother Root

epigraph.quote: The ground does not care what we think of it. That is why we can rest on it.
epigraph.by: A Tarvan herdsman on the high moor, at a standing-stone, to a lowland trader who asked for a better price

title: Sruth the Whisper-in-Coin
subtitle: Secrets, betrayal, blackmail.
summary: A coin pressed to the lips

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Sruth the Whisper-in-Coin: secrets, betrayal, blackmail.
A coin pressed to the lips
Sruth’s coin pressed to the lips gives secrecy a price. A confidence can buy silence or become leverage against the person who shared it, placing blackmail and betrayal within the same exchange.

epigraph.quote: The secret costs a coin. The friend who keeps it costs more. The friend who sells it costs nothing, and that is why they are the most valuable of all.
epigraph.by: A spymaster of the Council's secret houses, to a young clerk who had just been paid to read a sealed letter

title: Stormcaller Vael
subtitle: The wild sea, the free wind.
summary: The storm you ride for the thrill; patron of free captains and smugglers

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Stormcaller Vael: the wild sea, the free wind.
The storm you ride for the thrill; patron of free captains and smugglers

Vael’s storm appeals to free captains and smugglers who value the wind as a chance to sail beyond someone else’s control. The thrill belongs to a sea that remains wild even for a crew skilled enough to ride it.

facts: The wild sea, the free wind

title: The Sword
subtitle: War, strength, wrath, protection.
summary: War as a plain fact of life

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Sword: war, strength, wrath, protection.
War as a plain fact of life

The Sword holds wrath and protection within the ordinary fact of war. The strength that lets someone defend another person can be used to harm them just as readily, and both uses belong to this divine figure.

epigraph.quote: War is not a sin, and it is not a gift. It is weather. Dress for it and get on with your life.
epigraph.by: A Bastion veteran, to a boy who had asked whether the wars would ever end

title: Tholmar, the Star-Wake
subtitle: the Star-Wake.
summary: The art of crossing the sea alive; carries the drowned; every captain's first cup

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Tholmar, the Star-Wake: navigation, safe passage, the drowned.
The art of crossing the sea alive; carries the drowned; every captain's first cup
Tholmar holds both the skill of making a crossing alive and the care of those who drown. A captain’s first cup acknowledges that the voyage and its losses lie within the reach of the same god.

epigraph.quote: Every captain's first cup is for the drowned. We drink it before we count our own cargo.
epigraph.by: A Navy captain of Pearl Groove, at the first sailing of a new ship, to his crew who had not yet earned their wine

title: Tramica
subtitle: Moon, protection, darkness, meditation.
summary: Bound to the lesser, wandering moon

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Tramica: moon, protection, darkness, meditation.
Bound to the lesser, wandering moon
Tramica is bound to the lesser, wandering moon. Darkness in her domain can offer protection and room for meditation. The Aethyn honor her alongside Skaia and The Breath That Wanders.

title: The Unbound
subtitle: A name the islands know.
summary: Archfey of the Faewild. No Court. No season, throne, law or name. Summer calls him the Ash-Laugh, Winter the Thaw-That-Shouldn't, Autumn the Unpaid Debt, Spring the Late Frost.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Unbound is one of the Archfey, the divine-tier rulers of the Faewild.
Court: No Court.
Holds: No season, throne, law or name. Summer calls him the Ash-Laugh, Winter the Thaw-That-Shouldn't, Autumn the Unpaid Debt, Spring the Late Frost.

epigraph.quote: I have no throne, no law and no name. The Courts call me the Ash-Laugh, the Thaw-That-Shouldn't, the Unpaid Debt and the Late Frost. Call me what you like. I am coming anyway.
epigraph.by: A Faewild courier, at the edge of the Courts' borders, to a traveler who had asked for the Unbound's name

title: Ungoreth the Hollow Hunger
subtitle: The Void, annihilation, the unmaking.
summary: The god of nothing; a black circle

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Ungoreth the Hollow Hunger: the void, annihilation, the unmaking.
The god of nothing; a black circle
Ungoreth’s black circle stands for annihilation and the void. His unmaking concerns what is gone altogether, a fate more final than leaving ruins or remains behind for someone to find.

epigraph.quote: Nothing is waiting for you. That is the good news. Come and stop being afraid of it.
epigraph.by: A cultist of the Hollows, on the edge of the Void, to a man who had lost his wife and wanted to stop feeling the loss

title: Vael Mournthorn, the Crimson Reaper-King
subtitle: the Crimson Reaper-King.
summary: Archfey of the Faewild. Autumn, the Red Harvest. Harvest, decline, the price of all things; keeper of the Last Bargain.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Vael Mournthorn, the Crimson Reaper-King is one of the Archfey, the divine-tier rulers of the Faewild.
Court: Autumn, the Red Harvest.
Holds: Harvest, decline, the price of all things; keeper of the Last Bargain.

epigraph.quote: Every harvest has a price. I am the one who names it, and the price is always fair, though it is never kind.
epigraph.by: A Faewild steward of the Autumn Court, at the Last Bargain, to a farmer who had come to bargain for a son's life

title: Varneth, the Threshold Warden
subtitle: the Threshold Warden.
summary: Wards against fae crossings are sworn in his name

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Varneth, the Threshold Warden: boundaries, doorways, the veil, thin places.
Wards against fae crossings are sworn in his name

Varneth’s thresholds include the thin places where the veil can be crossed. A ward sworn in his name puts a boundary under his protection, marking the difference between a doorway and a passage through which something fae might enter.

facts: Boundaries, doorways, the Veil, thin places

epigraph.quote: Every door is a question. I stand in the frame and decide who may ask it. If you want to cross, knock, and tell me your name.
epigraph.by: A Warden of the Veil, at a sealed doorway in Silverport's old quarter, to a Heartland thief who had tried to walk through a wall

title: Vautun the Ledger-Keeper
subtitle: Cruel law, bondage by contract, debt.
summary: The chain that is legal; a quill dripping black

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Vautun the Ledger-Keeper: cruel law, bondage by contract, debt.
The chain that is legal; a quill dripping black

Vautun’s quill drips black because a written debt can bind a person as surely as iron. His cruel law gives bondage the appearance of an orderly agreement and lets the holder of the contract enforce it as a right.

facts: Cruel law, bondage by contract, debt

epigraph.quote: Nothing I have done is illegal. Read the contract. Every word of it is yours, and every word of it binds you to me.
epigraph.by: A debt-clerk of the Heartland's Registry, to a farmer who had asked why his grandmother's debt had never been paid

title: Venkovolkos
subtitle: Commerce, greed, wealth, charm.
summary: Wealth above all

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Venkovolkos: commerce, greed, wealth, charm.
Wealth above all

Venkovolkos brings charm to the pursuit of wealth. Under his creed a friendly bargain can be a way to put profit above every other obligation, even when the person across the table mistakes the charm for goodwill.

title: Veriden the Oathkeeper
subtitle: Justice, truth, oaths, honor.
summary: Witness to every promise; symbol an unbroken silver ring. Month: Veriden of Truth and Justice

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Veriden the Oathkeeper: justice, truth, oaths, honor.
Witness to every promise; symbol an unbroken silver ring. Month: Veriden of Truth and Justice

Veriden’s unbroken silver ring represents a promise that still holds when keeping it becomes difficult. As witness to oaths, he joins truth to honor and justice, the two virtues remembered in the name of his month.

epigraph.quote: Nobody lies in Veriden. Everyone lies in Veriden. They are simply more careful about it, because Veriden is watching.
epigraph.by: A Council magistrate of Sunhold, to a merchant who had sworn an oath on the wrong bell

title: Veshanna the Two-Faced
subtitle: Change, transformation, tides, seasons.
summary: All transitions; a coin always mid-flip

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Veshanna the Two-Faced: change, transformation, tides, seasons.
All transitions; a coin always mid-flip

Veshanna’s coin is always turning, suspended between faces. The tides and seasons bring that image into ordinary life: each change has a moment when the old state is passing and the new one has yet to settle.

epigraph.quote: Change is not a loss. It is the tide turning, and you turn with it or you drown in the old water. I have never once been surprised.
epigraph.by: A coin-flipper of the Pocchin's transition-houses, to a dying man who had asked whether he should be afraid

title: Volvieg
subtitle: Winter, cold, windstorm.
summary: The cold that kills; a god of the Frost Elves

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Volvieg: winter, cold, windstorm.
The cold that kills; a god of the Frost Elves

Volvieg holds the windstorm and the cold that kills. The Frost Elves honor him alongside Vukharr and Oorah, so their faith gives a place to the danger of winter as well as to the courage needed to survive it together.

title: Wanderlight the Far-Strider
subtitle: Exploration, the horizon, discovery.
summary: Cartographers and restless youth; a compass rose with no fixed north

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Wanderlight the Far-Strider: exploration, the horizon, discovery.
Cartographers and restless youth; a compass rose with no fixed north

Wanderlight’s compass rose has no fixed north. It suits cartographers and restless young travelers drawn toward a horizon they have yet to chart, for whom a blank space on the map can be reason enough to set out.

epigraph.quote: Chart it, then sail past the chart. The horizon does not wait for the cartographer.
epigraph.by: A cartographer of the Adventurers' League, at the edge of the last sheet of the Charted Isles, to a young surveyor who had been told the far sea was empty

title: Badron, Queen of Feathers
subtitle: A Savage Lord
summary: The thunderbird, mother of storms. The high winds.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Badron, Queen of Feathers: The thunderbird, mother of storms.

Hunting & feeding: Badron hunts the way weather hunts, she arrives. Where she beats her wings, storms are born; she takes whales from the surface and ships from the swell, and feeds on the great beasts of the open sea. Sailors who see her shadow on the water turn back, if they can.
Progeny: lesser thunderbirds, scattered across the high airs; the rare aarakocra bloodline claims descent from beasts that once served her.
Cults & tribes: the Aethyn regard her with wary reverence as a kindred of the high air; coastal and island folk read her appearances as storm-omens.
Rite: the Reading of the Wings: before the storm season, sky-watchers and Aethyn look for her, and a sighting reshapes the season's sailing.

Legend: that every truly world-ending storm in the archipelago's history has had her at its eye, and that she is not malicious, merely vast, and the storms are only what it looks like when she stretches.

illustration.alt: Badron sweeps over a storm coast, her lightning-filled wings and opening talons dwarfing three sailing ships and a coastal beacon.
illustration.caption: Her wings make the weather.

title: The Hunted
subtitle: A Savage Lord
summary: A juvenile apex the other Lords unite to kill. Everywhere, fleeing.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Hunted: A juvenile apex the other Lords unite to kill.

Across every region, observers report the impossible: progeny of rival Lords, beasts that should tear each other apart, hunting together. A thunderbird beside a fire-lizard. A girallon beside a mire-spawn. A pack of Swordtooths beside a shadow-thing out of the Bonewilds. They ignore all other prey and pursue a single fleeing animal, across territories that should mean nothing but death to each of them. It is not a choice; it is an instinct older than territory, written into the blood of everything a Lord has ever touched.

facts: A juvenile apex the other Lords unite to kill

illustration.alt: Progeny of rival Savage Lords pursue one unseen quarry together through a storm-washed jungle pass: a thunderbird, a fire-lizard and a four-armed girallon.
illustration.caption: Old enemies follow the same trail.

title: KakanKal, Emperor of Flames
subtitle: A Savage Lord
summary: A fire salamander asleep in the magma. Under Everfall.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: KakanKal, Emperor of Flames: A fire salamander asleep in the magma.

Hunting & feeding: when roused, KakanKal feeds on the island itself, stone, forest, and any living thing, and on the raw fire of the deep. Mostly it sleeps, and Everfall lives in the lull between its breaths.
Progeny: lesser fire-lizards, prized by smiths (their shed scales and ember-blood are forge-treasures); the Cindren hold them near-sacred.

Cults & tribes: House Emberheart's ancient fire-cult has ties to it; the Ash Wardens (largely Cindren) keep an unending vigil for its waking; Rankar's Krysta-mining in the volcanic deeps risks waking it, which the Ash Wardens swear will end Everfall.
Rite: the Ember Vigil: the Ash Wardens' watch, and the volcanic-isle festivals that mark each year the Emperor does not wake.

Legend: that KakanKal does not sleep but dreams, and that the volcano's tremors are the Emperor turning over, and that one day it will wake hungry, and Everfall, mines and houses and all, will be the first thing it eats.

facts: A fire salamander asleep in the magma

illustration.alt: The sleeping fire salamander KakanKal fills a volcanic caldera, his closed-eyed head and claws dwarfing distant Ash Warden strongholds.
illustration.caption: Everfall sleeps between his breaths.

title: Kayuntu, the Violent Monarch of the Five Skies
subtitle: A Savage Lord
summary: A colossal wyvern ruling the layers of the sky; at war with Badron. The skies over the Wilds.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Kayuntu, the Violent Monarch of the Five Skies: A colossal wyvern ruling the layers of the sky; at war with Badron.

Hunting & feeding: Kayuntu hunts on the wing through all five layers, chasing rivals (Badron above all) and prey from the breeze to the edge of the Veil; it feeds on whatever flies and whatever it can pluck from below.
Progeny: lesser wyverns of the upper airs, each claiming a narrow band of sky.
Cults & tribes: sky-watchers and some Aethyn track its wars through the layers; a Kayuntu and a Badron clashing across the heavens is an omen no one agrees how to read.
Rite: the Watch of the Five: Aethyn and storm-priests chart which layer Kayuntu rules in a given season, for it is death to fly there.
Legend: that Kayuntu has, twice in recorded memory, flown so high it crossed the thin veil into the Faewild, and come back changed, and angrier.

facts: A colossal wyvern ruling the layers of the sky; at war with Badron

illustration.alt: Kayuntu dives through torn storm layers with jaws and talons open, his serpentine wyvern body dwarfing an entire mountain eyrie.
illustration.caption: Five skies. One furious claimant.

title: Malim, the Laughing Flood
subtitle: A Savage Lord
summary: A giant otter, playful and lethal. Rivers, deltas, coasts.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Malim, the Laughing Flood: A giant otter, playful and lethal.

Hunting & feeding: Malim plays. It toys with boats the way an otter toys with a shell, batting, dragging under, surfacing to watch, and entire fishing fleets have vanished in its games. It feeds on river-beasts and fish in plenty, so its lethality toward people is not hunger but amusement, which the river-folk find far more frightening.
Progeny: lesser giant otters, mischievous and dangerous, that infest the larger rivers.
Cults & tribes: the river tribes adore and fear it in equal measure; they keep their rivers clean for it and tell their children Malim is watching, so be kind to the water.

Legend: that Malim once played with a drowning child, and, on a whim no one can explain, carried her gently to shore instead, and that this is why the river-tribes believe kindness to the water is repaid.

facts: A giant otter, playful and lethal

illustration.alt: Malim, an enormous playful river otter below kaiju scale, rolls beside canoes and sends turbulent water toward wary paddlers.
illustration.caption: The river is a game to him.

title: Momumba, Lord of Apes
subtitle: A Savage Lord
summary: A cunning colossal girallon. Southern Wilds jungle.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Momumba, Lord of Apes: A cunning colossal girallon.

Hunting & feeding: Momumba does not rampage; he plans. He commands a cohort of lesser girallons like a general commands a host, sets ambushes, takes territory, and eats what the jungle offers, fruit, beast, and the occasional army foolish enough to march under his trees. He prefers dominance to slaughter.
Progeny: his girallon cohort, lesser, but coordinated and clever, the most tactical of any Lord's brood.

Cults & tribes: the canopy-tribes who share his valleys pay him tribute in fruit and in enemies (bound captives left at the tree-line), and in return he leaves their villages standing. Some tribes treat his moods as law.
Rite: the Tribute of the Ape: the seasonal leaving of fruit and bound foes at the edge of his territory.

Legend: it is told that Momumba once held an entire conversation with a Hunter who'd come to kill him, and let her live, because "she asked the right question." No one agrees on what the question was, and the Hunter never told.

illustration.alt: Momumba, a colossal white four-armed girallon, bares his canines above a jungle acropolis whose ruined towers fit beneath his hands.
illustration.caption: The jungle has a throne.

title: Shakarr, the Shadow of Death
subtitle: A Savage Lord
summary: A sabertooth of living shadow. The Bonewilds.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Shakarr, the Shadow of Death: A sabertooth of living shadow.

Hunting & feeding: Shakarr is never seen, only its work: perfect kills, no struggle, no sound, the prey simply ended and left, or taken. It feeds on the dying and the dead of the Bonewilds, and perhaps on something subtler, the passing itself.
Progeny: shadow-things, lesser umbral predators that seep from the Bonewilds' dark; they leave the same signature, silent, clean, certain.
Cults & tribes: the natives do not name it aloud. To speak its name in the Bonewilds is to invite its attention. There is no cult so much as a vast, shared, careful silence.
Rite: the Unspoken: when one must cross the Bonewilds, one goes in silence, leaves a portion of one's kill, and does not look back.
Legend: that Shakarr is not a beast at all but the Bonewilds' own death given shape, and that everything that dies in the south, in some sense, passes through its jaws.

illustration.alt: Shakarr crouches among the Bonewilds ribs beneath two moons, black fur bristling, saber fangs exposed and claws extended toward a wary traveler.
illustration.caption: In the Bonewilds, even a name can be too loud.

title: Ssvayuk, the Mud That Breathes
subtitle: A Savage Lord
summary: A swamp-serpent grown over with false islands. The great bogs.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Ssvayuk, the Mud That Breathes: A swamp-serpent grown over with false islands.

Hunting & feeding: Ssvayuk barely moves: it waits, mostly submerged, and takes whatever wanders onto the false ground of its back or into the black water of its hollows. Travelers have built camps on what they thought was solid land. It feeds slowly and rarely, on the scale of seasons.
Progeny: the Mirewallow saurians are said to be its distant kin or lesser spawn; lesser bog-serpents haunt its margins.
Cults & tribes: the lizardfolk of the bogs revere it as a grandmother-god (and worship Sszathra through it, Volume V), reading omens in the rare shifts of its slow body.
Rite: the Reading of the Mud: lizardfolk elders interpret Ssvayuk's stirrings as prophecy; a single great movement of the Mud That Breathes can send a whole tribe migrating.

Legend: that Ssvayuk is so old it remembers the giants, and that if it ever truly rose: uncoiled its full length from the bog it has worn like a blanket for ten thousand years, the south would learn that what it called a swamp was a sleeping titan.

facts: A swamp-serpent grown over with false islands

illustration.alt: Ssvayuk opens its immense serpentine jaws as tree-covered coils rise like mountains from a bog, pouring mud and waterfalls toward a tiny escaping boat.
illustration.caption: The island takes a breath.

title: Thalgorath, the Tide-Tyrant
subtitle: A Savage Lord
summary: An abyssal horror; the Red Choir's choirmaster. The Sunken Thrones, Abyssara's edge.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Thalgorath, the Tide-Tyrant: An abyssal horror; the Red Choir's choirmaster.

Hunting & feeding: Thalgorath rises from the Sunken Thrones only rarely, and when it does, coastal towns are simply gone by morning, with no wreckage and no bodies, only empty foundations and a high-water line. What it does with what it takes, no one who has seen has lived to say.
Progeny: the deep horrors of the abyssal trenches; lesser abyssal things that the sea-peoples themselves flee.
Cults & tribes: the deep sea-peoples of the Coral Kingdoms have their own name for it, which they will not teach surface-dwellers; some of the darkest deep cults may worship it as Mhavros's own hand.

Rite: dread of the King Tide: when both moons and the sun align and the deep climbs highest, coastal folk who know the old fears stay far from the water, for that is when the Tide-Tyrant is likeliest to rise.

Legend: that Thalgorath does not rise to feed but to remember: that it surfaces only when something in the deep changes, and that a town vanishing is merely the cost of the Tide-Tyrant turning its attention briefly to the surface world.

facts: An abyssal horror; the Red Choir's choirmaster

illustration.alt: Thalgorath opens its predatory beak over an entire drowned city, its immense tentacles dwarfing palaces and tearing currents through the Sunken Thrones.
illustration.caption: The deep has turned its attention upward.

title: Tyrak'Zhul, the World-Eater
subtitle: A Savage Lord
summary: The tyrant-father of all saurians, the First Jaw. The saurian heartlands.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Tyrak'Zhul, the World-Eater: The tyrant-father of all saurians, the First Jaw.

Hunting & feeding: Tyrak'Zhul is the apex the apexes fear; it hunts the greatest beasts of the deep jungle, the Eldersaurs, the Dreadmaws, anything large enough to be worth the effort, and the saurians themselves flee its territory. It feeds on the mighty, because nothing small is worth its jaws.
Progeny: every Dreadmaw and Swordtooth is, in the deepest sense, its descendant; its direct progeny are titanic predatory saurians, Eldersaurs in their own right.

Cults & tribes: the saurian-tamers of Jakupur keep a careful, awed distance; the deep-jungle tribes name it the First Jaw and the Tyrant-Father, and some saurian-cults hold that all saurians will one day return to it.
Rite: the Stilling: when Tyrak'Zhul is known to be moving, the deep tribes still their saurian-herds and go silent, for a panicked herd draws the First Jaw.

Legend: that the saurians do not fear Tyrak'Zhul as prey fears a predator, but as children fear a stern god: and that it does not hunt them out of hunger but out of judgment, culling the saurian world to keep it strong.

facts: The tyrant-father of all saurians, the First Jaw

illustration.alt: Tyrak’Zhul roars above a jungle valley, his colossal clawed foot breaking a forested escarpment while tiny tamers flee a watchpost.
illustration.caption: The First Jaw passes. The herds fall silent.

title: Ulgrenn, the Hollow Song
subtitle: A Savage Lord
summary: A blind cave-leviathan that sings with the voices of the swallowed. The undercaverns and Orka ruins.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Ulgrenn, the Hollow Song: A blind cave-leviathan that sings with the voices of the swallowed.

Hunting & feeding: Ulgrenn sings: a resonance through the tunnels woven from the cries of all it has devoured, and the song lures: the lost, the curious, and the half-mad follow it down into the dark, and are added to the choir. It feeds on what the song brings it.
Progeny: lesser cave-things, blind and resonant, that echo fragments of the Hollow Song deeper in the earth.

Cults & tribes: the Orka knew it, and some of their deepest ruins were sealed against it, not built around it. Modern delvers who hear singing in the deep places are warned, by anyone who knows, to stop their ears and climb.
Rite: the Stopping of the Ears: those who must go deep carry wax and a vow of silence, and never, ever sing back.

Legend: that if you listen to the Hollow Song long enough you will hear a voice you love calling your name, and that this is how it takes the strong, who would never follow a stranger but will always follow that.

facts: A blind cave-leviathan that sings with the voices of the swallowed

illustration.alt: Eyeless Ulgrenn advances through flooded Orka halls, its cavernous throat dwarfing a submerged palace district and three retreating delvers.
illustration.caption: Do not answer the song.

title: Vukharr, the White Hunger
subtitle: A Savage Lord
summary: A starving tundra-beast of ribs and white fur. The deep Icy Expanse.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Vukharr, the White Hunger: A starving tundra-beast of ribs and white fur.

Hunting & feeding: Vukharr moves with the killing cold, and where it walks, the food runs out, game flees, fish vanish, the land goes barren. It feeds on everything and is never full; its hunger is its nature, and famine is its footprint.
Progeny: lesser white-hunger beasts, gaunt and ravenous, that herald its approach by the emptying of the land.

Cults & tribes: the Frost Elves both fear and emulate it, warbands paint their faces as its skull and take its endless hunger as a model of the merciless survival their exile demands. Some Frost Elf bands all but worship it, having forgotten the gods they lost.
Rite: the Skull-Paint before a Frost Elf raid, and the grim famine-watch of the Long Night, when the deep Expanse fears Vukharr is moving.
Legend: that Vukharr cannot be killed by any wound, only outlasted: that it is hunger, and you do not kill hunger, you merely survive until it passes you by.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Frost Elves have stopped raiding the Auroral Vault. The Frost Elves say Vukharr is dreaming of something new.” (heard in the Icy Expanse)

facts: A starving tundra-beast of ribs and white fur

illustration.alt: Gaunt, white-furred Vukharr snarls through a blizzard as one immense paw shatters a glacier above a tiny refuge and fleeing travelers.
illustration.caption: Famine walks with the killing cold.

title: The Hundred and Fifty Ways
subtitle: Magic in the islands
summary: A gathered list, as a well-traveled waybook might hold them, by the room of the house they live in.

sections.title: I. The Kettle & the Cup
paragraphs: The Sweetening: sweetens one cup without sugar; never sweeter than "just right."
The Even Pour: pours from any pot without a single drip.
Patience of the Kettle: the kettle holds just-boiled for the length of one visit.
The Fair Steep: tea steeps to exactly how you like it, every time.
Cream-That-Keeps: milk stays sweet one extra day.
The Unburnt Sip: the first sip never scalds.
Two Cups' Grace: stretches the pot to one more cup, a little thinner; no one minds.
The Reading Leaves: tea leaves settle into pretty shapes. (Meaningless ones. The Way is honest about this.)
The Quiet Spoon: stirring makes no clink against the cup.
Warm-Hands Cup: the cup warms cold fingers without cooling the tea.
The Last Drop: the honey jar yields one more spoonful than it should.
Salt-or-Sugar: tells you, by smell alone, which unmarked jar is which.
The Welcome Smell: the pot's aroma carries to the garden gate, as invitation.
The Steadied Tray: cups don't slide on a tray carried across the kitchen.
Grounds-Be-Gone: coffee grounds settle, and stay settled.

sections.title: II. The Oven & the Pot
paragraphs: The Rising: dough rises even in a cold kitchen.
The Unstuck Loaf: bread leaves the pan whole.
Crust's Blessing: the crust crackles just so.
The Watched Pot: a pot you've marked murmurs your name just before it boils over.
The Even Slice: cake and loaf come apart in equal slices, to the relief of every parent.
Stretch-the-Stew: the pot feeds one unexpected guest; everyone swears their bowl was full.
The Kindly Onion: onions bring no tears in your kitchen.
Burnt-Bottom's Pardon: lifts the taste of "slightly caught" from a dish. (Not truly burnt. The Way has standards.)
The Settled Grease: fat does not spit from your pan.
Fish-Without-Fingers: the smell of fish leaves your hands at a word.
The Ripe Reckoning: a knuckle-tap tells you truly whether the melon is ready.
Peel-in-One: the apple peel comes off in a single unbroken ribbon.
The Honest Taste: your tasting spoon tells you exactly what's missing. (Salt. It is usually salt.)
Crumbs-to-Corner: table crumbs gather themselves at one corner for the sweeping.
The Second-Day Pie: leftovers taste as if made this morning.

sections.title: III. Hearth & Candle
paragraphs: First-Spark: a well-laid hearth takes on the first strike. (Famously refuses to work outdoors in wind.)
The Banked Promise: embers keep till morning without feeding.
Smoke-Knows-the-Flue: hearth-smoke never backs into the room.
The Steady Flame: a candle doesn't gutter when the door opens.
Wax-Miser: a candle burns one extra evening.
The Soft Light: lamplight turns kind to tired eyes.
Ash-to-Pan: cold ashes sweep themselves into the pan.
The Fire's Color: hearth-flames take a festival color for an evening.
Pop-and-Settle: the fire's crackle falls into a pleasing rhythm for storytelling.
The Unsinged Sleeve: reaching across your own hearth, your cuff never catches.
Chimney's Breath: a low hum tells you the flue is clear before you light.
The Last Coal: there is always one live coal in the morning ash to start from.
Candle-Mind: the candle snuffs itself when you fall asleep reading.
The Shared Warmth: the warm spot by the fire widens by exactly one more chair.
Hearthstone's Welcome: the hearthstone stays warm underfoot an hour past the fire.

sections.title: IV. Needle, Thread & Cloth
paragraphs: Thread-the-Needle: the thread finds the eye on the first try.
The Patient Knot: thread never tangles while you work.
Hem's Memory: a hem you pin stays pinned, without pins.
The Hidden Mend: a darn vanishes into the weave. (Cosmetic. The sock knows the truth.)
Button's Loyalty: a button sewn with this Way outlives the shirt.
The Fitting Shimmer: a half-made garment shows, faintly, how it will hang when finished.
Wrinkles-Away: a shaken garment hangs as if pressed.
The Dry Line: laundry dries on the line even under a grey sky.
Color-True: dyes do not run in your wash.
The Even Shear: cloth cuts along a true line.
Cedar's Constancy: the cedar smell of a woolens-chest never fades. (Moths draw their own conclusions. The Way touches the chest, never the moth, and that is the whole law of it.)
The Borrowed Fit: a hand-me-down hangs a little kinder on its new wearer.
Sock-Finds-Sock: stray socks turn up in pairs on washing day.
The Soft Collar: a stiff new collar breaks in overnight.
Stain's Confession: a stain shows you what made it, so you know how to wash it.

sections.title: V. Broom & Basin
paragraphs: The Gathering Sweep: one pass of the broom, and the dust walks to the pile.
Bright-Basin: wash-water stays warm to the last dish.
The Unchipped Stack: stacked crockery never chips against itself.
Grease-Yields: pans release their grease at the first scrub.
The Fresh Room: a closed room smells aired.
Window's Clarity: glass dries without streaks.
The Obedient Spill: spilled liquid pools neatly instead of spreading.
Dust's Delay: a cleaned shelf stays clean a week longer.
The Sweetened Pail: the slop pail keeps its opinions to itself.
Boot-Scrape: mud lets go of boots at the doorstep.
The Folded Fate: linens fold themselves crisp at a pat.
Tarnish-Turn: spoons brighten in the drawer overnight.
The Kind Mirror: your mirror shows you after a good night's sleep. (The Way is a liar, but a kind one.)
Cobweb's Notice: cobwebs glint so you spot them before your guests do.
The Settled Featherbed: the bed plumps itself when patted.

sections.title: VI. Garden, Windowsill & Yard
paragraphs: (Every Way in this room works on water, soil, pot, and path, never on the plant, and never on the bee.)
The Charmed Water: watering-can water falls as the softest rain.
Soil's Answer: a pinch of soil tells your fingers whether it is thirsty.
The Straight Row: seeds sow themselves in a line to make a drill-sergeant weep.
Frost's Courtesy: the windowsill pot stays a breath above freezing.
The Shade That Shifts: a patch of garden shade leans over to where you're working.
Weed-or-Seedling: tells you which green shoot is which.
The Full Can: the watering can is always a little fuller than you remember filling it.
Scarecrow's Posture: the scarecrow holds whatever dashing pose you set it.
The Ripening Sill: windowsill fruit ripens in agreeable order, not all at once.
The Washing Warning: a prickle at the neck says bring the line in before the rain.
The Unbothered Bulbs: stored bulbs and seed-jars keep dry, and keep their labels.
Path-of-Least-Puddles: the garden path's puddles drain by morning.
The Leaning Ladder: the orchard ladder settles true on uneven ground.
The Vase's Secret: the water keeps cut flowers fresh for days longer.
Gate's Tally: the gate-latch clicks once for each head that passed through it today. (It counts hens admirably. The Way works the gate, mind, never the hen.)

sections.title: VII. Tools, Bench & Barrow
paragraphs: (No Way will touch a weapon. They sulk.)
The Found Tool: the tool you set down "somewhere" hums softly until found.
Nail's Confidence: nails start straight at the first tap.
The True Level: a bowl of water shows you true level and true plumb.
Splinter's Farewell: worked wood gives you no splinters.
The Willing Jar-Lid: stuck lids give way to your grip alone. (By common agreement, the most-copied Way in the islands.)
Rust's Patience: the tools in your box keep from rust.
The Measured Twice: a cord remembers one measurement till sundown.
Knot-That-Knows: household knots hold till you, specifically, untie them. (Parcel, clothesline, and gate, ashore. See the Third Refusal.)
The Pot-Mender's Whisper: a hairline crack in crockery seals. (It holds soup, not secrets.)
Squeak's Silence: one hinge, oiled by word alone, for a season.
The Loaded Barrow: the barrow balances its load so it pushes a little lighter.
Saw's Song: the saw sings on-key while your cut runs true.
The Apprentice's Chalk: chalk lines stay crisp till the cut is made.
Glue's Patience: glued joints hold themselves clamped till set.
The Swept Bench: sawdust gathers itself into the bin at day's end.

sections.title: VIII. Ink, Letter & Ledger
paragraphs: The Unsmudged Hand: fresh ink never smears under your palm. (The left-handed call it the Blessing.)
Quill's Economy: one dip of ink writes three lines longer.
The Straight Margin: your lines run level on unlined paper.
Blot's Mercy: an ink-blot lifts, if caught within a breath.
The Sealed Thought: wax seals press clean under your bare thumb, and show a little flower.
Letter's Weather: a letter you write reaches its reader dry.
The Patient Page: a book holds your page without a mark.
Candle-Hours: reading light seems to stretch the evening a little.
The Checked Sum: in your own small household book, a wrong total itches your eye as you read back over it.
Ink-of-the-House: your ink takes a faint color of your choosing.
The Remembered Recipe: a recipe read aloud once from your own waybook stays word-perfect till the dish is done.
Paper's Crease: paper folds itself sharp along your fingernail's line.
The Soft Scratch: your pen makes a pleasant sound instead of a scratching one.
The Dry Well: the inkwell never tips. Though the cat tries.
The Faded Line's Return: old, faded ink darkens while you read it, then politely fades again. (For grandmother's letters.)

sections.title: IX. Comforts of One's Own
paragraphs: (Self only, see the Second Refusal.)
Warm-Hands: your own hands warm as if cupped round a mug.
The Pre-Warmed Bed: the sheets feel slept-in-warm when you climb in.
Morning's Mercy: the first step onto a cold floor doesn't bite.
The Good Stretch: your morning stretch cracks everything, satisfyingly.
Rain-Off-the-Brim: rain beads off your own hat brim. Mostly.
The Untangled Braid: your own hair braids smooth and holds the day.
Shoes-Remember-Feet: new shoes feel broken-in by the second wearing.
The Quiet Yawn: your yawns are silent in company.
Sun-Spot: you always find the patch of sun on a cold porch.
Spectacles' Perch: your spectacles stay up your nose, and un-fogged by the soup.
The Carried Tune: a song you hum stays on key. To your own ear, at least.
Gray-Hair's Dignity: your gray comes in as distinguished streaks, not patches.
The Nap's Measure: you wake from a nap exactly when the bread needs you.
The Kind Banister: the banister meets your hand exactly where you reach for it.
The Rememberable Dream: a pleasant dream stays with you clear through breakfast.

sections.title: X. Small Courtesies & Harmless Wonders
paragraphs: The Guest's Chair: the spare chair never wobbles for company.
Door's Good Morning: your door opens with a cheerful creak instead of a grim one.
The Shared Umbrella: one umbrella keeps two people mostly dry.
Festival Ribbons: ribbons tie themselves into holiday bows.
The Lantern's Wink: your window lantern dips once in answer, beloved along every coast that keeps the Answering Light.
Snow-off-the-Step: your doorstep sheds the night's snow by itself.
The Patient Gift-Wrap: wrapping paper folds without fighting you.
Coin-on-its-Edge: a coin you spin lands on its edge, delighting children and infuriating gamblers. (It decides nothing. That is the joke.)
The Birthday Flame: the candle relights once, so the littlest child may blow it out too.
Chalk-That-Stays: children's chalk drawings last until the third rain. (The Chalk Tide's oldest friend.)
The Toast's Ring: raised cups ring one clear note together.
Smoke-Shapes: your hearth-smoke curls into simple shapes for a story's sake.
The Welcome Mat's Truth: the mat lies straight, and the mud takes the hint.
The Keeping's Friend: the dawn fire you tend burns silent and low-smoked, so the house sleeps on. (Found on the first page of more waybooks than any other Way.)
The Lullaby Ember: the night-lamp dims itself to an ember-glow as the room's eyes close.
Last page intentionally blank.

title: Magic in the Islands
subtitle: Magic in the islands
summary: Small magic is woven into daily life. Greater workings ring the world’s Krysta; magic of the Third Circle and above requires a Registry Writ in Council lands.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Small magic is everywhere in daily life. Greater workings carry a different weight: magic of the Third Circle and above rings the world’s Krysta.
Four sources: arcane (the University's), divine, primal, and fae, which comes only by pact.
The Arcane Registry requires a Writ for casting of the Third Circle and above in Council lands. Its Arbiters serve by annual lot. The Concord refuses to register its casters.
The Small Ways are the hearth-magic beneath the law.

Materials: every metal and material of the old stories exists in Kalvatar, mithril and adamantine among them, but the rare ones are very rare. A mithril piece is a house heirloom or a Gold Hunter's prize, not a market good.
Prices: a charm costs 50 to 100 Anchors, a lesser working 100 to 500, a greater working 500 to 5,000, and a masterwork 500 to 5,000 Orsals. A healing draught is 50 Anchors; a greater one, 250.

title: Dress and the Five-Glance Read
subtitle: Daily life
summary: Every islander reads a stranger's sash, metal, cloth, boots, and ink without thinking. Color is the luxury in the Heartland.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The five-glance read. Every islander reads a stranger's sash, metal, cloth, boots, and ink without thinking. You should too.

The Frontier: heavy wool, leather, oiled cloth, and iron, in greys, browns, and Ironfort woad blue, because the dye is cheap and salt-stains and soot don't show. Every family knits its own pattern into the kin-knit sweaters, which is how the drowned are known.

The Heartland: silks, brocades, and fine wools. Color is the luxury: reefpurple is reserved by custom for Council seats and high clergy, and working folk wear oat-and-blue. University folk wear their copper rings.
The South: reds, oranges, golds, and earth-tones against black; light, flowing garments; abundant gold, worn as "a vote of no confidence in Goldwind"; and body-art that records lineage and deed.
The Ice: furs and hides layered deep, carved bone and ivory charms; the seam between two sheets of ice is the measure of a family's standing.
Mourning:
Undyed cloth on the Frontier.
Grey in the Heartland.
White face-paint in the south.
Soot on the brow on the ice.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Someone is buying every reefpurple dye that comes through Pearl Groove. The Council cannot find the buyer, and the Pelagar house will not say.” (heard in the Central Heartland)

title: Food of the Islands
subtitle: Daily life
summary: Saltknots, wrackcandy, fishbread, pickets, chowder-loaves, Pibcha, and Bloodbroth: what the islands eat, port by port.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Everywhere:
Saltknots: seawater-boiled bread twisted into real sailors' knots. Children learn knots by eating them: rye in the north, honey in the Heartland, redknots in the south, fatknots on the ice.
Wrackcandy: candied honeywrack. The first cut of each season is owed to the sea-pact.
Fishbread: the quick street meal; a Bit buys one.
By region:
The Frontier: salt fish and black bread, root-and-barley stew, smoked meats, hard cheese, Ironfort black ale, the Frontier Pot, and pickets, smoked-herring sticks from the quayside barrows.
The Heartland: spiced dishes and delicate sauces, Sunhold wines, chowder-loaves, coffee-houses, and the Windborne Cake, sold on the Goldwind harbor wall at dawn.

The South: saurian meat at the center of the table, from Bellowback roasts to Cluckmaw eggs; jungle fruit, river fish, peppers, Pibcha, coal-eggs, and tsoka, the shared root-beer gourd that it is an insult to refuse. Mammal-dairy is a luxury, since saurians give no milk.
The Ice: whale, seal, ice-fish, and blubber, preserved against the Long Night; Bloodbroth and crackle. A guest is given fat and fire without question.

title: Games and Pastimes
subtitle: Daily life
summary: Tidecall on every beach, the Long Pull regattas, Nine Ports in the taverns, kite-duels in Goldwind, ringstone in the south.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Tidecall: the game on every beach. Seven against seven at low water, a floating cork ball called the buoy, two posts called the marks, and no clock: it ends when the tide reaches the callstone. "The tide calls it." The knee-deep finish is last water. The great match of the year is the Charter Match in Goldwind: Armada against Hunters.
The Long Pull: gig-racing regattas.
The Peg Leg Race: sailors race the deck with one leg tied up; every long voyage has one.
Nine Ports: the tavern game of cargo tiles and bluff. Pocchin cheat.
The Frontier: the Haul, the dockers' rope-pulling contest that settles disputes between crews, and Gatehold, a board game of walls and sieges.
The Heartland: the card game Council, taught to the children of the houses; kite-duels on glass-dusted lines; and the Turning, the sunset promenade on the Goldwind harbor wall.
The South: ringstone, a hip-ball game through a high stone ring that settles village quarrels, and Swiftcrest racing at the Sunspine Run.
The Ice: the Long Throw of harpoons and seal-bone darts, the Hold, a board game of walls and captured pieces, and the Long Tell, a storytelling contest where the listeners decide what is true.
Smoke and song: Southleaf pipeweed from Southhaven, and "Bring Her Home," the shanty everyone knows.

title: Languages of the Archipelago
subtitle: Daily life
summary: Everyone speaks the Island tongue for trade; most people also speak the tongue of their own people or region.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Every character knows Common and two other languages. In Kalvatar, choose the two from the standard languages below. A rare language needs a reason in your story.

rows: Everyone in Council lands, and most of everyone else
The mainland of Assios, the old houses, the dragonborn clans
The native peoples and chant-keepers of the south
Every caravan; fast, slangy, and thick with words for value
All five kinds of elf, with five accents and one long grudge about pronunciation
The Vorthani, the goliaths, and the Tarvan's old tongue
The warrens of the Skarn's children
Galven storm-songs and Aethyn star-rolls (Auran), the Coral song (Aquan), the Cindren forge-cant (Ignan)
The Liriath, and the Courts of the Faewild
The Sporrn and the drow, and whatever else lives Below
Orka glyphs, and the old words some of the Marked keep

title: Manners Among the Peoples
subtitle: Daily life
summary: Laugh at a Pocchin's Fat Offer, never make a Vorthani repeat themselves, and never touch a Tarvan's horns.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: A Pocchin opens every deal with an outrageous Fat Offer. Laugh, spit (it's polite), and haggle down. Once a Pocchin shakes on it, the deal is iron.
A Vorthani never says a thing twice; making one repeat themselves announces you're a fool.
Never touch a Tarvan's or a Vorthani's horns.
Never read a dwarf's tally-beads uninvited. Never insult the tally.
A Galven who covers their arms is hiding something.
A Cindren who covers their glow is in mourning.
Frost Elves who paint their faces as a skull are about to raid.
A Marked door is never closed to a Marked stranger.
The sea-folk: greet them in song, give them gifts of sound, and never show them bare cold iron.

title: The Answering Light
subtitle: Customs and festivals
summary: When a ship's lantern passes at night, coastal houses dip their lamp once in reply. A coast that answers is a kind coast.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: When a ship's lantern passes at night, coastal houses dip their lamp once in reply.
A coast that answers is a kind coast.
"Not every kind coast is kind," southern captains add, passing the wreckers' cliffs of Crystalhaven.

title: The Chalk Tide
subtitle: Customs and festivals
summary: Harbor children chalk the morning's high-water line on the harbor steps; that's how they learn the moons.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Harbor children chalk the morning's high-water line on the harbor steps.
That is how they learn the moons.

One chalk line records a single morning. Seen together over time, the marks show how far the harbor water rises and falls as the moons change. Children learn to read the tides by keeping a record of the steps they use every day.

title: Door Coins
subtitle: Customs and festivals
summary: Visitors to a new home leave a copper Bit on the lintel all its first year. When the row is full, the house is paid true.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Visitors to a new home leave a copper Bit on the lintel all its first year.
When the row is full, the house is paid true.
A copper Bit on the lintel is a small contribution a visitor can make throughout the house’s first year. The row grows one visit at a time, and its completion is the sign that the house is paid true.

title: Festivals Everywhere
subtitle: Customs and festivals
summary: The Still Days and the King Tide are kept in every port in the islands.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Still Days: five days between Okram and Eo that belong to no god. Debts pause, the courts close, and every fae bargain comes due.
The King Tide: stay home, ward the door.
Restday: temple, tidecall, and the long meal, every Cycle.

title: Festivals of the Frontier
subtitle: Customs and festivals
summary: The feasts and rites of Northern Frontier.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Landing-Day, Eo 1st: solemn, then rowdy.
The Ironwake: midwinter bonfires for the garrison-dead.
First-Sail: the spring blessing of the ships, in Ezra.
Storm-Watch: every harbor-light in the north blessed and lit before the Murk, the autumn fog season, in Memnara.
The Bastion tourneys: the great martial spectacle of the north, every summer.
The Tarvan Gathering at Northreach, in the year all the clans come down together.

title: Festivals of the Heartland
subtitle: Customs and festivals
summary: The feasts and rites of Central Heartland.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Festival of Winds, in Idel: kites, regattas, and Windborne Cake.
The Founding of Goldwind.
The Merrin Games, all through Liora.
The Bounty of the Sea, in Halvenir: salting, smoking, and storing; every windowsill overflows.
The Lanterns of Unity, in Okram.
The Artisans' Faire.
The Sunhold Accord, Veriden 6th: a "friendly" rivalry no one finds friendly.

title: Festivals of the Ice
subtitle: Customs and festivals
summary: The feasts and rites of Icy Expanse.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Long Night: the famine-watch, when the lamps are kept lit in every hall.
The Return of the Sun: the joy of the first daylight.
The Ghostlight Vigil: the night of the strongest aurora, when the coast goes out on the ice to watch the lights pool below the rim of the Auroral Vault.
The whaling-feasts, after every great kill.
The Naming of the Survived.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Long Night will be early this year. The Brine Brotherhood's oil-houses are already sold for the next two winters.” (heard in the Icy Expanse)

title: Festivals of the Wilds
subtitle: Customs and festivals
summary: The feasts and rites of Southern Wilds.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Green Waking: the rains return; the great festival of the jungle's renewal.
The Night of the Ancestors: faces painted as skulls, lights on the water, and the chant-keepers reciting the lineages until dawn.
The Laughing Water: Malim's river-festival of races, music, and fish-offerings at the foot of Malim's Stair.
The Sunspine Run: Jakupur's great saurian racing meet, a festival in its own right.
The Tribute Days: offerings at the edges of the Savage Lords' territories, where joy and fear share a drumbeat.

title: First Bread
subtitle: Customs and festivals
summary: A stranger quietly pays a newcomer's first meal in a new port. You never learn who; you pay it forward.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: A stranger quietly pays a newcomer's first meal in a new port.
You never learn who. You pay it forward.

The newcomer receives a meal before they know who has made room for them in the port. Because the giver stays anonymous, the debt is paid forward when that same traveler has the chance to cover the first meal of another arrival.

title: The Mending
subtitle: Customs and festivals
summary: After a storm, the whole street mends the worst-hit roof first.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: After a storm, the whole street mends the worst-hit roof first.
"Start with the worst roof."

A storm can leave every household with work to do. By starting with the worst-hit roof, neighbors put their shared labor where it can first give someone shelter again, before turning to damage that can wait.

title: The Merrin Games
subtitle: Customs and festivals
summary: All through Liora the harbors hold twelve trials on the water. On the Untying, under the full moon of Liora 18th, a girl unties the merrin of the sailor she chooses.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: All through Liora, the Heartland harbors hold twelve trials on the water and the quay, and each winner earns a merrin: a red kerchief stitched with the port's mark, named for Merrin Dawe, the netmender's daughter who tied the first in Goldwind's first harbor years.
Liora 1st: friends trade friend-knots.
The trials include the Long Pull and the Chowder Pot, a fish stew cooked on a boat's brazier and judged by the harbor's grandmothers, said to be the hardest trial in the Heartland.
One merrin per boat; spares go to friends.

The Untying, Liora 18th, under the full Valtaire: the winners stand silent in boats dressed like peacocks, and a young woman who wants an evening on the water with one of them unties his merrin and ties it on her wrist.
The row-out stays in sight of the harbor lights, or the aunts' boat comes.
