It is not a betrothal, but untie the red, and soon you'll wed, say the harbor wives, and they claim it comes true eight times in ten. At the wedding, the merrin binds the couple's hands.

When nobody chooses: a merrin still on the bow-post at Valtaire-set is in the sea's keeping. At dawn the sailor's friends row out with bread, saltknots, and kellum for the Friends' Breakfast. Nobody sails home alone in Liora.

Where: every Heartland port, the Lower Harbor of Goldwind loudest of all; Greyhaven and Southhaven have taken it up, and the Oruma run their own on the Nine Mouths in river canoes. In Silverport, women sail for merrins too.

title: The Naming Spoon
subtitle: Customs and festivals
summary: Every child gets a carved spoon that hangs on the kitchen wall. Take yours down when you leave home.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Every child gets a carved birth-spoon that hangs on the kitchen wall.
Take yours down when you leave home; hang it back up when you return.

A child’s carved birth-spoon hangs in the kitchen until they leave home and take it down. Hanging it back in its place on return makes coming home something the household can see in an ordinary object it has known for years.

title: The Returning Cup
subtitle: Customs and festivals
summary: A sailor's cup hangs upside down while they're at sea and is turned up in the window on the day they're due home.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: A sailor's cup hangs upside down while they are at sea.
On the day they are due home it is turned up in the window, and the neighbors leave food on the step.

title: The Salt Promise
subtitle: Customs and festivals
summary: Before a long parting, two people each keep a pinch of salt from the same cellar. When they meet again, both go into the same pot.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Before a long parting, two people each keep a pinch of salt from the same cellar.
When they meet again, both go into the same pot.
"We still have salt between us" means this isn't over.

title: Sea Customs
subtitle: Customs and festivals
summary: The first drop over the rail, never whistle for wind, a Tide in your boot sailing south, and a silver Tide on the tongue of the dead.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The first drop of every bottle aboard ship goes over the rail to the sea.
Never whistle for wind. It brings too much.
A Tide in your boot when you sail south, "to pay the sea if it asks."
A silver Tide on the tongue is how the dead are buried in southern and ice-coast ports.
Never set sail on a Graveday.
Greet the sea-folk in song, any song; effort counts.
The sea-burial: on the Frontier the dead are given to the water with their name spoken once and not again.

title: The Sill
subtitle: Customs and festivals
summary: Leave what you have too much of on the windowsill; take what you need. The sill provides.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Leave what you have too much of on the windowsill; take what you need.
"The sill provides."

The sill puts a household’s surplus within reach of someone who can use it. A neighbor can take what they need without having to explain themselves at the door, and leave something of their own the next time they have extra.

title: Winter-kin
subtitle: Customs and festivals
summary: Whoever sheltered with you through a Long Night or a storm-season is kin for life. We wintered together.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Whoever sheltered with you through a Long Night or a storm-season is kin for life.
"We wintered together" means a plate and a bed for life.

Winter-kin is a tie earned by sharing shelter through a Long Night or a season of storms. Saying “We wintered together” recalls that time and carries a standing promise of a plate and a bed, even years later.

title: The Ascendant's War
subtitle: Copper remembers the siege.
summary: 105 EC: the Archmage Eldric Morvane raised a Krysta-bound mage-army and nearly took the Heartland. Out of it came the Arcane Registry.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: In 105 EC the Archmage Eldric Morvane, "the Ascendant," raised a Krysta-bound mage-army and nearly took the Heartland.
His army was halted short of Goldwind's gates by the first Grand Coalition; the Frontier garrisons held the strait against his fleets.
Out of it came the Arcane Registry and its copper rings, and the Emerald Wrath was founded as the river-guard of the south.
Goldwind's grandparents still tell the siege as a warning, and the Registry is enforced in the capital with particular zeal because of it.

title: The Battle of the Kraken's Maw
subtitle: Sixteen hours that joined the islands
summary: In 165 EC, Navy, Hunters and volunteer crews faced Blackheart’s pirate armada at the Kraken’s Maw. The victory saved the islands and left a graveyard at sea.

sections.title: More than two to one
paragraphs: Admiral Blackheart had bound the scattered pirate crews of the south under his command. He brought more than a hundred and twelve ships into the treacherous southern waters of the Kraken’s Maw. The Kalvatar Coalition, Navy and Hunters together, mustered some fifty-six.

The battle lasted sixteen hours. Its remembered story moves between great ships, individual duels and the smaller vessels that eventually joined them. The islands survived through the work of all three.

sections.title: The ships that held
paragraphs: Johann Faust’s Jubilant held the Coalition’s defense together. Titania’s Iron Swan struck through the pirate line again and again. The Crimson Tide and its crew breached and sank the colossal Gaze of Abyss, at terrible cost.

Captain Magnus of the Sledgehammer fell in a duel against Shade Serpentfang, Blackheart’s venom-bladed lieutenant. Magnus’s son Leoric took command mid-battle and fought on. Captain Falken Brightsight fought beside Admiral Thulissa from the Falkoner.

sections.title: The islands answered
paragraphs: In the darkest hour, fishing boats, merchantmen and private yachts arrived from across the archipelago. They had been hastily made into warships and were crewed by volunteers. Their arrival turned the tide.

That part of the battle belongs to people whose names are not all on the captains’ roll. A sea world answered with the vessels it had, and the crews willing to bring them into a battle already underway.

sections.title: Thulissa’s last charge
paragraphs: Admiral Thulissa of the Trident drove through the pirate fleet to the Dread Sovereign. She fought Blackheart on his deck and killed him with her trident. His armada broke; the surviving pirates fled.

She returned to her own ship, collapsed and died of her wounds. Serpentfang escaped into the night, and Sharin Bloodblade was never found. The Coalition’s victory left grief and unfinished stories alongside its relief.

sections.title: Ten years later
paragraphs: In 175 EC, the Maw remains a graveyard of wrecks worked by salvagers. Brightsight is now Fleetlord of the Last Psalm and still commands the same Falkoner. The names of Thulissa and Magnus belong to the islands’ shared account of what the victory cost.

The Armada and Hunters continue to squabble, but the Maw is a reason they will stand together when it counts. Their cooperation is written into remembered ships, surviving crews and a battle fought for the same home.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Every year on the night of the Maw, someone leaves a red-bladed knife on the reef where Blackheart fell.” (a Maw salvager)

title: The Breakwater
subtitle: Thirty-one names. One lesson.
summary: 91 EC: the one time the Armada and the Hunters fought each other in earnest. It gave the islands the Breakwater Protocols and the yearly Wargames.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Breakwater (91 EC) was the one battle between the Armada and the Hunters.
It was the second year of the Plague of the Burning Sea. A Council quarantine writ, held by the Armada, and an Easthold rescue contract, held by the Hunters, collided at Easthold's harbor mouth.
The standoff lasted two days in fog. On the second night the ebb carried a refugee ship across the line, a frightened gun crew fired, and both sides fought for an hour.
It ended when Larissa Whitewave and the Gold Hunter Odran Halloway rowed out between the lines, unarmed.
200 wounded, 31 dead. The refugees were healthy.
What it changed:
The Breakwater Protocols: when an Armada order and a Hunter contract collide, both stand down and the matter goes to the nearest Council officer.
The Wargames: every year in Veriden, joint maneuvers, convoy drills, boarding contests, and joint command. They close by reading the 31 names.
The Charter Match of Tidecall on the Goldwind sands is the friendly face of the same rivalry.

title: The Exodus and the Landing
subtitle: Fifteen years to a first shore.
summary: About 190 years ago the anti-imperial houses of Assios fled south: fifteen years of desperate crossings, guarded by the companies that became the Hunters.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: About 190 years ago (about −15 EC), after catastrophic defeats on the mainland, the great anti-imperial houses of Assios and their people made the hard choice to abandon everything and flee south, by way of Castia.
It was no overnight crossing but fifteen years of desperate evacuation, guarded by the escort-companies that became the Hunters.
The refugees came ashore on the fog-bound coasts of the Northern Frontier. Every great house in Kalvatar has, somewhere in its family, an ancestor who landed in the Frontier fog and decided to stay.
1 EC: the nobles declared the Landing complete and signed the Charter at Ironfort. The Council, the Count of years, and the Hunters were founded the same year.
Landing-Day, Eo 1st, is New Year: solemn, then rowdy.

title: The Great Slave Rebellion
subtitle: No person is cargo.
summary: About 60 EC: the enslaved of the young federation rose, and slavery was abolished in Council lands.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: In about 60 EC the enslaved of the young federation rose.
Slavery was abolished in Council lands, though it survives, illegal and stubborn, in the south to this day.
The plantations of the south were the flashpoint. The Southern Rebels trace themselves to it, and the Chainbreakers, the Reclaimers, and the Free Tide all grew out of the same grievance.
The Frontier's ports refused the slave-traders' ships for a generation afterward.

title: The Plague of the Burning Sea
subtitle: The sea carried more than sails.
summary: About 90 EC: a great maritime pestilence that swept the archipelago and scarred a generation.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: In about 90 EC a great pestilence spread from the warm, treacherous water called the Burning Sea, and swept the archipelago.
The ports closed for a season. The sea-folk of the Sunlit courts healed the sick brought to them, and the sea-pacts were renewed in gratitude.
In its second year came the Breakwater, when the Armada and the Hunters fought at Easthold.
The Charterhouse Company's first southern salt monopoly was granted in the crisis.

title: The Southern Quarantine
subtitle: Closed by Council order.
summary: 148 EC: a fever killed the colony of Fairhope and a Charter survey squadron in the far south, and the Council sealed those waters.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: In 148 EC a fever killed the colony of Fairhope and a Charter survey squadron in the far south.
The Council sealed those waters as "plague waters," and they have been closed ever since.
Southern sailors call them the Wrong Coast, and tell stories of grey ships and of the Hum.
Southern custom: a silver Tide in your boot when you sail south, "to pay the sea if it asks," and a silver Tide on the tongue of the dead.
See the Wrong Coast for what the sailors say.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Wrong Coast. The quarantined waters of the far south are "plague waters," the Council says. Southern sailors tell stories of grey ships with no names that sail without lanterns, and of the Hum: a note under hearing that you feel in the hull on calm nights. Never hum along.” (common talk)

title: Albion Tempest
subtitle: A courtblade, a quill, a different path
summary: Gold Hunter and First Mate of the Crimson Tide, Albion Tempest brings a warrior’s skill, a tinkerer’s hands and a deliberate hope for his people to the same deck.

sections.title: The path off the ice
paragraphs: Albion grew up in the Icy Expanse among the raids of the Frost Elves. A chance meeting with the Hunters gave him another path. Dedication and combat skill brought him to Gold; his tactical calm won him the First Mate’s place aboard the galleon Crimson Tide.

He serves with a purpose that reaches beyond his own advancement: to change how the islands see the Frost Elves. His people’s reputation travels ahead of them. Each act of service gives him a chance to leave a different memory behind.

sections.title: Blade and quill
paragraphs: There are two branches on Albion’s Gold Sigil. The blade is for the warrior, the quill for the administrator. On the Crimson Tide, he needs both. He has a crew to keep working on ordinary days and to lead when a fight breaks out.

Albion is a master of the elven courtblade and a practiced tinkerer. He carries tools, builds devices and traps, and makes repairs for the Hunters. The same officer who can fight in the foremost line can turn his attention to a mechanism that needs putting right.

sections.title: Mithril on a working deck
paragraphs: He wears one of the islands’ rare suits of mithril full plate and keeps regal attire for the Lodge and the deck. His straight black hair, broad Frost Elf build, amber eye and left eyepatch make a distinct figure above that armor. A scar crosses his left cheek and nose toward the patched eye.

The Crimson Tide is itself one of the names remembered from the Kraken’s Maw. Its crew breached and sank the colossal Gaze of Abyss at terrible cost. Albion’s present office belongs to a company carrying that shared history, alongside Kirith, Gorman, Hangman and Shadow.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A giant of a Frost Elf walks the ice with a hooded priest who never eats. The Hunters posted a contract on him, and Albion Tempest took it.” (a Frosthold Lodge clerk)

illustration.alt: Albion Tempest, a broad-shouldered young Frost Elf with straight jet-black hair, an intense amber eye and a left eyepatch, stands in engraved mithril plate on the deck of the Crimson Tide, his Gold blade-and-quill Sigil pinned to his black scarf.
illustration.caption: A different path. The same cold sea.

title: Johann Faust
subtitle: The Gate of the North, the deck of the Jubilant
summary: Head of House Faust and a celebrated Hunter, Johann Faust carries both a house’s obligations and a captain’s oath. At the Maw, he held the Coalition’s defense together.

illustration.alt: Johann Faust, a youthful-looking captain in his fifties with dirty-blond hair, a curled musketeer moustache and a pointed goatee, stands on the deck of the Jubilant before a northern harbor.
illustration.caption: Johann Faust aboard the Jubilant.

sections.title: Bastion and the Jubilant
paragraphs: Lord Johann Faust heads House Faust, the Gate of the North, one of the Five foremost noble houses. He rules from Bastion and commands the Jubilant as a celebrated Hunter. His authority belongs to both a house and a company at sea.
In his fifties, Johann looks younger than his years. His dirty-blond hair, curved musketeer moustache and pointed goatee make him easy to recognize at court or on deck.

Those responsibilities bring different kinds of loyalty. A house is carried by kin, inheritance and country; a Hunter’s command is carried by the order’s oath and the people serving aboard. Johann’s divided loyalty between blood and oath is the house’s most discussed private trouble.

sections.title: Holding the defense
paragraphs: At the Kraken’s Maw in 165 EC, the Jubilant was part of the Coalition of Navy and Hunters facing Blackheart’s much larger force. Johann held the Coalition’s defense together while the battle’s attacks and duels unfolded around it.

The islands remember Thulissa’s charge, the Iron Swan’s repeated attacks and the Crimson Tide’s costly victory over the Gaze of Abyss. Johann’s remembered task belongs to the line that had to hold while those chances were taken.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Johann Faust has been seen in a Greyhaven tavern with a man who wears the Last Psalm's badge. Nobody knows which side he means to take.” (heard in the Northern Frontier)

facts: Faust; the Gate of the North
Holding the Coalition’s defense at the Maw

title: Lactinius Windcaller
subtitle: The city’s favorite interruption
summary: The Hunters’ voice on the Council, Lactinius Windcaller is a beautiful platinum-blond elf, a beloved public figure and the only openly known Platinum Hunter of the Ten.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: A strikingly beautiful elf with platinum-blond hair and pointed ears. His public presence is charismatic and easy to recognize, as familiar in Goldwind as the Council seat he occupies.

sections.title: The Hunters’ seat
paragraphs: Lactinius holds the Hunters’ seat on the Council of the Charted Isles. Beside the representatives of the nobles, the Mercantile Congress, the Navy and the University, he brings the order’s knowledge of the archipelago’s dangers into the chamber.

He is charismatic, unpredictable and beloved in Goldwind. His colleagues tolerate the disruption because his knowledge is difficult to replace. The public figure has as much warmth and disorder about him as the Council’s business has procedure.

sections.title: One publicly known Platinum
paragraphs: Only ten Platinum badges can exist. Their bearers stand on a different plane from the Bronze, Silver and Gold ladder, and most keep their identities out of public view. Lactinius is the one the islands can name openly.

A Council seat and a Hunter’s Sigil describe different kinds of authority. In Lactinius they meet: the publicly known Platinum is also the person who must give the Hunters a voice among the powers that govern the charted isles.

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Lactinius brings warmth and disorder into a chamber built around procedure. He is unpredictable, and his colleagues have learned to accommodate that quality: few people can match his knowledge of the dangers beyond the harbor.

His popularity belongs to the city as much as to the Hunters. Goldwind knows his face, while the order knows the weight of the badge behind it. Those two kinds of recognition make him a particularly visible link between the people on the streets and the powers at the table.

sections.title: The Lodge and the Council
paragraphs: The Goldwind Lodge is the Hunters’ principal house. Its Contract-Master, Quartermaster and Chronicler attend to the work, equipment and recorded deeds of an order spread across the islands. Lactinius represents that wider order when the five seats meet.

Hunter work can bring a crew into the same waters as an Armada patrol. The Breakwater Protocols require conflicting naval orders and Hunter contracts to stand down before the nearest Council officer. His seat belongs in that uneasy, necessary relationship between independent crews and the navy.

sections.title: In Kalvatar
paragraphs: To understand his place in the islands, follow the path from the Council chamber to a Lodge’s contract board: public decisions at one end, a crew accepting the risk at the other. The Code binds Hunters to the client, the crew and the dead. Lactinius is the best-known face of the people who speak that oath.

title: Mother Kess
subtitle: Debts keep the harbor

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Mother Kess is the polite, matronly, terrifying head of the Fairweather Combine, which runs Varan Port.
She brokers ransoms, settles disputes, and owns everyone's debts.
She rules over three chairs:
Marcus, the vice trade.
Mira, the smuggling: the heir or the usurper, depending on whom you ask.
Elendor, the slave trade: a high elf whose family has never been seen without a white glove.
The muscle: Admiral-Retired Gerrit Haskell and his fifteen ships.
The Combine signs with a white glove.

title: Reinhardt Holst
subtitle: Corina’s weapons, his own course
summary: The youngest Gold Rank Hunter in history, sworn to drown every pirate in the archipelago.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: A strikingly handsome young man, tall and imposing, with unkempt shoulder-length black hair framing sharp, chiseled features and pale skin. His electric-blue eyes carry a cold, merciless stare. He is almost never seen without his reinforced naval officer's jacket: once the deep blue of the Armada, now dyed black in mourning for his sister, worn with the high collar turned up. His sister's sword hangs at his hip and her pistol rides in his belt.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Reinhardt was born into the ancient and prestigious House Holst, and grew up with the weight of its long military tradition in the Armada on his shoulders. The Holsts keep close ties with their branch on the continent of Assios, sharing news and resources across the strait. A child prodigy, Reinhardt joined the Armada at the age of ten, the year after Kraken's Maw, and showed an uncanny aptitude for maritime combat and organization. He also studied the arcane arts under a renowned mage, and the blend of martial and magical skill made him a formidable force.

His sister, Corina Holst, was a respected captain of the Armada and commanded the Sea Seraph. She was known for her dedication to her crew and her tactical brilliance, often leading her ship to victory against impossible odds, and she was Reinhardt's inspiration. In 170 EC, Corina and her crew faced a massive pirate fleet that was hunting a convoy of refugee cruisers. Heavily outnumbered, they held the line long enough for the refugees to escape, at the cost of their own lives. The legend of her final stand has since spread across the archipelago.

At fourteen, Reinhardt's world was shattered. Determined to avenge his sister, he demanded a rank and a ship to hunt down the pirates responsible, but his superiors refused, citing his age and their lack of trust in him. He then turned to his family, but they considered vengeance a lost cause and refused to support him. Fueled by frustration, Reinhardt gathered his most loyal comrades and pursued the pirates on his own. This act of defiance led to his disinheritance from House Holst for insubordination.

Feeling abandoned and betrayed, Reinhardt found refuge among the Hunters, an organization he had once disapproved of. He climbed through the ranks with frightening speed, and at nineteen he is the youngest Gold Rank Hunter in the organization's history, currently 17th in popularity. He is a feared figure now, with a relentless drive to eradicate every pirate in the Kalvatar Archipelago.

sections.title: Powers and abilities
list: Master of Arcane Arts: highly skilled in offensive, defensive and utility magic.
Exceptional Strategist and Tactician: a natural leader with a keen grasp of maritime combat.
Unyielding Resolve: an iron will that pushes him through the hardest challenges and inspires his comrades.
Skilled Swordsman: deadly precision with the blade.

sections.title: Equipment
list: Corina's Pistol: a beautifully crafted firearm that once belonged to his sister, and a constant reminder of his quest.
Corina's Sword: a finely made weapon, imbued with the determination of his late sister.
Hunter's Badge: the mark of his Gold Rank.
Arcane Grimoire: the spells and incantations he gathered during his studies.
Reinforced Naval Officer's Jacket: a symbol of his past and of his sister's sacrifice, and extra protection in battle.
The Retribution's Wrath: the ship he captains.

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Reinhardt is cold and calculating, with little empathy for his enemies. He is ruthless and merciless against pirates and marauders, driven by his desire for vengeance, and has no patience for weakness or treachery. Beneath the hardened exterior, he is loyal and protective of his comrades, and expects the same dedication in return. His resentment toward his family fuels his pursuit, and makes him both feared and respected among the Hunters.

The account in A Midsummer Gala shows the wit beneath that cold reputation. Reinhardt answers a host’s condescension with a bow held too long, makes gallows jokes with Hyacinth, and notices when the crowd has become too much for her. He can be patient and careful with someone in distress while remaining sharply aware of the room around them.

sections.title: Goals
list: Exact brutal revenge on every pirate and marauder in the archipelago.
Prove his worth, and prove that his family's dismissal of his cause was a grave mistake.

sections.title: In Kalvatar
paragraphs: Reinhardt is the youngest Gold Hunter; Silver Stingray is the former pirate who climbed to Gold in record time. They are different claims, and a difficult pair of reputations to carry within one order.
Corina died in 170 EC, five years after the Kraken’s Maw. Reinhardt was nine at the battle, joined the Armada at ten in 166 EC, and was fourteen when he lost her.

sections.title: A Midsummer Gala
paragraphs: At Lord Mortimer Vanris’s midsummer masquerade, Reinhardt works as paid security aboard the Floating Pavilion off Goldwind. The account follows him through a public slight, an improvised introduction to Hyacinth Alastor and a quieter conversation in the garden. His sister’s weapons and black-dyed Armada jacket remain with him even in the ballroom.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Reinhardt Holst buys a drink for every old pirate in Hollowkey and asks each of them the same question: whose colors sank the Sea Seraph?” (a Hollowkey barkeep)
Some whisper that he is only using the Hunters for his personal vendetta.

“Hyacinth Alastor and Reinhardt Holst were seen together at Lord Vanris’s Midsummer Gala. A chance conversation, they say. Of course. The drawing rooms are already wondering whether there is something more between the Rose House’s heir and the disinherited Holst.” (whispered behind a silk fan)

facts: Hunter, former Armada officer, mage and swordsman, disinherited noble
source: The Discord Roster · 175 EC; Kalvatar Library; A Midsummer Gala

epigraph.quote: You can't escape the tide of retribution. It will find you and drag you to the depths.

illustration.caption: Black for Corina. Eyes on the horizon.

title: Titania and the Iron Swan
subtitle: The Gold every rising captain must pass
summary: Eleventh in the Ranking for eight years, Titania commands the Iron Swan: a sailless metal ship, crewed by living flame, whose passage every harbor talks about.

illustration.alt: Titania sits barefoot on a harbor wall beside her smoking shoes, with the low, swan-prowed Iron Swan moored in the mist behind her.
illustration.caption: Titania at the quay, beside another pair of ruined shoes.

sections.title: A ship unlike any other
paragraphs: Every sailor has heard of the Iron Swan. Its hull is solid metal, its stacks pour black smoke and it moves against the wind without a sail. Living flame crews it. It is the only steamship in the world.

Titania is beautiful in a way that feels almost supernatural, and her presence can be unsettling. She always goes barefoot: any shoes she puts on burn. Her clothing is made of metal and the hides of animals resistant to fire.

The ship answers to Titania, a Gold Hunter. Its singular appearance belongs to the ordinary talk of the islands: something unmistakable enough that a harbor can recognize it, and extraordinary enough to keep the dockside accounts alive.

sections.title: At the top of the Golds
paragraphs: Titania stands eleventh in the Ranking, the highest of the Golds, a place she has held for eight years. For a rising Gold Hunter, her name marks the summit of that tier. The Ten occupy the separate Platinum rank above it.
At the Kraken’s Maw in 165 EC, the Iron Swan struck through the pirate line again and again. Titania’s place in the present Ranking sits beside a place in the islands’ shared memory of survival.

sections.title: A name absent from the posters
paragraphs: The Iron Swan appears on no wanted poster. No Council has dared post a price on Titania. That public fact follows her as surely as the smoke follows the ship, and leaves plenty of room for sailors to argue about what they have seen.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Nobody has ever seen the Iron Swan take on coal.” (every dockside in the islands)

Since 175 EC they hold Golgarma's Throat, the great Orka stair into the dark.
Their raids push north of Golgarma each season. The Emerald Wrath has asked for another squadron; the Council is "reviewing."
They are the Emerald Wrath's recurring nightmare, and the Wrath is theirs.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Free Tide is piracy with a creed: the sea belongs to no one.
The Last Smile, its pirate queen, whose flag is a pale grinning crescent on black, is gathering the remnants of Blackheart's armada into something like a pirate nation, and people follow her gladly.

Her flagship is said to be a Krysta-forged monster carrying a weapon called the Drowning Star that can erase a port. Some old sailors swear it is Blackheart's own Dread Sovereign, raised from the Maw, which is impossible, they admit, and keep swearing anyway.
Harrow Mane leads the wolf-pack crews too brutal even for the Last Smile.
The Remnants of Blackheart are the crews who survived the Maw.
Hollowkey is the greatest of the Pirate Freeholds, a drift-market where no Council flag flies.

subtitle: Outlaws of the islands
summary: Captain of The Wind Dancer. Bounty: 900 Anchors.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Siroc the Swift, captain of The Wind Dancer, is on the Council's Most Wanted poster for 900 Anchors.
What the docks say:
He can outrun the wind and vanish into thin air.
He carries an ancient elven artifact that commands the winds.
He has escaped the armada more than a dozen times.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Siroc the Swift: he can outrun the wind and vanish into thin air.” (the docks, about the Most Wanted)
“Siroc the Swift: he carries an ancient elven artifact that commands the winds.” (the docks, about the Most Wanted)
“Siroc the Swift: he has escaped the Armada more than a dozen times.” (the docks, about the Most Wanted)

title: The Southern Movements
subtitle: Outlaws of the islands
summary: The Southern Rebels, the Reclaimers, and the Chainbreakers: freedom-fighters or criminals, depending on who you ask.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Southern Rebels: the broad uprising of the south, heirs of the Great Slave Rebellion.
The Reclaimers: they want the south back, and invoke Yaxqel, the First Walker.
The Chainbreakers: they free the enslaved, and are not universally villains.
The Verdant Pact: the green militants who defend the Wilds' oldest country with their lives.
Depending on who you ask, they are freedom-fighters or criminals.

illustration.alt: Dockworkers argue beside rival broadsides as a patrol enters the harbor street at dawn.
illustration.caption: Dockworkers argue beside rival broadsides as a patrol enters the harbor street at dawn.

title: Theodora Nightshade
subtitle: Outlaws of the islands
summary: Captain of The Nightingale. Bounty: 650 Anchors.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Theodora Nightshade, captain of The Nightingale, is on the Council's Most Wanted poster for 650 Anchors.
What the docks say:
She keeps a collection of every poison in the islands.
She has slipped in and out of the reckoners' hall.
No lock has ever held her.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Theodora Nightshade: she keeps a collection of every poison in the islands.” (the docks, about the Most Wanted)
“Theodora Nightshade: she has slipped in and out of the Reckoners' Hall.” (the docks, about the Most Wanted)
“Theodora Nightshade: no lock has ever held her.” (the docks, about the Most Wanted)

title: The Undertow
subtitle: Outlaws of the islands
summary: Not a gang but a current: the smugglers' web that moves what the harbors won't. Find it by the turned hook and ask for Aunt Brine.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: The Undertow is not a gang. It is a current: the smugglers' web that moves what the harbors won't. Everyone has a cousin who knows someone.
How to find it: look for the turned hook, a fishhook carved point-up, and ask for "Aunt Brine."
The Code. Break it and you are cut loose:
No business at a dawn fire.
No paper.
A struck deal holds.
Nothing to the Inquisition.
Don't drown the harbor.
The cant:
Dark glass: unregistered Krysta.
Wet goods: cargo that came out of the sea.
The Bell: the law.
A long tide: prison.
Stone, ink, and brass rings: forged stamps, marques, and licenses.
Drowned Anchors: counterfeit coin.
Bright work: casting of the Third Circle or higher without a Writ.
Paying salt: a bribe.
Ghost-cargo: goods that were never aboard.
The outfits everyone has heard of:
The Fogrunners of Black Harbor, under Wenna Hollis, "the Bellmistress," who talk in bell-codes through the Murk.
The Tollmen on the sea-road, under Brann Fessick, "the Tollmaster."
The Skein, the brokers of secrets.
The Ringless, the unregistered casters, and "the Tutor."
The Ledger Wolves, under Dagny Sorrel, "the Interest."
The Mint-in-the-Mire, the Duskmire coiners, under the gnome Ottar Glimm.
The Gilt Hands, harbor pickpockets, under the halfling Old Pell.
The Crest Syndicate of the Sunspine Run, under Teshka Orrin, "the Odds-Mother."
The Ninth Shovel, the looters of Zal'Kareth, under Half-Hand Dorrin.
The Blackleaf Runners, under Lumai Okonja, "Sister Smoke."
The Fairweather Combine of Varan Port, under Mother Kess.
The False Lights, the Crystalhaven wreckers, under Granny Ylva Skerrow. "Not every kind coast is kind."
The Quiet Auction, the floating black market of the sea.
Glint, Krysta-dust snuff, costs 2 Tides a pinch. A forged stamp costs 50 Anchors, and a forged marque 300.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “A blackened copper Bit on a dead man's tongue means one thing in the Undertow: don't ask.” (heard in the Central Heartland)
“The Undertow: the smuggler's web that moves what the harbors won't. Everyone has a cousin who knows someone.” (common talk)
“Captain Umbrel: he stole an invisible cloak from the Skein.” (the docks, about the Most Wanted)

illustration.alt: Smugglers pass a crate beneath a busy harbor pier.
illustration.caption: Smugglers pass a crate beneath a busy harbor pier.

title: Halsof Varselis
subtitle: The Even Hand at the Council
summary: The Nobles' seat on the Council: young, ambitious, calculating, and often colder than he is.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Halsof Varselis holds the Nobles' seat on the Council of the Charted Isles.

He is the heir of House Varselis, the Even Hand, whose head is his father, old Lord Linus Varhall Varselis. The house is the closest thing the peerage has to a conscience, and the chief lawful check on Vol Kaern's ambition.
At the Council table he is young, serious, and calculating, and he often seems colder than he is.

sections.title: The inheritance of the Even Hand
paragraphs: House Varselis rules from the Hall of Scales in the Central Heartland. Its silver scales stand over an open book on grey-blue, and its motto is “Weighed, Not Wagered.” Law, justice and balance are the family’s public commitments.

Lord Linus remains the head of the house. Halsof is both his heir and the peerage’s voice on the Council, carrying responsibilities that already reach beyond the succession. Varselis is closely allied with the University and stands as the chief lawful check on House Vol Kaern’s ambition.

sections.title: Family and allies
paragraphs: Lady Octavia Varselis works to keep the noble families from one another’s throats. Julius, a wizard devoted to knowledge, forms a bridge to the University. Calista is a gifted negotiator; Aelius commands the house guard and defends its interests when words run out.

Halsof’s Council seat therefore rests within a working family, with diplomacy, scholarship and armed protection all supporting the house’s position. The Nobles’ representative speaks for a peerage whose members do not share one interest.

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: He is young, ambitious, serious and calculating. He often appears colder than he is, and the weight of representing the nobility falls on him in a fracturing age.

The open question is what he will make of his father’s principles. The Even Hand has a reputation worth protecting; Halsof must decide how to carry it through a political world that rewards pressure, obligation and compromise.

sections.title: In Kalvatar
paragraphs: His name connects a Council vote to the Hall of Scales, the University alliance and the ambitions of the great houses. These are the places to look for the stakes behind his measured public manner: who asks the law for protection, who asks it for permission, and which request reaches the nobles’ seat.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Halsof Varselis has been asked to take the Five's chair, and he has said no three times. The fourth time he may say yes.” (heard in Goldwind)

illustration.alt: Halsof Varselis in a burgundy coat reviews an open petition in the Hall of Scales beneath his house’s silver scales and open-book emblem.
illustration.caption: The weight behind a measured answer.

title: Horace Goldspire
subtitle: A flag on the Spire Floor
summary: The Mercantile Congress's seat on the Council: pompous, ostentatious, and indispensable.

sections.title: The Congress’s voice
paragraphs: On Coinsday, the great merchant families of Goldwind announce what a sack of grain or a barrel of oil will fetch. When those families need to be heard in the Council, the Mercantile Congress sends Horace Goldspire.
He is pompous and ostentatious, and the other seats find him indispensable, which annoys them more than anything else about him.
His family, the Goldspires, own the Goldspire Exchange and hold one of the Twelve Flags on the Spire Floor, where the board-prices are called every Coinsday.

sections.title: The Exchange and the Twelve Flags
paragraphs: The Goldspires own the Exchange, whose Spire Floor gives the great merchant families their public stage. Every Coinsday, the Twelve Flags call the board-prices of goods such as coffee, salt, oil and grain. A flag-post requires a bond of 1,000 Orsals and twenty years on the floor, and passes only within a family.

Goldspire’s flag is a gold spire on cobalt, ringed by twelve small gold stars. “The Price Is the Truth” is the family motto. Wine and luxury imports form part of its trade, and the Tallis vintners of Sunhold bring their wine to market under the Goldspire seal.

sections.title: Family and succession
paragraphs: His daughter and heir, Celestine Goldspire, runs the floor. Dry, tired and exceptionally good with numbers, she carries the Exchange’s daily work while her father carries the family’s voice into public affairs.

Horace’s late wife belonged to House Veldane. His family’s reach also includes sworn and indebted connections: the expedition patrons of House Wingate, the Pellow price-criers and House Zane. The Goldspire name is a network as well as a flag.

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Horace likes his wealth to be seen and can be generous with it. His Council colleagues may find him exhausting. They still need the man who can tell them what the merchants on the Spire Floor will live with.

sections.title: Political weight
paragraphs: The Congress is a collective of guilds, each with its own work and interests. Its banking guild, the Reckoners’ Hall, holds deposits, makes loans and insures cargoes under First Reckoner Maera Blackstrand. Horace’s public seat is one part of that larger commercial structure.

sections.title: From cargo to Council
paragraphs: A cargo of Sunhold grain can make its way from a ship’s hold to a price call on the Spire Floor. A dispute over that cargo can make its way to the Council. Celestine runs the floor where the price is called. Horace is the man in the chamber who hears about it.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Horace Goldspire has never worn the same coat to the Council twice, and he has never once been late with a vote.” (a Goldwind tailor)

facts: The Mercantile Congress, on the Council

illustration.alt: Merchant Lord Horace Goldspire gestures from an Exchange gallery toward a busy trading floor, wearing his ochre brocade waistcoat.
illustration.caption: A voice above the Spire Floor.

title: Arios and Alina Fafner
subtitle: One seat, two voices
summary: The Navy's seat on the Council belongs to Arios Fafner. His daughter Alina sits in it, and has begun to speak for herself.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Arios Fafner holds the Navy's seat on the Council of the Charted Isles, and rarely attends in person.
His daughter, Alina Fafner, sits in his stead. She carries his views on security and defense, and lately she has begun to bring her own.

sections.title: The work of the seat
paragraphs: Security and defense reach the Council through the Navy’s representative. Across an archipelago, those concerns travel with ships: protected passages, convoy routes, port defenses and the consequences of closing a stretch of water.

Arios holds the seat, while Alina does its regular work in the chamber. The arrangement places a daughter’s judgment alongside the views she has been entrusted to carry. Her interventions are beginning to have a voice of their own.

sections.title: The Council and the Admiralty
paragraphs: The Council governs under the Charter from Goldwind. The Armada’s operational command rests with Grand Admiral Kalivos Durant and the Admiralty, with nine Fleetlords responsible for their own fleets and waters. The Fafners’ seat brings naval concerns into the five-way political debate.

The other representatives answer to the nobles, Hunters, Congress and University. A defense question at their table also touches trade, licensed scholarship, noble obligations and the independent crews who cross the same sea.

sections.title: A history behind the arguments
paragraphs: The Breakwater remains part of the relationship between navy and Hunters. In 91 EC, a quarantine writ and a rescue contract collided in fog; thirty-one people died. The resulting protocols require conflicting orders and contracts to stand down before the nearest Council officer.

Alina’s brief on security and defense sits within a setting where protection has a human cost and different duties can collide. The protocols, the Armada and the Hunters’ Code give that debate a history beyond the chamber.

sections.title: In Kalvatar
paragraphs: Arios and Alina share an entry because they share the public story of this seat. One holds it; the other is becoming its familiar voice. Read their place in the Council alongside the Nine Fleets and the Breakwater to see the institutions and consequences behind that change.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Alina Fafner asked the Admiralty for the Breakwater files. All of them.” (an Admiralty copy-clerk)

illustration.alt: Alina Fafner studies an unlettered harbor-defense chart in a lamplit Admiralty office, wearing the white coat seen at the Council.
illustration.caption: One seat. A voice becoming her own.

title: Thessaly Kane
subtitle: The University’s voice at the table
summary: Head of the University of Kalvatar and its seat on the Council, who succeeded her father, Thobias Kane.

sections.title: The University’s seat
paragraphs: When the University of Kalvatar has business before the Council, Thessaly Kane speaks for it. She took both the Council seat and the headship of the University from her father, Thobias.
She succeeded her father, Thobias Kane. The old headmaster, retired, still advises her from his library, and the Council still asks him what she thinks.
Every licensed mage of the University wears its copper ring.

sections.title: The institution she leads
paragraphs: The University is the archipelago’s oldest and largest school of the arcane. Its copper-ringed spires rise over Goldwind’s banking quarter, and its archives preserve more old charts than the Chartwrights’ own.

Its two great schools are the Goldwind Academy, devoted to maritime science, commerce and the arts, and the Sylariel Institute of Arcane Studies. Thessaly leads an institution whose work extends from a navigator’s calculations to licensed arcane practice.

sections.title: Copper rings and public authority
paragraphs: The University keeps the Arcane Registry and its copper rings. In Goldwind, scholarship and casting meet a closely regulated public life; the ring connects a mage to that system of instruction and license.

At the Council, Thessaly gives the University a voice beside the nobles, Hunters, Congress and Navy. The institution’s knowledge is part of the government of the charted isles, as well as the work of its classrooms and archives.

sections.title: A succession still in the room
paragraphs: Thobias retired to his library, where he still advises his daughter. His old colleagues still ask him what she thinks. Thessaly has the office now. Some of the people who want an answer from it are still accustomed to knocking on his door.

Thessaly now holds both the headship and the Council seat. Her story at the table is bound to that overlap: a present responsibility, a well-known predecessor and an institution accustomed to the Kane name.

sections.title: Through the University doors
paragraphs: In Goldwind, a person might come to the University for practical training at the Academy, to study the arcane at the Institute, or to trace a course on an old chart in the archives. A mage seeking a copper ring comes for a different reason. Thessaly answers for all of that work when the Council has questions.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Old Thobias answers letters addressed to his daughter, and she lets him. It saves her the time.” (a University porter)

facts: Head of the University of Kalvatar

illustration.alt: Thessaly Kane, in teal academic layers with a copper ring, checks a book in a quiet University library while a student waits beside her.
illustration.caption: The University’s answer comes from her.

title: Maera Blackstrand
subtitle: All accounts come due
summary: First Reckoner of the Reckoners' Hall and head of House Blackstrand, who holds half the islands' debts.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: A merchant who needs a loan or wants to insure a cargo can turn to the Reckoners’ Hall, the bank of the Mercantile Congress. Its First Reckoner is Lady Maera Blackstrand. She also heads House Blackstrand, the Ledger’s Lord.
Horace Goldspire has the Congress's chair on the Council. Everyone knows the real power of the Congress is the Hall, and that the Hall is Maera Blackstrand.
She holds half the islands' debts. The house motto is All Accounts Come Due.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Maera Blackstrand reads every ledger in the Hall herself. The clerks say she has never had to read one twice.” (a junior reckoner)

title: Imelda Roque
subtitle: The Lady of Writs
summary: Governor of the Charterhouse Company, "the Lady of Writs," whose brass-collars keep its monopolies.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Imelda Roque is the Governor of the Charterhouse Company, the Council-chartered trading company that stands outside the guilds. The docks call her the Lady of Writs.
The Company holds the southern salt monopoly, the Verdayan jade concession, and the indenture contracts, and keeps company towns of its own. Its writ-men are the brass-collars.
When the Company won the southern salt monopoly, two ports rioted, and the brass-collars "restored order."

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Lady of Writs signs in green ink, so the brass-collars know which orders are really hers.” (a Southhaven longshoreman)

title: Morgha Wall-Holder
subtitle: The Longshore sets the pace
summary: Boss of the Longshore, the dockers' guild, on the wharves of Goldwind.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Morgha Wall-Holder runs the Longshore in Goldwind: the dockers' guild of the Mercantile Congress, and the people who decide how fast anything is unloaded.
Captains who want their cargo ashore before it spoils learn her name early, and learn to say it politely.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Nothing leaves Goldwind's wharves on a strike day. Not even the tide, if Morgha Wall-Holder says so.” (a Goldwind harbor-pilot)

title: Grand Dame Ottilie Veldane
subtitle: Kin to all, kept by none
summary: The matriarch at the center of House Veldane's Marriage-Web: every betrothal in the Heartland crosses her table.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Grand Dame Ottilie Veldane is the matriarch of House Veldane, the Marriage-Web, whose motto is Kin to All, Kept by None.
Every betrothal in the Heartland crosses her table, and she arranges half the weddings in it. Lady Mirabel Veldane heads the house; the Grand Dame decides who marries into it, and who marries out.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Grand Dame Ottilie keeps a book of every child born to a great house, and beside each name, the year she expects them to marry.” (a Veldane governess)

title: Sunward Alesse Brightwater
subtitle: Sunward over a sea of prayers
summary: Head of the Concord of the Risen Sun and the Deep Tide, beside the Tidecaller Ondrel Greywake.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Sunward Alesse Brightwater leads the Concord of the Risen Sun and the Deep Tide, the civic faith of Piety, Harmony, and Justice, beside the Tidecaller Ondrel Greywake.

The Concord holds no seat on the Council and needs none: nearly everyone prays at its temples. Under the Sunward it still refuses to register its casters with the Arcane Registry, and everyone pretends not to notice the standoff.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Sunward walks the Goldwind quays at dawn every Sunsdawn and blesses whatever boat is nearest, honest or not.” (a Goldwind net-mender)

title: Tidecaller Ondrel Greywake
subtitle: Thirty years reading the moons
summary: The Tidecaller of the Concord: an old sea-priest of Easthold who read the moons for the Last Psalm for thirty years.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Tidecaller Ondrel Greywake leads the Concord beside the Sunward Alesse Brightwater.

He is an old sea-priest of Easthold, and for thirty years he read the moons aboard the ships of the Last Psalm, the Concord's fleet. Tidecallers bless the fleets, read the moons, and broker the sea-pacts, and every Tidecaller in the islands learned the moons from someone he taught.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Ondrel Greywake has named the week of the next King Tide twice, and changed his mind both times.” (a Tidecaller novice)

facts: Thirty years with the Last Psalm

title: Grand Admiral Kalivos Durant
subtitle: The Anvil at the heart of the fleet
summary: Lord of the Nine Fleets and Fleetlord of the Iron Wall: Kalivos Durant commands the Armada from the Conqueror, with the capital behind him and an archipelago before him.

sections.title: The capital’s shield
paragraphs: Kalivos Durant commands the Armada and retains direct command of its First Fleet. That fleet, the Iron Wall, guards Goldwind and the Central Heartland. Together with Dastan Graylock’s Iron Blockade in the northern strait, it forms the Twin Irons. One shields the capital. The other keeps watch against the Korvan Imperium.

His flag flies from the Conqueror, one of the nine Executioner-class men-of-war ever built. Zophiel is its First Blade, the second-in-command who leads its boarding actions. Even the Armada’s greatest command still depends on the officers and hands of a particular ship.

sections.title: Four kinds of responsibility
paragraphs: The orders may come from Kalivos, but the ships need somewhere to take on supplies, shelter and put men ashore. Edran Holst oversees the ports and fortifications. Brigid Thane leads the Armada’s fighting line, and Serane Marr, his second in command, leads the Ivory Command.

Kalivos’s title spans all nine fleets, whose duties reach from river patrols to polar waters. Keeping the First does not make the others interchangeable. The Anvil’s command is the point where their different obligations must be held together.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Grand Admiral has never raised his voice in the Admiralty. He has never needed to.” (a White Coat aide)

facts: Grand Admiral, Lord of the Nine Fleets

illustration.alt: Grand Admiral Kalivos Durant watches the fleet from the quarterdeck of the Conqueror, in his dark navy coat with ivory collar and gold braid.
illustration.caption: Nine fleets. One order.

gallery.alt: Brigid Thane, Serane Marr, Kalivos Durant and Edran Holst confer over the Admiralty's sea chart, with the fifth chair visibly empty.
gallery.caption: Four voices. Five chairs.
gallery.label: The High Command

title: Lady High Marshal Serane Marr
subtitle: The war before the first broadside
summary: Second in the Armada and First of the Ivory Command, Serane Marr works where charts, diplomacy and the movement of fleets become a plan.

sections.title: The Ivory Command
paragraphs: Lady High Marshal Serane Marr answers only to the Grand Admiral in the Armada’s command. She is First of the Ivory Command, the White Coats: a largely noble, strategic and diplomatic branch whose officers are bound to no single fleet.

Their creed is “Wisdom Guides, Power Follows.” Serane’s place in High Command gives that creed a practical weight. A fleet must know where it is going, what it is meant to achieve, and what its orders will cost the other ships needed elsewhere.

sections.title: Across the chart table
paragraphs: When the Admiralty plans a war, it does so in Serane’s rooms. A proposed move has to make sense to Kalivos Durant in overall command, to Brigid Thane with the Cerulean Vanguard, and to Edran Holst at the stations and harbor defenses. Serane’s work takes her across all three commands.

An officer becomes a White Coat at the Ivory Investiture. If you bring a warning or a disputed order before the Admiralty, the white tells you what sort of work that officer does. Read the rank to see what they can do about your problem.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Serane Marr has a chart of every harbor in the islands on the walls of her study, and a pin in every one she would take first.” (a White Coat cadet)

facts: First of the Ivory Command (White Coats)

illustration.alt: Silver-haired Lady High Marshal Serane Marr, with warm olive skin, plans an operation by lamplight in her ivory officer's coat.
illustration.caption: Before the first sail rises.

gallery.alt: Brigid Thane, Serane Marr, Kalivos Durant and Edran Holst confer over the Admiralty's sea chart, with the fifth chair visibly empty.
gallery.caption: Four voices. Five chairs.
gallery.label: The High Command

title: Storm Marshal Brigid Thane
subtitle: Where the blue line holds
summary: Storm Marshal Brigid Thane leads the Cerulean Vanguard, the Armada’s fighting line: the Blue Coats who must carry a plan through shot, spray and a boarding rail.

sections.title: The Cerulean Vanguard
paragraphs: Brigid Thane is the senior officer of the Cerulean Vanguard and its voice in High Command. The Blue Coats are the Armada’s fighting line, and their creed is “In Valor, We Stand.” Their branch is entered through the Cerulean Trials.

Her office connects the Admiralty’s plans to the people who fight them. Serane Marr leads the strategic work of the Ivory Command; Brigid’s responsibility lies with the line expected to hold when those plans meet an enemy.

sections.title: Earning the blue
paragraphs: A recruit starts in grey. Earning a blue coat means passing the Cerulean Trials, and aboard ship there’s still a watch to keep and a chain of command to learn. The Sword-Lieutenant keeps the watch, the Master of Thunder commands the guns, and when it’s time to board, the First Blade leads.

Blue Coats returning from the Trials say they would rather face the sea than Brigid’s inspections. The story belongs beside her office: in a branch built around courage, readiness is what makes courage useful.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Brigid Thane boarded a pirate sloop alone with a boathook and came back with its colors and its cook.” (a Blue Coat bosun)

facts: Senior of the Cerulean Vanguard (Blue Coats)

illustration.alt: Storm Marshal Brigid Thane, auburn braid flying and cobalt coat caught by the wind, supervises a warship's crew through a rain squall.
illustration.caption: Stand your watch.

gallery.alt: Brigid Thane, Serane Marr, Kalivos Durant and Edran Holst confer over the Admiralty's sea chart, with the fifth chair visibly empty.
gallery.caption: Four voices. Five chairs.
gallery.label: The High Command

title: Lord Castellan Edran Holst
subtitle: The strength behind the harbor chain
summary: Master of the Armada’s ports, stations and fortifications, Edran Holst holds the shoreward half of a navy’s power.

sections.title: The shoreward command
paragraphs: Lord Castellan Edran Holst sits on High Command as master of the Armada’s ports, stations and fortifications. Harbor chains, signal towers and naval docks answer to his office. His charge is the network of fixed places from which the fleets can act.

A warship can leave a station; the station must remain. Its defenses, signals and harbor watch are part of the same naval system as the ships offshore. The title Lord Castellan places that work at the Admiralty’s table.

sections.title: Order Before Mercy
paragraphs: His house is Holst, keeper of the customs-codes, whose motto is “Order Before Mercy.” It is a fitting name to encounter where a harbor’s law becomes a chain across its mouth.

Within the Armada, a Castellan commands a fortress or naval station, while a Wardmaster is charged with a port’s defenses and harbor watch. Edran’s wider office binds those shoreward responsibilities into the High Command’s work.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Every harbor-chain from Ironfort to Frosthold was hung on the Lord Castellan's order, and he keeps the keys to most of them.” (a Frosthold chain-warden)

illustration.alt: Lord Castellan Edran Holst inspects a fortified harbor-chain mechanism with his keys and a rolled plan, in a practical dark slate coat.
illustration.caption: The chain holds.

gallery.alt: Brigid Thane, Serane Marr, Kalivos Durant and Edran Holst confer over the Admiralty's sea chart, with the fifth chair visibly empty.
gallery.caption: Four voices. Five chairs.
gallery.label: The High Command

title: The Shroud
subtitle: The empty chair
summary: The fifth chair of the Armada's High Command is officially empty. The docks say someone called the Shroud sits in it.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: The Armada's High Command has a chair that is officially empty.
The docks say it is not. They call whoever sits in it the Shroud, and they say it quietly. Nobody who has served in the Admiralty will say the name at all.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “There are five chairs in the Admiralty and four admirals. Nobody dusts the fifth, and it is never dusty.” (an Admiralty cleaner)

facts: The empty chair of the High Command

illustration.alt: The fifth command chair stands empty beside the Admiralty's chart table at night, with no figure or identity depicted.
illustration.caption: The fifth place is kept.

gallery.alt: Brigid Thane, Serane Marr, Kalivos Durant and Edran Holst confer over the Admiralty's sea chart, with the fifth chair visibly empty.
gallery.caption: Four voices. Five chairs.
gallery.label: The High Command

title: Dastan Graylock
subtitle: Maverick at the northern gate
summary: From the Charter’s Oath, Dastan Graylock commands the Iron Blockade: the northern watch against the Korvan Imperium and one half of the Twin Irons.

sections.title: The strait and the Crown Route
paragraphs: Fleetlord Dastan Graylock commands the Second Fleet, the Iron Blockade. Its charge is the northern strait and the interdiction of the Crown Route. The Korvan Imperium lies beyond that watch; the islands lie behind it.

The fleets call him Maverick. His flagship is the Charter’s Oath, an Executioner-class man-of-war. The Iron Blockade’s work also belongs to the Interdictor cruisers built for blockade and area denial: ships designed to make passage a question of naval power.

sections.title: The Twin Irons
paragraphs: The Second and Kalivos Durant’s First Fleet share the name Twin Irons. The Iron Wall protects Goldwind and the Heartland; the Iron Blockade keeps the northern approach. Their names describe two linked duties along the same sea-road.

Dastan’s place in the Armada is easiest to understand from that strait. Exploration, rescue and distant expeditions have other Fleetlords. His fleet’s task is to hold the approach through which the Imperium would have to come.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Maverick has turned back three imperial envoys at the strait without reading their letters. The Council has asked him to read the fourth.” (an Ironfort customs-man)

illustration.alt: Dastan Graylock keeps watch over the northern strait from a fog-bound harbor tower, with the Charter's Oath beyond the window.
illustration.caption: The strait stays closed.

title: Falken Brightsight
subtitle: The Psalmist and the ship that remembers
summary: A veteran of the Kraken’s Maw, Falken Brightsight still commands from the Falkoner. His Last Psalm carries the Armada’s obligations to the sea-pacts and the Coral Kingdoms.

sections.title: A Tidecaller on every hull
paragraphs: Falken Brightsight, the Psalmist, is Fleetlord of the Third Fleet, the Last Psalm. It is the Concord’s fleet, charged with enforcing the sea-pacts and maintaining relations with the Coral Kingdoms. Every hull carries a Tidecaller.

Those priests bless sailings and broker the pacts between the peoples above and below the water. Their presence makes the Last Psalm a fleet whose duties include keeping promises as well as bringing force to bear. It is blessed and feared in equal measure.

sections.title: The Falkoner at the Maw
paragraphs: In 165 EC, Brightsight was captain of the Falkoner and fought beside Admiral Thulissa at the Kraken’s Maw. The Coalition survived; Thulissa did not. Ten years later he is a Fleetlord, still flying his flag from the ship he commanded that day.

The Armada has nine Executioners, but its Fleetlords do not all command from one. Brightsight’s Falkoner is the clearest reminder that a flagship’s place in the islands’ memory can matter as much as its class.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Psalmist hangs the Falkoner's Maw-scarred plank in his cabin, and every captain he promotes has to touch it.” (a Last Psalm Hand)

illustration.alt: Falken Brightsight listens to a sea-court envoy at the Falkoner's embarkation steps, receiving a mother-of-pearl token beside a sea-pact bell.
illustration.caption: The oath travels both ways.

title: Zeras Durant
subtitle: The Breaker beyond the home waters
summary: Zeras Durant commands the Spearfall from the Spearhead: the expeditionary fleet sent wherever the Council directs the Armada’s offensive strength.

sections.title: Where the Council points
paragraphs: Zeras Durant is Fleetlord of the Fourth Fleet, the Spearfall, and is known as the Breaker. His ship is the Spearhead. The Fourth’s charge is expeditionary offense, wherever the Council points.

Other fleets are identified with a stretch of sea, a northern strait or the rivers of the south. The Spearfall is identified with a task. Its place on the chart follows the Council’s decision to send it.

sections.title: One fleet in a wider command
paragraphs: That outward charge places Zeras within a larger division of labor. Kalivos Durant’s Iron Wall guards the capital, while the Spearfall carries offensive force beyond those home waters. Both answer to the Armada’s command and the Council whose navy it is.

The arrival of the Spearfall makes a Council decision visible offshore. For the islands receiving it, the Breaker’s command means that the navy’s offensive strength has been directed toward their waters.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Spearfall is always somewhere else. That's the point of the Spearfall.” (a Spearhead gunner)

title: Enara Torraflame
subtitle: One more aboard the Intervention
summary: Called the Undrowned, Enara Torraflame leads the Killing Tide into crises: rescue, evacuation and the dangers that surface from the deep.

sections.title: When something surfaces
paragraphs: Enara Torraflame is Fleetlord of the Fifth Fleet, the Killing Tide. Its charge is intervention: crisis, rescue and evacuation, and above all what rises from the deep. When something surfaces, the Killing Tide answers.

Her ship is the Intervention. Haldan Flint serves as its First Blade, second-in-command and leader of its boarding actions. The fleet’s work places fighting and rescue within the same command; driving a danger back and getting people away from it can belong to the same emergency.

sections.title: The Torraflame rivalry
paragraphs: The fleets call Enara the Undrowned. The name has gathered its own dockside explanations, but her public charge is plain: the Fifth is the fleet that answers when a situation has already become urgent.

Her cousin Hoskelis Torraflame commands the Warsprite. They have competed at everything since childhood, and the Killing Tide keeps a book on it. Among fleet titles and orders, their rivalry gives the sailors something considerably more personal to follow.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “They call her the Undrowned because she went over the side at Mirrormere in a gale and climbed back aboard on the other side of the ship.” (a Killing Tide Hand)

illustration.alt: Enara Torraflame steadies an adult evacuee boarding the Intervention at blue hour after a squall.
illustration.caption: One more aboard.

title: Uha Farsight
subtitle: The Seeker beyond the chart’s edge
summary: Smiling Uha commands the Far Watch, the Sixth Fleet: exploration and naval cartography in partnership with the Chartwrights.

sections.title: The fleet that draws the map
paragraphs: Fleetlord Uha Farsight commands the Far Watch from the Seeker. The Sixth works with the Chartwrights on exploration and naval cartography. Its contribution to the Armada begins with knowing where ships can go.

The islands are too numerous for anyone to know their true count. A verified passage or a newly surveyed island can change a route that other sailors depend upon. The Far Watch’s place in the nine fleets is tied to that continuing work of discovery.

sections.title: Smiling Uha
paragraphs: Uha is a Black Coat, of the Ebon Blade, as well as a Fleetlord. A coat marks a branch; a fleet command marks an office. The Far Watch makes both titles visible in the same officer.

It famously flies no Executioner. Sailors have turned that fact into their favorite account of its commander: Smiling Uha needs no Executioner, they say, because she is one. It is a dockside judgment of a formidable reputation.

title: Zyanya Greymoor
subtitle: Gunboats beneath the green
summary: The Jaguar commands the Emerald Wrath from the Jadefang, taking the Armada into the rivers and along the coasts of the Southern Wilds.

sections.title: The riverward fleet
paragraphs: Fleetlord Zyanya Greymoor commands the Seventh Fleet, the Emerald Wrath. Its waters are the rivers and coasts of the Southern Wilds, its emblematic work the gunboats moving through the green. The Justicar river gunboat is its workhorse.

Her ship is the Jadefang and her fleet-name is the Jaguar. Against the Crimson Legion’s raids, the Emerald Wrath is the Armada’s southern presence. Here the work of a navy reaches inland, along waterways through the islands’ largest land.

sections.title: The Fair Hand of the South
paragraphs: Her house is Greymoor, the Fair Hand of the South. Her naval charge and her house’s country meet in the same region, where the Council’s authority must contend with powers and loyalties of its own.

With Legion raids pushing north of Golgarma in 175 EC, Zyanya has asked the Council for another squadron. The Council is reviewing the request. For the Seventh, that distance between a request and an answer is measured in the waters it must continue to patrol.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Jaguar sleeps in her boots on the Jadefang's deck in the rains, so she's first to the guns.” (a Justicar helmsman)

title: Runa Kaldmark
subtitle: The Vow does not thaw
summary: Frostbite holds the Armada’s far southern watch. From the Rimeheart, Runa Kaldmark commands a Frozen Vow stretched thin across the Icy Expanse.

sections.title: The last oath at the world’s edge
paragraphs: Runa Kaldmark is Fleetlord of the Eighth Fleet, the Frozen Vow, and is known as Frostbite. Her ship is the Rimeheart. The Eighth keeps the Icy Expanse, far south of the Heartland and the Admiralty’s center of power.
The fleet is stretched thin and remains unbroken. “The Vow does not thaw” is its own account of itself: a promise of endurance in waters where weather and distance already ask much of any ship.

sections.title: We Outlast
paragraphs: “We Outlast” is the motto of House Kaldmark, the Cold Hold. It suits its Fleetlord. From the Rimeheart, Runa commands the Frozen Vow in the Icy Expanse, far from the Admiralty in Goldwind.

Frosthold and the whaling seas belong to the same region as her watch. The Eighth’s story is read against those holds, fleets and long southern distances, where the presence of a naval ship means the Council’s reach has made it all the way down.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Frostbite has never asked Goldwind for anything. Goldwind has noticed, and it worries them.” (a Frosthold harbor-clerk)

title: Skarrei Ninth-Squall
subtitle: Into the weather
summary: Thunderhead leads the Standing Storm from Stormreach. Skarrei Ninth-Squall is the Galven Fleetlord whose charge is the Armada’s heavy-weather operations.

sections.title: The storm that never disperses
paragraphs: Skarrei Ninth-Squall commands the Ninth Fleet, the Standing Storm, out of Stormreach. The fleet runs the Armada’s heavy-weather operations. Its name is a statement of where it is expected to work: in the weather that shapes the northern sea-road.

The fleets call her Thunderhead. Her flag flies from the Stormcrown, one of the Armada’s nine Executioner-class men-of-war. The scale of that hull gives the storm-admiral’s command a presence to match its name.

sections.title: A Galven command
paragraphs: Skarrei is Galven, one of the blue-skinned storm-folk whose branching marks brighten like lightning. The Galven’s place in the Armada also appears in its Juggernaut heavy frigates, the storm-runners crewed by her people.

Her office is naval; the stories told about her belong to the sailors. The rumor that Thunderhead sings to the weather is repeated at Stormreach, where a fleet’s reputation has the sea itself to compete with.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Thunderhead takes the Stormcrown out when every other ship is coming in. The crew say she sings to the weather, and the weather sings back.” (a Stormreach dock-hand)

illustration.alt: Skarrei Ninth-Squall steers the Stormcrown into heavy weather, her human-shaped ears, blue skin and branching light-marks visible above her bare forearms.
illustration.caption: Into the weather.

title: Zophiel
subtitle: The Anvil’s right hand
summary: First Blade of the Conqueror, and the Grand Admiral's right hand.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Zophiel is the First Blade of the Conqueror, the Grand Admiral's flagship, and Kalivos Durant's right hand.
When the Anvil cannot be in two places, Zophiel is in the second.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Zophiel has carried the Grand Admiral's orders for eleven years and has never once been asked to repeat one.” (a Conqueror Hand)

title: Hoskelis Torraflame
subtitle: The other Torraflame at sea
summary: Ship-Lord of the Warsprite, Enara Torraflame's cousin and lifelong rival.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Hoskelis Torraflame is the Ship-Lord of the Warsprite and the cousin of Enara Torraflame, Fleetlord of the Killing Tide.
The two have competed at everything since they were children: who sails faster, who fights better, who gets the medal. The Killing Tide keeps a book on it, and the book is very long.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Warsprite came into Goldwind with a sea-serpent's tooth lashed to her bow. The Intervention came in the next morning with two.” (a Goldwind harbor-boy)

title: Maelis Windleaf
subtitle: A name misspelled for luck
summary: Ship-Lord of the Dreadnaught, first hull of the Dreadnought class, misspelled for luck.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Maelis Windleaf is the Ship-Lord of the Dreadnaught, the first hull of the Dreadnought class.
Her builder misspelled the name on the hull. The Armada kept it for luck, and so far the luck has held.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Paint the Dreadnaught's name right and she sinks. Every shipwright in Goldwind knows it, and Maelis Windleaf has a painter flogged for trying.” (a Goldwind shipwright, who may be joking)

title: Asim Kelu Manutar, "the Helder"
subtitle: The Helder, both of them
summary: Ship-Lord of the Helder. The man and the ship share the name, and nobody remembers which had it first.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Asim Kelu Manutar is the Ship-Lord of the Helder, and the fleets call him the Helder too.
The man and the ship share the name, and nobody remembers which had it first.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Ask the Helder whether he was named for the ship, and he asks you whether the ship was named for him.” (a Hand of the Helder)

title: Kizur Malekium
subtitle: The chase that will not end
summary: Ship-Lord of the Vindicator Darthmaw, a pursuit sloop that never gives up a chase.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Kizur Malekium is the Ship-Lord of the Darthmaw, a Vindicator-class pursuit sloop.
The Darthmaw has a reputation for never giving up a chase, and its captain has a reputation for liking it that way.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “The Darthmaw chased a smuggler from Silverport to the ice. The smuggler surrendered from boredom.” (a Silverport tavern-keeper)

title: Innaro of the Fifteenth
subtitle: The Fifteenth boards first
summary: Sword-Warden of the Fifteenth Company, the oldest company of marines in the Armada.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Innaro is the Sword-Warden of the Fifteenth Company, the oldest company of marines in the Armada. His second is Thom.
The Fifteenth boards first. It is the only company in the Armada that does not keep a list of its dead, because it says it never stopped counting them as its own.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Innaro of the Fifteenth has been offered a ship four times and turned it down four times. He says a ship would get in the way of the boarding.” (a Blue Coat marine)

title: Admiral Thulissa
subtitle: The charge the islands still remember
summary: Admiral of the Trident and leader of the Coalition at the Kraken’s Maw, Thulissa reached Blackheart’s deck, killed him and returned to her own ship with wounds she would not survive.

sections.title: Sixteen hours against the pirate line
paragraphs: In 165 EC, Thulissa of the Trident led the Kalvatar Coalition at the Kraken’s Maw. Navy and Hunters brought some fifty-six ships against more than a hundred and twelve under Admiral Blackheart. The battle lasted sixteen hours.

Falken Brightsight fought beside her from the Falkoner. Across the Coalition, the Jubilant held the defense, the Iron Swan broke through the line repeatedly and the Crimson Tide took on the Gaze of Abyss. Thulissa’s command belonged to that shared, costly effort.

sections.title: On the Dread Sovereign
paragraphs: She led a charge through the pirate fleet to Blackheart’s flagship, the Dread Sovereign. There she fought him and drove her trident through his heart. His death broke the pirate armada’s resolve.
Thulissa made it back to her own ship. She collapsed on its deck and died of her wounds. The islands’ victory and the loss of the admiral belong to the same ending; her return was not a recovery.

sections.title: The name left to the living
paragraphs: Ten years later, she remains the great hero of the age. The battle is part of the reason the Armada and Hunters can quarrel so fiercely and still stand together when the islands need them. Brightsight now commands the Last Psalm from the same Falkoner he captained beside her.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Thulissa's trident was never found. Some say the sea kept it, and will give it back to the next one who earns it.” (a Kraken's Maw salvager)

facts: Died of her wounds after the battle

illustration.alt: Admiral Thulissa drives her trident against Blackheart's heavy sabre in a ferocious close-quarters duel on the storm-tossed deck of the Dread Sovereign.
illustration.caption: The line ends here.

gallery.alt: Admiral Thulissa, seen from behind holding her trident, directs the Trident through the pirate line toward the Dread Sovereign in the smoke of the Kraken's Maw.
gallery.caption: Through the line.
gallery.label: The Trident through the line

title: Captain Magnus and Leoric
subtitle: The Sledgehammer’s command, passed in battle
summary: Magnus fell to Shade Serpentfang at the Kraken’s Maw. His son Leoric took command of the Sledgehammer while the battle was still being fought.

sections.title: Magnus at the Maw
paragraphs: Captain Magnus was a legendary Hunter, captain of the Sledgehammer. In 165 EC his ship fought in the Coalition of Navy and Hunters against Admiral Blackheart at the Kraken’s Maw.

Blackheart’s lieutenant Shade Serpentfang carried a venom-bladed weapon. In their duel he cut Magnus down. The death of a captain became part of a battle in which the Coalition was already heavily outnumbered.

sections.title: Leoric takes the deck
paragraphs: Leoric took command of his father’s ship in the middle of the fighting and carried on. His name enters the islands’ account of the battle at the instant Magnus’s part in it ends.

The Coalition won and Blackheart died, but Serpentfang escaped into the night. The Sledgehammer’s story therefore holds both a continued command and an unfinished reckoning. What Leoric keeps of his father’s memory beyond that day is the subject of sailors’ stories.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Leoric keeps his father's chair on the Sledgehammer's quarterdeck empty, and stands beside it.” (a Hunter of the Goldwind Lodge)

title: Admiral Blackheart
subtitle: The iron fist that broke at the Maw
summary: Blackheart bound the southern pirate crews into a force of more than a hundred and twelve ships. At the Kraken’s Maw, Thulissa reached his flagship and ended his command.

sections.title: One command over scattered crews
paragraphs: Admiral Blackheart was the pirate-lord who forced the scattered crews of the south beneath a single iron-fisted command. His flagship was the Dread Sovereign. By 165 EC he could bring more than a hundred and twelve ships against the archipelago.

At the Kraken’s Maw, the Coalition of Navy and Hunters met that force with some fifty-six ships. The scale of the threat lay in the crews Blackheart had brought together: piracy gathered into a fleet capable of challenging the islands collectively.

sections.title: The Dread Sovereign’s deck
