illustration.caption: A knight’s work on the village road.

title: Kiel Keyron
subtitle: Far from finished here
summary: An independent monster slayer, hunting the thing that destroyed his village.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: A tall young man with a lean, muscular frame, dark brown hair falling in tousled waves to his nape, and a youthful face that belies what he has endured. His honey-colored eyes are the most striking thing about him: intense and determined, with a flicker of vulnerability underneath. He wears reinforced leather armor and functional clothes in dark, earthy tones, with a weathered rust-colored scarf, and intricate protective patterns etched into his armor and weapons. A silver-edged longsword rides across his back, twin handguns sit at his hips, and his gear hangs from straps and a rugged pack.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Kiel grew up in a jungle village in the Southern Wilds, the son of its chief and one of seven children. He was close to his six siblings. His curiosity and hot temper made him restless, but the wilderness taught him resourcefulness, patience and survival.

A supernatural catastrophe destroyed the village in a single night. His parents and all six siblings were lost. Monster-hunters took the survivor in and trained him in the occult, weapons and the containment of supernatural dangers.

As his skill grew, he resisted the demands for obedience that came with his training. He left to work independently. He now hunts the creatures that ruined his life, seeking answers about the ancient ruins and the thing that came through their seal.

sections.title: Powers and abilities
list: Blade Mastery: exceptional swordsmanship, precise attacks and evasion.
Unarmed Combat Expertise: proficient in hand-to-hand combat, disarming and grappling.
Occult Scholar: vast knowledge of the supernatural and of strategies to defeat dark beings.
Cunning Strategist: adapts quickly, invents unexpected tactics and outwits opponents.
Indomitable Will: resists fear, pain and psychological manipulation, and never wavers in battle.
Relentless Training Regimen: peak physical and mental condition through disciplined commitment.

sections.title: Equipment
list: Reinforced Leather Armor: lightweight yet durable, with protection and flexibility.
Silver-Edged Longsword: forged for supernatural foes; the silver edge bites creatures vulnerable to silver.
Dual Handguns: custom-made for rapid fire and accuracy, loaded with silver bullets blessed in holy rites.
Crossbow: for the silver-tipped bolts in his kit.
Monster Slayer's Kit: stakes, silver-tipped crossbow bolts, holy water and salt.
Grappling Hook and Rope: for difficult terrain, climbing and swift escapes.
Traps and Snares: bear traps, net traps and tripwires.
Talisman of Protection: an enchanted amulet that wards against dark forces and harmful spells.
Sealing Scrolls: for binding and containing supernatural creatures and dark energies.
Potion Kit: healing potions, antidotes, and elixirs that enhance the body or counter magic.
Maintenance Tools: a whetstone, a gun-cleaning kit and sewing supplies for his armor.
Rugged Backpack: durable and spacious, for supplies and research materials.

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Kiel has a temper and little patience for being told what to do. Give him a monster to track and he’ll spend as long as it takes studying it and laying traps. He can be cruel once he has it cornered. He lets few people get close, and when he does, he guards them fiercely.

sections.title: Goals
list: Hunt down and eliminate the dark creatures that haunt the world, above all the thing that destroyed his village.
Uncover the secrets of the ancient ruins and the forces that dwell within them.
Master his craft and preserve his independence.
Protect the innocent, so that no one else suffers what his family suffered.

sections.title: In Kalvatar
paragraphs: Kiel works independently in the Southern Wilds. His monster-slaying combines practical weapons, occult study, traps and sealing work.

facts: his father, the village chief; his mother; six siblings. All lost the same night.
source: The Discord Roster · 175 EC; Kalvatar Library

epigraph.quote: Where do you think you're going...? We're far from finished here.

illustration.alt: Kiel Keyron, a brown-haired human monster-slayer in reinforced leather and a rust scarf, cleans a firearm part at a workbench in a rainy Southern Wilds waystation, his holstered pistols and sheathed silver-edged sword nearby.
illustration.caption: Ready for what waits beyond the rain.

title: Hyacinth Alastor
subtitle: They do not kneel for her, yet
summary: Heir of the Rose House, occult swordswoman, and a young woman who knows the world does not kneel for her yet.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: An exceptionally beautiful, tall, slender tiefling with an athletic build and soft baby-pink skin. Her ears are pointed. Small lavender horns rise from her forehead, and her long pink hair is styled into an elaborate ponytail with brooches and braids. Her eyes match her horns, framed by small red dots and pale, thick lashes. Her gaze is usually stern or slightly annoyed, and softens only when something truly captivates her. She wears fitted robes in her house's rose-pink and deep crimson, embroidered with arcane symbols, under her most treasured possession: a glamour-woven cloak covered in a hundred butterflies that flutter with every step. Her slim sword trails a thin veil of shadow.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: Hyacinth was raised as the cherished heir of House Alastor, attended by a dozen servants and tutored by Valthor and Nemeia Alastor. Her mother planted thousands of carefully nurtured pink flowers around the estate after her birth. The Rose House’s gardens became a regional landmark.

Her education joined knowledge, the occult and swordsmanship. Her father, a renowned warrior of the Knights of the Pale Rose, delighted in her interest in the blade. His pride became apprehension as shadows gathered around her sword.

She has received deference all her life, and knows how much of it belongs to her birth rather than her achievements. Beyond the estate she wants to make that inherited respect her own. Agari, the house’s tiefling servant-emissary and her closest friend, is the person before whom she need not perform.

sections.title: Powers and abilities
list: Arcane Knowledge: an exceptional understanding of the arcane arts, and powerful spells drawn from her innate magic.
Shadow Manipulation: she bends shadows to her advantage, for stealth, offense or defense.
Swordsmanship: a formidable duelist with a unique style, fighting with a sword made in the image of her father's.
Summoning: she calls creatures and spirits from other planes to fight for her or carry out tasks.
Telepathy: she speaks with others mind to mind, which is useful for gathering information or coordinating tactics.

sections.title: Equipment
list: Sword: crafted in the image of her father's weapon, deceptively simple and lightweight.
Robes: made to fit her perfectly, in her house's colors, embroidered with arcane symbols that enhance her magic.
Bag: a magical bag that holds a surprising amount, useful for spell components and other necessities.
Glamour Weave Cloak: her most treasured possession, adorned with a hundred moving butterflies that flutter with each step.

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Hyacinth grew up attended by a dozen servants and has little practice compromising. She knows exactly how much of her influence comes from her name, even when she uses it to get her way. In company, she can flirt while taking someone’s measure, and she’ll defy her family if their plans get in the way of her own. With Agari, who serves the house, she can drop the performance.

Fine food, music and a garden without an audience can draw her attention as readily as court intrigue. At the midsummer gala she listens closely to the women whom other guests dismiss as gossips, resents being crowded by unwanted suitors, and finds room for teasing and curiosity when she can choose her own company. Her impatience with ceremony does not keep her from knowing exactly how to use it.

sections.title: Goals
list: Solidify her power and influence.
Earn the respect and admiration she has always been given by birthright.
Assert her dominance as she ventures further into the world, and break the limits her noble lineage imposes on her.

sections.title: In Kalvatar
paragraphs: The Rose House is one of the Five. Its colors, rose-pink and deep crimson, and its black-rose sigil make Hyacinth’s allegiance immediately legible.

The family motto is “All Power Has a Price.” Her own ambition is to earn the respect she has always received by birth. Her tension with Reinhardt Holst is already part of the islands’ account of the houses.

sections.title: A Midsummer Gala
paragraphs: At the midsummer gala, Hyacinth arrives in a butterfly mask amid drifting pink petals. Later she slips into the garden barefoot and falls into conversation with Reinhardt Holst. Hosts prize an appearance by the Pink Lady because she so rarely makes one. The garden is where you get to see what actually holds her attention.

sections.title: Vesna, her prized Songcrest
paragraphs: Vesna, Hyacinth’s prized pink-and-white Songcrest, was a birthday gift. Hyacinth affectionately calls Vesna “Wunwun”, the childhood name she used for Songcrests in imitation of their calls. The name has stayed with her, a small trace of the girl beneath the Rose House’s heir. Riding Vesna brings out a quieter pleasure in her, her expression softening as the mount settles into its running stride.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Hyacinth Alastor and Reinhardt Holst were seen together at Lord Vanris’s Midsummer Gala. A chance conversation, they say. Of course. The drawing rooms are already wondering whether there is something more between the Rose House’s heir and the disinherited Holst.” (whispered behind a silk fan)

facts: Agari, a tiefling servant-emissary of the house
source: The Discord Roster · 175 EC; Kalvatar Library; A Midsummer Gala

epigraph.quote: They do not kneel for me... yet.

illustration.alt: Hyacinth Alastor, a beautiful pale-pink tiefling with pointed ears, lavender horns and eyes, and long braided pink hair, walks in rose-colored robes and a butterfly cloak through a flowering garden; a butterfly hovers by her raised hand.
illustration.caption: The Pink Lady in the Rose House gardens.

gallery.alt: Hyacinth Alastor rides Vesna, her prized pink-and-white Songcrest, through a sunlit rose garden. Vesna runs on its hind legs beneath an elevated saddle and an ornate gold bridle.
gallery.caption: Hyacinth rides Vesna, her birthday gift and beloved “Wunwun”, a name for Songcrests she has kept since childhood.
gallery.label: Hyacinth & Vesna · Wunwun

title: Luralana Nightingale
subtitle: More voices in the forest
summary: A wandering witch found as a baby on a moonlit riverbank, still looking for the truth of her birth.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: A dainty, fair-skinned young woman with long black hair, striking silver-gray eyes and delicate features. She dresses in the typical garb of a witch: a ruffled white blouse under a short black capelet, long boots, knee socks, and the ever-pointy hat that gives her an unmistakable silhouette. She leans on a hand-carved hazel staff set with sigils and small crystals, and a travel pack covered in mismatched pockets hangs at her back. Moths and butterflies drift around her and settle on her hands without fear.

sections.title: Background
paragraphs: The circumstances of Luralana's birth are shrouded in mystery. The woman who would become her mother, a witch named Morgan, was once guiding a caravan through the Southern Wilds, helping them navigate the treacherous forests in exchange for protection while she gathered ingredients for her potions and spells.

On the third day of the expedition, the party reached a river glen where they decided to rest for the night. There was a chill in the air, and the moonlight turned the waters a silver-blue. To everyone's surprise, wisps of light began to dance along the riverbanks in a magical spectacle. The dance went on for some time, the party watching in awe, until a strange sound turned their attention: there on the riverbank lay a crying baby, a girl with jet-black hair and silver-gray eyes.

Taking her as a gift from the moon itself, Morgan raised the baby as her own daughter and taught her the arts of witchcraft as she grew. Luralana was a shrewd student, helping her mother with potions and spells from a young age, and eventually grew into a skilled and potent witch herself. Once she came of age, she decided to wander the world as her mother had before her. With Morgan's blessing, she set out to learn the secrets of the world for herself, and perhaps to discover the true nature of her birth.

sections.title: Powers and abilities
list: Shadow Magic: a firm grasp of the shadow arts. She molds the energies of the spirit world to summon apparitions, control shadows, lay hexes, and briefly speak with the dead through seances and rituals.

Expert Alchemist: she creates and develops her own concoctions, harmful and beneficial alike. This makes her a very effective healer and an accomplished poison maker, and, curiously, a very good cook.
Proficient Biologist and Botanist: raised in the forest under her mother's tutelage, she can identify a myriad of herbs and plants, and many of the animals she has met in her travels.
Divination: as any witch worth her salt, she practices several kinds:
Astromancy
Chiromancy
Osteomancy
Reading tea leaves
Witchcraft: her craft also covers crystals, exorcisms, folk medicine and other crafting arts.

sections.title: Equipment
list: Hand-carved Staff: a walking aid and a focus for her spells, carved from a long hazel branch and inlaid with sigils and crystals. It is pleasantly warm to the touch, and some say it glows faintly under the full moon.
Witch Hat: just a plain old pointy hat that smells faintly of hazelnuts. Nothing too magical about it... or is there? Somehow, it never gets damaged.
Dusty Old Grimoire: an old notebook with far too many pages, full of spells, scribbles, recipes and sigil drawings that no one but its owner can read. Like the hat, it never seems to wear out.

Travel Pack: a beautiful handmade pack with a random assortment of pockets around its main compartment, full of dolls, ingredients, tools and cooking gear. She puts anything of interest in it, as long as it fits. It seems bottomless...

sections.title: Personality
paragraphs: Luralana has an airy, pleasant demeanor, with an ethereal air of elegance and tranquility. She is easy to get along with and doesn't speak much, but when she does, she speaks in a soft, motherly tone despite her age. Somewhat lacking in social skills after a childhood in the forest, she tries her best to make friends when she can, and people tend to say she has a "big sister" air. She has a supernatural gift for befriending animals, especially butterflies and moths, which never fly away from her; the teacup moths that so many islanders keep as companions will leave their owners to drift toward her. She loves nature, and is more comfortable in cozy, quiet places than in busy ones full of people.

sections.title: Goals
list: Improve her craft and become the best witch she can be, learning from the world and from the nature of magic itself.
Travel and document everything the world has to show.
Discover the circumstances of her birth.

sections.title: In Kalvatar
paragraphs: Morgan raised Luralana in the forests of the Southern Wilds. Her travels continue that education through plants, remedies, spirits and the customs of new shores.
Moths and butterflies settle on her without fear. Even teacup moths, among the islands’ familiar companions, are drawn toward her. The reason remains unexplained.

facts: looks to be in her early twenties; her true age is unknown
in the forests of the Southern Wilds
Morgan, the witch who found and raised her
source: The Discord Roster · 175 EC; Kalvatar Library

epigraph.quote: Close your eyes... Listen to the wind... There are more voices in the forest than in any city you will find. You just need to listen carefully.

illustration.alt: Black-haired wandering witch Luralana Nightingale offers a hand to moths while holding a cup of tea in a forest cottage, her hazel staff and many-pocketed pack beside the hearth.
illustration.caption: Tea, moths and a moment by the fire.

title: The Knights of the Northern Lights
subtitle: A people before a crown
summary: Amalorian knights serving in the Frontier under Council permits, sworn to the common folk and opposed to the Korvan Imperium’s agents.

sections.title: Across the strait
paragraphs: The order was founded in Amalor on Assios during the Thousand-Year War. Its name comes from the lights above the strait on winter nights. Amalorian children call them the lanterns of knights who died keeping watch.
Its knights pursue imperial agents in Frontier ports, protect refugees from those who prey on them and serve ordinary people wherever they travel. Their oath places the people before the crown.

sections.title: On Council soil
paragraphs: The knights are foreigners bearing arms in Kalvatar. They operate under permits of passage issued by the Council of the Charted Isles, and must hand captured agents over to Council justice.
Their chapter house stands in Ironfort. Frontier magistrates often welcome the help; the Armada is less comfortable with it, and some Council members suspect Amalor of keeping eyes in the islands.

sections.title: Ranks and sign
paragraphs: The order’s ranks are Knight, Knight-Errant, Knight-Captain and Lord Warden. A Knight-Errant has leave to travel alone on pilgrimage. The Lord Warden commands the order in Kalvatar.

Its sign is a silver star above a ribbon of green light on midnight blue. Caelan Caelius carries that sign into the forgotten islands, where an oath may require mending a roof as readily as drawing a sword.

facts: Silver star, green light, midnight blue

title: Kaskan
subtitle: An independent trading island
summary: Merchant ships share Kaskan’s bay with patrol vessels, while giant aurocs work on land.

sections.title: The regent’s harbor
paragraphs: Kaskan’s gold mines and trade in goods from across the region have paid for a private army and a fleet of roughly nine vessels. At least three guard the bay. Regent Hugo Goldvein governs the island as a neutral port, and riding and working aurocs are part of daily life.

title: Monumak
subtitle: Island of Ironport and Blackstone
summary: A southern island where the wealth beneath the rock has shaped the politics above it.

sections.title: The mines and the crown
paragraphs: The Blackstone Mines are a major source of Krysta. In Ironport, merchants and sailors feel the reach of Lord Hadros Morvain, whose claim to a crown put the island at the center of a dispute over who gets to rule it.

title: Ironport
subtitle: A port on Monumak
summary: On Monumak, Ironport brings merchants, sailors and smugglers into the same streets.

sections.title: Around the port
paragraphs: Bonny’s Rest and the Rusty Bucket are landmarks from the party’s time in town. The city was also the setting for much of the unrest around Hadros Morvain’s attempt to establish his kingdom.

title: Lyle Lynch
subtitle: Human • Trickery Cleric
summary: If a plan falls apart, Lyle can usually make it sound as though it was meant to go that way.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Known as Lacuna Lynx, Lyle is a con artist with an improbable talent for getting out of trouble. He works with disguises, quick explanations and the magic of a Trickery cleric.

title: Mithras Steelheart
subtitle: Human • Rogue / Monk
summary: Mithras has a sharp eye and a habit of noticing what others walk past.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: He scouts ahead, watches entrances and takes stock of a room before making his move. His companions can rely on him for a quiet approach or a fight at close quarters.

title: Agari of House Alastor
subtitle: Tiefling • Necromancy Wizard
summary: Agari speaks for the Rose House with the air of someone who would rather be somewhere else.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: She serves House Alastor as an emissary. The name she travels under tells you whose interests she represents. Her command of necromancy is her own.

In Monumak, Agari’s visit to Hadros Morvain’s masquerade put the Rose House’s emissary in the company of his guests. Beck and Grolsh accompanied her as her personal escort, giving the visit the visible form of a noble delegation.

title: Cassian Virel
subtitle: Aasimar • Paladin of Conquest
summary: An aasimar paladin who knows Imperial procedure from the inside.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Cassian follows the Oath of Conquest and travels with the company in the southern islands. He arranged passage aboard the Last Word, a vessel with mercenaries and Hunters among its crew.

title: Hugo Goldvein
subtitle: Regent of Kaskan
summary: Kaskan’s regent listens closely when a visitor proposes a deal. He has an island’s independence to weigh against the price.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Hugo rules a wealthy trading island with gold mines, a private army and ships of its own. He prizes stability and profitable agreements. Anyone asking him to pick a side will have to explain what Kaskan gains by doing so.

title: Viktor Goldvein
subtitle: Son of the Regent
summary: Viktor makes a quick answer look easy, even in company where every word gets weighed.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Hugo Goldvein’s son is clever, relaxed and quite aware of his own talents. He’s quick with a comeback and can hold his own in the company of Kaskan’s merchants and visiting dignitaries.

title: Rhal
subtitle: Tavern proprietor in Kaskan
summary: Rhal has lived on Kaskan long enough to know which introductions are worth asking for.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Imperial-born and long settled on the island, Rhal runs a tavern and knows people across Kaskan’s trading community. For arrivals who need to get their bearings, his place is a good first stop.

title: Hadros Morvain
subtitle: Merchant lord of Monumak
summary: Hadros Morvain built his standing as a merchant lord, then laid claim to a crown.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Morvain styled himself king of Monumak. The Blackstone Mines, a major source of Krysta, were central to the power he sought to build on the island.

Morvain put his claim on display by holding a masquerade for his coronation. The celebration brought guests to his court, while the Blackstone Mines gave his bid for power something more tangible than ceremony: a major source of Krysta.

title: Veyren Quill
subtitle: An Ironport scoundrel
summary: Veyren can make a cutting remark sound like an invitation to sit down.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Quick with a joke and comfortable among Ironport’s underworld, he met Agari and her companions during their time in the city. He took particular pleasure in teasing the envoy.

Veyren’s familiarity with Ironport’s underworld gives his encounter with Agari a different setting from the noble company of the masquerade. His habit of teasing the envoy makes the contrast plain: he is comfortable joking with her even when her name carries the weight of House Alastor.

title: Otto Van Galen
subtitle: Imperial officer
summary: An Imperial officer whose dealings reach beyond the quarterdeck.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Otto Van Galen understands the weight a trade agreement carries in the southern islands. On Kaskan, a visiting officer must reckon with a regent who has his own ships, soldiers and interests.

title: Beck
subtitle: Bodyguard to Agari
summary: Beck travels with Agari on House Alastor’s southern business.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Beck and Grolsh make up the envoy’s personal escort. Both accompanied her to Hadros Morvain’s masquerade.

Beck’s presence at the masquerade shows how close the duties of an escort can run to a noble house’s public business. He and Grolsh were there in Agari’s service while she attended as the emissary of House Alastor.

title: Grolsh
subtitle: Bodyguard to Agari
summary: Grolsh is one of the two guards charged with Agari’s safety.

sections.title: In the southern islands
paragraphs: Alongside Beck, Grolsh accompanied the Rose House’s emissary to Monumak and attended Hadros Morvain’s masquerade as part of her escort.

Traveling with Agari to Monumak put Grolsh’s duties alongside the Rose House’s dealings on the island. At the masquerade he and Beck remained her personal escort in a gathering hosted by the man who claimed its crown.

title: Twincrest
subtitle: Keshix · Hunt tradition
summary: A light, twin-crested predator, smaller than a Swordtooth and dangerous at close quarters.

sections.title: Form and character
paragraphs: A Twincrest is a lightly built bipedal hunter with two narrow crests rising above its snout, a long balancing tail and a mouth full of fine, recurved teeth. It is smaller than the southern cavalry predators, but large enough to threaten a person. Its quick turns and short bursts of speed make narrow jungle paths dangerous ground.

sections.title: Hunting and handling
paragraphs: It tests an opening before committing to a bite, circling the edge of a camp or following an injured animal through cover. A pair can be especially troublesome when one holds attention and the other approaches from the side. Handlers work with it for hunting and guarding enclosed grounds, keeping a clear separation between feeding and training.

illustration.label: Keshix
illustration.alt: A twin-crested predator steps onto a wet jungle path, with an adult traveler beyond it.
illustration.caption: Keshix

title: Songcrest
subtitle: Saalix · Riding tradition
summary: An elegant herbivorous riding saurian with a sweeping hollow crest and a resonant herd-call.

sections.title: Form and character
paragraphs: The Songcrest carries a long crest swept back from its head and a strong tail that balances its stride. It walks comfortably on four feet and can rise onto its hind legs when it needs to move quickly. Its deep, carrying calls help scattered members of a herd keep contact through woodland.

sections.title: An elegant mount
paragraphs: Its measured gait and striking profile make it a favored mount for processions, leisurely travel and the households of wealthy southerners. A well-fitted saddle leaves the shoulders free and distributes the rider’s weight across the back. Keepers judge a riding animal by its composure around crowds as carefully as by the line of its crest.

sections.title: On the road
paragraphs: Travelers carry light baggage behind the saddle and allow regular stops for water and browsing. A startled Songcrest can knock a person aside with its bulk or tail, so a rider accustomed to gentle manners still gives it room when the herd becomes alarmed.

sections.title: Vesna
paragraphs: Vesna, Hyacinth Alastor’s prized pink-and-white Songcrest, was a birthday gift. Hyacinth affectionately calls Vesna “Wunwun”, the name she used for Songcrests as a little girl, imitating their calls.

illustration.label: Saalix
illustration.alt: A blue-green riding saurian with a long coral crest carries a traveler through a sunlit island port.
illustration.caption: Saalix

gallery.caption: Hyacinth rides Vesna, her birthday gift and beloved “Wunwun”, a name for Songcrests she has kept since childhood.
gallery.label: Hyacinth & Vesna · Wunwun

title: Loadback
subtitle: Tammok · Labor tradition
summary: A broad working category of sturdy herbivorous pack saurians, used for caravan baggage, long journeys and hauling.

sections.title: Form and character
paragraphs: Loadback is the working name for several sturdy herbivorous saurians bred to carry baggage over long routes. It includes animals with broad beaked mouths, strong forelimbs and pointed thumb-spikes, alongside similar pack animals selected for a strong back, endurance and a steady pace. Tammok is the Kalvatari name used for this working group.

Caravan keepers distinguish local breeds by build, gait and the loads they can carry. A broad back and sound feet matter more to this category than a particular crest or a thumb-spike, and a pack saddle must fit the individual animal.

sections.title: Caravans and baggage
paragraphs: Caravan keepers fit it with balanced panniers for tents, tools, provisions and trade goods. It also pulls a suitable cart where the road permits. Long-distance crews check the harness at each stop, since an uneven load can injure even a strong animal over several days of walking.

sections.title: A working partnership
paragraphs: Its value grows with the journey: a familiar handler can lead it through repeated loading, rest and travel without turning each departure into a struggle. Its weight, and the thumb-spikes of some breeds, make it dangerous when cornered, so teams leave it space to turn and approach where it can see them.

illustration.label: Tammok
illustration.alt: Two herbivorous pack saurians carry balanced baggage on a jungle caravan trail beside their guide.
illustration.caption: Tammok

title: The Arbiters
subtitle: One year, one thread, the authority of the office
summary: Chosen by annual lot from registered casters of the Third Circle or higher, Arbiters serve a paid year overseeing powerful magic in Council lands.

sections.title: The ones who listen
paragraphs: Casting of the Third Circle and above rings the world’s Krysta like a struck bell. In Council lands, working magic at that threshold requires a Writ from the Arcane Registry. The Arbiters are the ones who listen and exercise the public authority attached to that law. Their office concerns powerful magic; household Small Ways and workings below the Third Circle do not require a Writ.

An Arbiter may have been a sailor, a scholar, a Hunter, a hedge-wizard or a priest before the draw. Their familiar trade remains part of who they are during service. What changes is the authority they carry for the year.

sections.title: The Charter Day draw
paragraphs: Each Charter Day, the Registry draws lots among every registered caster of the Third Circle or higher, across all trades. Those drawn serve for one year. Service is paid and honored, and assignments are made near home when possible.
Qualified volunteers may serve for up to ten years in a lifetime. After ten years of service, they may serve no further.
Once made, an assignment is absolute. An Arbiter cannot negotiate a different posting by offering a longer term of service.

sections.title: The thread each one weaves
paragraphs: At investiture, every Arbiter receives raw Krysta-thread and weaves their own regalia. Every piece made with that thread is attuned to its maker: when powerful casting rings the world’s Krysta, the regalia resonates and its Arbiter feels it. The garments are the means by which they listen.

Every Arbiter wears something on their head, and every set of regalia bears an embroidered eye. Beyond those shared marks, their dress is personal. One may favor an enormous pointed hat in extravagant colors, another an entirely black outfit. Turbans, bandanas and broad-brimmed musketeer hats all belong among the year’s silhouettes. Cloaks, sashes and other pieces woven from the allotted thread share the same bond.

No two sets are alike. The style comes from the wearer; the headwear and embroidered eye identify the office when the mark is displayed. An Arbiter can make the embroidered eye appear or disappear at will, concealing the identifying mark while investigating undercover and revealing it when they choose to make their office known. With the eye displayed, the regalia is unmistakable at a hundred paces, whether its maker favors a riot of color or the restraint of black cloth.

sections.title: A word that can stop a ship
paragraphs: An Arbiter can ground a ship, void a duel, seal a ruin or suspend a Writ. A captain’s sailing plans, a noble’s arrangements and an expedition’s investment may all be interrupted by the exercise of that office. Its authority is recognized in the Council’s jurisdiction, whose reach covers roughly one island in six.

That authority belongs to the office for the term of service. Beyond the Council’s reach, local law governs. Recognition of an Arbiter there depends on the people and powers who hold the harbor, road or shore.

sections.title: Each Arbiter’s judgment
paragraphs: How an Arbiter responds to a resonance depends on the individual. Each decides how to approach the caster, investigate the circumstances and exercise the authority of the office. There is no single prescribed sequence of intervention shared by every Arbiter.

A familiar sash or distinctive hat therefore tells a harbor more than who holds the office. People learn the manner of the person wearing it: how they ask questions, what they notice and how they choose to act.

sections.title: The Hall of Threads
paragraphs: At the end of a term, the regalia retires to the Hall of Threads in Goldwind. A returning volunteer may take up their own thread again. The hall keeps the garments of former service together, each shaped by the hands and taste of its wearer.
An old sash in the hall may once have belonged to the quiet person now selling charts or teaching a lesson back home. The office passes on; its thread remains.

sections.title: Public faces and private friction
paragraphs: The Inkers’ Circle prints collectible Arbiter cards. Children trade them alongside Hunter Ranking cards, making a year of civic service part of the same portside culture that follows famous crews. The striking variety of regalia gives each card its own silhouette.

Priests who are registered and meet the circle requirement enter the same draw as other practitioners. The Concord’s refusal to register its casters remains an unresolved institutional dispute. It does not remove other religious traditions from the draw.
The Arbiters hold an acknowledged public office. The Registrar, the alleged hunter of unlicensed casters in Goldwind’s fog, remains a figure whose existence the University and the Registry deny.

sections.title: The newly chosen Arbiters of 175 EC
paragraphs: Radan Sunmere, Lysandra Vellune and Kettik of the Ninth Step are the three newly chosen Arbiters assigned to Goldwind for one full year, from the Charter Day draw of 175 EC until the next Charter Day.

Radan is an easygoing sorcerer used to odd jobs and extraordinary luck. Lysandra owns a fashionable shop selling clothing and enchanted articles and enjoys a degree of local celebrity. Kettik brings the patient scrutiny of a warehouse assessor. Each exercises the office in their own way.

Radan and Lysandra knew one another before the draw. She tried to change her posting, even offering two additional years of service to avoid being assigned with him. The assignment was absolute; the three will serve their original one-year term together in Goldwind.

facts: Registered casters, Third Circle or higher
One year, paid; near home when possible
Up to ten years in a lifetime
Personally woven Krysta-thread, attuned to its maker
Headwear and an embroidered eye, revealed or concealed at will
Resonance felt through the attuned regalia
source: Welcome to Kalvatar · Magic and the Arbiters · Kafeii’s setting text · 175 EC

epigraph.quote: You do not choose to become one; the year chooses you.

title: Radan Sunmere
subtitle: A little work, a little luck, and finally a salary
summary: A muscular, easygoing sorcerer who lives on odd jobs and improbable good fortune, newly chosen for a salaried year as one of Goldwind’s three Arbiters.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: A handsome, deeply tanned human with a powerful muscular build, dark curls and a broad, easy grin. His enormous pointed hat bends beneath its own extravagance: turquoise, magenta and gold, with an embroidered eye. An open sleeveless vest leaves his arms bare; billowing trousers, sandals and a rich sash complete the outfit. Necklaces, rings, earrings and heavy cuffs catch the light whenever he moves.

sections.title: Before the thread
paragraphs: Radan has little money and makes his living taking whatever work comes along. A paid errand, a short contract or a job that needs a sorcerer keeps him moving until the next opportunity appears. His extravagant appearance is a poor guide to his finances.

His magic is innate, and he has a habit of improvising his way through situations that other people would prepare for. Astonishingly often, it works. The right person happens to be passing, a bad turn opens an unexpected door, or a plan invented halfway through the problem proves sufficient.
Being drawn as an Arbiter finally gives him a salary for a full year. He is pleased by the prospect of regular pay and appears entirely confident that the responsibilities will work themselves out.

sections.title: The newly chosen year
paragraphs: Newly chosen in the Charter Day draw for 175 EC, he serves a full one-year term, ending at the next Charter Day. His assignment is Goldwind.

His hat and woven regalia are attuned to him. He feels powerful magic through their resonance and can reveal or conceal the embroidered eye at will. He enjoys the public side of the office, though he is quite capable of hiding the eye when discretion serves him.

sections.title: Manner and judgment
paragraphs: Radan is sociable, physically confident and exceptionally laid-back. He tends to meet a new problem with the expectation that something useful will turn up. He listens, talks easily and adjusts his approach as events unfold. Long preparation rarely precedes the adjustment.

This ease can be reassuring to frightened witnesses and infuriating to a colleague who has already identified everything that might go wrong. His cheerful confidence survives setbacks, often just long enough for another stroke of luck to make him look justified.

sections.title: Lysandra knew him before
paragraphs: Radan and Lysandra knew one another before the Charter Day draw. She already knew his habit of winging it, and his apparent ability to get away with it. Sharing an assignment gives her a full year of close exposure to both.

Her complaints rarely disturb his composure. He can listen to a detailed account of his failings with the same relaxed attention he gives an interesting story. Their familiarity makes their exchanges immediately noticeable to anyone nearby.

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: He is an approachable official for a crew whose spellcasting has drawn attention. His method is conversational and improvised, and his lack of money gives regular employment a very practical appeal.
His good fortune should appear through circumstances and opportunities. Whether a power of luck actually favors him remains a rumor, and his relaxed attitude does not itself prove divine protection.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “Some power of luck must have a soft spot for Radan Sunmere. Nobody gets that far on ‘it’ll probably be fine’ alone.” (a Goldwind regular)

facts: One full year, Charter Day to the next
Little money; Arbiter service provides a regular salary
Remarkable; a divine blessing is rumored

epigraph.quote: Tell me what you cast. Then tell me who was standing next to it.

source: Kafeii’s approved Arbiter illustration and NPC expansion · 175 EC

title: Lysandra Vellune
subtitle: A very large hat and very little patience for the sun
summary: A pale, impeccably groomed owner of a fashionable enchanted-goods shop and a local celebrity, assigned to serve Goldwind alongside the maddeningly relaxed Radan Sunmere.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: An attractive pale human woman with long light hair, an immaculate manicure and a freshly finished coral-pink pedicure. She dresses for the coast in a fine light blouse, a flowing beach skirt and delicate open sandals. Her enormous sunhat casts a generous shadow over her face. An embroidered eye rests among its elegant gold-threaded patterns.
Her dislike of direct sun is immediately apparent. She adjusts a brim, seeks an awning or moves a conversation two steps sideways into the shade without interrupting what she is saying.

sections.title: Before the thread
paragraphs: Lysandra owns Vellune — Finery & Enchantments, a Goldwind boutique selling fashion and enchanted articles. Her taste, presentation and recognizable style have made her something of a local celebrity. Fine clothes, careful grooming and discerning customers are familiar parts of her working life.

She is a practicing illusionist with a carefully kept spellbook. She expects things to be done properly and has little patience for the assumption that preparation can always wait until after a problem arrives.

sections.title: The spellbook
paragraphs: Lysandra carries a substantial spellbook bound in ivory leather, with gilt geometric tooling, gilded page edges and an elegant clasp. Its careful spellwork sits comfortably beside the fashion and enchanted goods of her shop. She keeps it close at hand during her year as an Arbiter.

sections.title: The newly chosen year
paragraphs: Newly chosen in the Charter Day draw for 175 EC, Lysandra serves a full one-year term, ending at the next Charter Day. Her assignment is Goldwind.

The Krysta-thread in her regalia is attuned to her. She feels its resonance beneath the broad brim, and can make the embroidered eye appear or disappear at will. With the mark hidden, her hat can pass as a particularly determined response to the climate.

sections.title: Manner and judgment
paragraphs: Lysandra is composed, observant and dryly funny. She notices small inconsistencies in an account and dislikes an elaborate explanation that leaves the simple question unanswered. She often lets a person finish speaking before repeating their own words back to them.

Her manner can be cool, but she is attentive to embarrassment and privacy. A cooperative person may find her willing to conduct a difficult conversation quietly. An attempt to influence her through flattery usually earns a patient look and the original question again.

sections.title: An assignment she tried to change
paragraphs: Lysandra and Radan knew each other before they were drawn. She detests his laid-back manner, his improvisation and the frequency with which things work out for him anyway. Finding his name beside hers on Goldwind’s assignment gave her every reason to expect a difficult year.

She tried to have the assignment changed. She even offered to serve two additional years as an Arbiter if the Registry would place her away from him. The assignment was absolute. The offer secured no change, and her actual term remains the original single year.
They will serve together in Goldwind alongside Kettik of the Ninth Step. Radan’s composure through her complaints has done very little to improve her opinion of the arrangement.

sections.title: Vellune, while she serves
paragraphs: Tessa Bellfold manages the boutique’s daily business while Oren Sedge keeps its cutting and repair work moving. Lysandra returns for important fittings and commissioned spellwork during her one-year Arbiter term. The shop remains a familiar place to encounter her and, occasionally, the colleagues who interrupt her appointments.

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: Her shop and public profile give a crew reasons to know her before they see the embroidered eye. A customer seeking an enchanted article may discover that the woman behind the counter is also one of the city’s newly chosen Arbiters.

With Radan, let the irritation have a history: she knows the expression he wears when he has no plan, and he recognizes the tone that means she has noticed. Their familiarity can invite speculation without settling what either privately feels. Kettik remains their equally appointed colleague.

facts: Fashion and enchanted-goods shop owner; illusionist
One full year, Charter Day to the next
Ivory leather, gold tooling and clasp

epigraph.quote: We can discuss your Writ under that awning. The sun has contributed enough.

source: Kafeii’s approved Arbiter illustration and NPC expansion · 175 EC

title: Kettik of the Ninth Step
subtitle: Three feet tall, with every question written down
summary: An elderly kobold assessor newly chosen as an Arbiter for 175 EC, carrying a black turban, a small notebook and a lifetime’s habit of noticing what others overlook.

sections.title: Appearance
paragraphs: A wiry elderly kobold, about three feet tall, with weathered copper-brown scales, an angular reptilian snout, amber eyes and a short tail. His black turban bears a silver embroidered eye. Charcoal robes, subtle Krysta-thread seams, fitted leather shoes and a well-used satchel give him a restrained silhouette beside his flamboyant fellow Arbiters.
His notebook fits neatly in one hand. He looks up at taller people without seeming to grant them any particular advantage.

sections.title: Before the thread
paragraphs: Kettik belongs to the Ninth Step warren beneath Goldwind’s docks. He worked as a warehouse assessor and arcane examiner of cargo, tracing discrepancies between a manifest and the things that actually came ashore. Useful materials return to the warren, and he dislikes waste as much as an account that conceals it.

His familiarity with cramped storerooms and underdock passages is practical experience. He knows where a person can fit, where a crate could have been moved and how easily a supposedly sealed room can acquire another entrance.

sections.title: The newly chosen year
paragraphs: Newly chosen in the Charter Day draw for 175 EC, he serves a full one-year term, ending at the next Charter Day. His assignment is Goldwind.

The thread in his turban and robes is attuned to him and carries the resonance of powerful magic. He can hide or reveal the embroidered eye at will. With the mark concealed, he can return to the familiar work of asking warehouse questions without announcing his office.

sections.title: Manner and judgment
paragraphs: Kettik is patient, practical and quietly persistent. He favors short questions and records the answers before asking the next. He will hear an ordinary porter’s account as carefully as a captain’s. Being ignored while taller people discuss a problem often gives him time to inspect it.

He decides his own approach to each inquiry. Where Radan may begin with a conversation and Lysandra with an inconsistency, Kettik often begins by asking who last handled the object, opened the door or changed the manifest.

sections.title: At the table
paragraphs: He is a natural contact for cargo mysteries, concealed passages and magical incidents aboard merchant vessels. He appreciates a clear sketch, an intact object and witnesses who distinguish what they saw from what they assumed.
He finds Radan’s jewelry excessive but well maintained, an important qualification. Lysandra’s care for fine materials earns his respect. He expects both to wait while he finishes writing.

facts: The Ninth Step, beneath Goldwind’s docks
Warehouse assessor and arcane cargo examiner
One full year, Charter Day to the next

title: Giant Betta
subtitle: One jewel, one pool
summary: Beautiful, fiercely aggressive giant fish kept in private indoor pools by Jakupur’s wealthy households, now becoming fashionable among Heartland nobles.

sections.title: Beauty with a temper
paragraphs: A giant betta moves through the water beneath an extravagant spread of flowing fins. Its scales and fin membranes catch the light in rich shifting colors, turning a quiet pool into the center of a room. The beauty is accompanied by extreme aggression: a displaying fish can go from a slow, measured turn to a sudden rush at a rival.
The broad fins and flared gill covers that collectors admire are also part of its threatening display. A specimen spreading its colors across the water may be answering a challenge.

sections.title: The private pools of Jakupur
paragraphs: In Jakupur, wealthy households build indoor pools around a single giant betta. The pool may occupy the heart of a reception room, with guests seated around its tiled edge while the fish passes beneath them. Its water, space and upkeep are as much a declaration of wealth as the animal itself.

Collectors who want several maintain several separate pools. A row of rooms, each holding a different fish, can become a private gallery. The separation is necessary: these aggressive animals are not kept together as an ornamental school.

sections.title: Keeping a living jewel
paragraphs: Each fish needs a pool large enough to move freely and someone who understands its behavior. Owners admire color, the shape and condition of the fins, and the spectacle of a full display. Experienced keepers pay attention to the animal beneath the ornament.

A household pool is for the fish. People watch from the dry edge, and keepers treat feeding and maintenance as work around an aggressive beast. An expensive specimen remains a dangerous animal, however calmly it circles before dinner guests.

sections.title: The clandestine fights
paragraphs: Jakupur’s underground betta fights are lucrative events. Owners, handlers, organizers and bettors gather around contests where valuable fish and substantial wagers change the atmosphere of an otherwise private house. The same beauty that makes an animal desirable for display can make a fighting specimen recognizable.

The trade brings together two kinds of buyer: those who want a magnificent pool ornament and those interested in an aggressive contender. Behind a collector’s respectable introduction, a broker may be negotiating for either market.

sections.title: A fashion traveling north
paragraphs: Nobles and other wealthy people in the Central Heartland have begun importing giant bettas for their own houses. The fashion carries Jakupur’s private pools into northern reception rooms, accompanied by the expense of bringing a large live fish across the sea and preparing its new home.

Visitors compare colors and fin shapes, hosts plan rooms around their acquisitions, and a second pool announces a collection. Southern keepers and dealers find new customers among people who have seen the beauty before they have learned the temperament.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “His lordship says the second pool is for a different color. The man who delivered the fish asked where the guests would place their wagers.” (a Heartland household servant)

facts: Nobles and wealthy households of the Central Heartland
source: Kafeii’s bestiary additions · Giant bettas and private pools · 175 EC

epigraph.quote: One jewel, one pool. If you want another jewel, build another pool.

illustration.alt: Seen from an upper gallery, a giant turquoise-and-crimson betta swims fully submerged in a vast deep indoor pool in a wealthy Jakupur house, with ample open water around it and an adult owner at the far edge.
illustration.caption: A private pool in Jakupur. One jewel, one pool.

title: Vellune — Finery & Enchantments
subtitle: Good taste, by appointment
summary: Lysandra Vellune’s shaded Goldwind boutique sells fine clothes, discreet enchantments and the pleasure of being recognized by its owner. During her Arbiter year, the staff keep the shop running.

sections.title: Finding the door
paragraphs: Vellune occupies a narrow-fronted shop on the rising streets above Goldwind’s harbor promenade, within an easy walk of the Turning. Its cream awning shades a blue-painted door and a window containing a single carefully chosen outfit. The name Vellune is picked out in small brass letters. People who copy its window display are rarely the people who can afford what is in it.

Inside, pale wood, linen curtains and brushed brass keep the room cool. A fitting alcove and ordinary full-length mirror occupy the rear. The proprietor’s closed ivory-and-gold spellbook has its place beside the ledger. Tea is offered while measurements are taken, and a customer can usually hear the street without being heard from it.

sections.title: What Lysandra sells
paragraphs: The business rests on good cutting, well-chosen cloth and Lysandra’s eye for what suits a person. Customers come for fittings, alterations, hats, accessories and bespoke outfits. Some arrive with an invitation and ask to be made ready for it. Others want one piece that will still be worth wearing after the season changes.

Enchanted articles are expensive, scarce work. A few finished pieces or demonstration samples may be displayed in the glazed counter; much of the real business is commissioned, repaired or sourced for a particular client. A matching sketch is no promise that the enchantment can be finished by tomorrow.

Each enchanted piece is described plainly: what changes, how the wearer controls it and what care it needs. Lysandra’s shop keeps receipts and accounts for the Registry’s tenth on legal magical sales. The little household Ways used while sewing and cleaning are part of the workshop’s daily life.

sections.title: From the fitting book
paragraphs: These are examples of the shop’s work and recent commissions. Prices are starting quotations in Council coin; cloth, fit and the particular enchantment determine the final account. Completed magical pieces are not kept in unlimited stock.

rows: An unenchanted silk scarf, finished and dyed to Lysandra’s standard.
A finely made broad sunhat, fitted to its wearer; unenchanted.
A bespoke unenchanted coat, with fittings and ordinary alterations.
Its wearer changes the silk among three chosen colors by smoothing its edge. The material and cut stay the same.
Keeps enclosed papers dry through rain or an accidental spill. Its clasp must be shut; it is not made for prolonged immersion.
Repeats one short phrase its owner deliberately records, in that owner’s voice, when fully opened. It retains only one phrase at a time.
table.caption: Examples from Vellune’s fitting book

sections.title: Tessa Bellfold, front of house
paragraphs: Tessa is a middle-aged halfling with chestnut hair, a practical plum waistcoat and a memory for measurements, appointments and unpaid balances. She manages the counter and fitting book. During Lysandra’s public service, Tessa is the person most visitors meet first.

She is welcoming to someone who admits they need help and exquisitely polite to someone trying to impress her. She never mistakes an expensive outfit for a paid account. Her favorite answer to an impossible deadline is, “Certainly. Which of the other customers shall I disappoint for you?”

sections.title: Oren Sedge, needle and hem
paragraphs: Oren is a young human cutter and apprentice enchanter, usually found in the rear workroom with a pin cushion at his wrist. He is excellent at small repairs and too inclined to keep improving a piece after the agreed work is finished. He knows household Ways for untangling thread, lifting fresh ink spots and keeping a pinned hem in place.

He wants Lysandra to trust him with a complete enchanted commission. Tessa wants him to finish the three ordinary garments already promised for collection. He is the most likely person to ask a visiting crew to fetch a missing parcel before either woman notices it has gone astray.

sections.title: People who keep coming back
paragraphs: Odelia Ferren, a prosperous salon hostess, orders restrained pieces and takes a close interest in what everyone else has ordered. She can turn a fitting into a survey of the next social gathering. Tessa discusses only Odelia’s own clothes, which Odelia treats as a challenge.

Pell Orris, a theatrical singer, brings beautiful sketches, uncertain money and very definite opening nights. His requests make excellent work for the window when they are actually finished. He sometimes pays a deposit with proceeds from the performance that made the commission possible.

The shop also receives people with one carefully saved sum and an occasion that matters to them. Lysandra’s attention to such a fitting can be just as exacting as her treatment of a wealthy regular. That mix of customers helps explain why her name travels beyond the people who buy her enchanted work.

sections.title: A shopkeeper’s year of public service
paragraphs: Lysandra remains the owner while she serves as one of Goldwind’s three newly chosen Arbiters for 175 EC. Tessa handles daily business and appointments; Oren keeps the workroom moving. Lysandra returns for important fittings and commissioned spellwork when her duties allow.

Customers seeking an official decision are directed to arrange an official meeting. Lysandra will not treat a purchase as payment for a favorable ruling. The shop’s standing makes that distinction visible, and its enemies would be delighted to see her blur it.

Radan knew the proprietor before either was drawn. His arrival can interrupt an orderly morning with the confidence of someone who thinks there is still plenty of time. Lysandra recognizes that expression immediately. Kettik occasionally calls on either colleague; Tessa puts his tea within reach and waits for him to finish his question.

sections.title: Commissions that need outside help
paragraphs: The copied label. A visitor brings in a scarf bought elsewhere under Vellune’s name. Its advertised color change leaves dye on the wearer. Lysandra wants to know where it was sold and who is using her label. The seller’s receipt, the cloth and the customer’s account give a crew three places to begin.

The missing fitting trunk. A completed outfit has been collected by a porter carrying the right claim slip, but the customer says nobody was sent. Tessa has a precise collection time; Oren remembers the porter’s coat; the customer wants the garment recovered before an evening appearance. Someone must establish how a valid slip changed hands.

The fan with the wrong last word. An owner returns a Last Word Fan that now repeats an unwelcome personal remark. The fan only preserves a phrase deliberately recorded by its current owner. Lysandra asks for a discreet account of who owned it, borrowed it and gave it back. The commission may be a repair, a disagreement over ownership or a story the customer has not finished telling.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “He has a year’s salary now and still comes in just to ask what she thinks of his hat.” (a customer, on Radan Sunmere)
“If your fitting runs long, say nothing. You may leave with a better coat and the name of everyone attending the gala.” (heard near the Turning)

facts: Oren Sedge, cutter and apprentice enchanter
Fine clothes, alterations and commissioned enchanted articles
Staff run daily business through Lysandra’s Arbiter term
source: Kafeii’s approved Goldwind development · Lysandra’s shop expansion · 175 EC

title: Gnoll Warbands
subtitle: Raiding bands of the Bonewilds
summary: Born in the drylands of the Bonewilds, gnoll warbands raid across Kalvatar. Their banners have recently been sighted in the Northern Frontier.

sections.title: From the drylands
paragraphs: The drylands around the Bonewilds hold the greatest concentration of gnoll warbands. Bands also raid the dry reaches of the Southern Wilds and cross the archipelago on captured ships or aboard smugglers’ boats. Reports from the Northern Frontier describe wired jawbones on banners seen on opposite sides of a strait.

New warbands still form, usually from splintered raiding parties or followers who walk away from a chief. Few last. The Sworn actively hunt these smaller bands, and many survivors have little choice but to join the Ironfang Warband, the Bonewatchers, the Ashmaws, or the Redjaws.

sections.title: The Hunger
paragraphs: The Hunger is the first stage of demonic possession. One gnoll beginning to change during a raid can stir the same frenzy in others. The afflicted devour whatever they can, from provisions and livestock to captives. When there is nothing left, they turn on one another. Returning to their former selves is almost unheard of. Some sworn bands deliberately let the frenzy sweep through their ranks.

To the Sworn, gnoll flesh is the most delicious meat of all and the surest, quickest way to trigger The Hunger. They reserve a particular hatred for the Unsworn and attack them whenever they get the chance, eager to feast on their flesh. A feast that begins with fallen enemies can end with the Sworn devouring their own.

sections.title: The Flints
paragraphs: The rare survivors who emerge transformed are called Flints. Larger and stronger, they experience visions tied to the old pact. Among the sworn bands, a Flint often becomes a war leader or priest. Even when the frenzy passes, the possession has left its mark.

sections.title: Kharveth, the Hollow Maw
paragraphs: The daemon Kharveth receives the first bite of the raid from his sworn bands. His mark is a jaw with teeth turned inward. His priests call the visions of the Flints instructions, though two priests can hear the same account and send their bands to war against each other.

sections.title: The Unsworn
paragraphs: Some bands broke away from the worshippers of Kharveth so long ago that their singers count the separation in millennia. They still raid and ransom captives, and some chiefs keep bargains with settlements for years. They watch their own for signs of The Hunger and will drag an afflicted companion away from the others before the frenzy spreads.

illustration.alt: An Ironfang leader with a riveted iron jaw and oversized metal tusks leads a caravan raid beneath ancient titan ribs.
illustration.caption: An Ironfang raid in the Bonewilds.

title: Orc Tribes
subtitle: War banners and old rites
summary: Orc war bands are under tighter control along the Northern Frontier and the approaches to the Central Heartland. In the Southern Wilds, several raiding tribes are growing in strength.

sections.title: Where the banners gather
paragraphs: Along the northern roads and approaches to the Central Heartland, garrisons and regular patrols keep most armed raiding parties scattered. In the Southern Wilds, some tribes have gained fighters, seized crossings and forced isolated settlements to pay tribute. Their strength varies with the season and with which chiefs can keep their followers together.

sections.title: Old rites
paragraphs: Among the tribes now drawing notice, the Embertusks carry coals from a shrine older than their oldest recorded ancestor, while the Reedskulls offer their first spoils to a presence they say lives beneath a drowned mound. The Telling survives among both, though each recites a different account of what the dead are owed.

title: Ironfang Warband
subtitle: The first bite belongs to Kharveth
summary: A sworn band that carries iron teeth and welcomes The Hunger in the midst of a raid.

sections.title: Iron in the mouth
paragraphs: Ironfang warriors wire iron caps over broken teeth. Their chiefs wear the caps of their predecessors on a cord and surrender them only to a successor who has survived The Hunger. Their standards show Kharveth’s teeth facing inward.

sections.title: The open pen
paragraphs: When a warrior begins to change, the priests cut the livestock loose and call the rest of the band to feed. The Ironfangs count every Flint who rises from such a raid as a new voice of Kharveth. They also remember the names of raids from which nobody returned.

title: Bonewatchers
subtitle: The watch at the edge of the white flats
summary: Unsworn raiders who guard their camps against The Hunger and sometimes keep terms with caravans.

sections.title: At the edge of the bones
paragraphs: The Bonewatchers camp along the rim of the Bonewilds, beyond the great white flats. A chief may take salt, livestock or a ransom and guarantee safe passage until the next well. Their sentries remember which caravans paid and which tried to ride around them.

sections.title: Keep the night watch
paragraphs: Pairs of watchers sit apart from the feasting after a raid. At the first sign of a change, they draw the afflicted away from the fires and bar the trail behind them. Their singers name the ancestors who turned away from Kharveth, though they disagree about how long ago the break came.

facts: Paired bone stakes at the edge of camp

title: Ashmaws
subtitle: The jaws beneath the ash
summary: Kharveth’s wandering devotees mark their muzzles with ash and seek out raids foretold by their Flints.

sections.title: The trail of ash
paragraphs: The Ashmaws carry clay jars of ash from the fires of earlier raids. Before marching they rub it into their muzzles and press a jawprint into the dust behind them. A Flint chooses their destination from visions of places they have never seen.

sections.title: What the priests remember
paragraphs: They have crossed the dry country for a granary that offered little plunder, then passed within sight of a wealthy caravan without following it. Their priests claimed they had seen the granary door in a shared vision. The survivors of the raid remembered the Ashmaws calling for someone inside by name.

illustration.alt: An Ashmaw Flint leads ash-marked gnolls through a dry ravine at dusk.
illustration.caption: An Ashmaw Flint leads ash-marked gnolls through a dry ravine at dusk.

title: Redjaws
subtitle: Red jawbones on the sea roads
summary: The Redjaws are Unsworn raiders who learned to sail. Now an almost entirely maritime warband, they strike ferry landings and coastal stores as far north as the Northern Frontier.

sections.title: Life on the sea roads
paragraphs: The Redjaws learned to navigate between islands and now spend most of their time afloat. Their crews read tides, sound unfamiliar channels, and know which sheltered coves can hide a ship until a patrol passes. They still raid ashore, but they choose targets they can reach from the water and load their plunder aboard before the coast can muster a pursuit.

sections.title: The red jaw
paragraphs: The Redjaws dye their jawbone standards with red earth from the drylands. They raid isolated storehouses and ferry landings, then sell what they cannot carry. Their chief will return a captive once a ransom is paid. Settlements that refuse have found their ferryboats gone the following morning.

sections.title: A bargain in the north
paragraphs: Frontier watchmen tell of a Redjaw party that returned its captives under a truce and came back two nights later asking for shelter. The gnolls said they had left one of their own tied below deck after the first signs of The Hunger. By nightfall the ship was drifting back toward the landing.

facts: Maritime raiding along the sea roads

illustration.alt: Redjaw gnoll sailors navigate reef waters at dawn beneath a red jawbone banner.
illustration.caption: Redjaw gnoll sailors navigate reef waters at dawn beneath a red jawbone banner.

title: Embertusks
subtitle: The coals under the black ridge
summary: An orc tribe of the Southern Wilds that carries sacred coals into battle and raids the roads below its shrine.

sections.title: The buried hearth
paragraphs: The Embertusks say their shrine was burning when the first ancestor found it under a split ridge. They carry its coals in lidded clay pots. A war leader puts one down at the foot of a gate before demanding tribute, and the fighters wait for the answer while the pot smokes.

sections.title: The ridge road
paragraphs: They have drawn smaller bands into their ranks by offering access to the shrine and a share of the cattle driven up from the low roads. Some elders want the tribe to hold the ridge. Younger war leaders are pushing farther down the valleys, where a captured crossing can bring in more than a burned farm.

facts: Glowing coals in lidded clay pots

illustration.alt: An orc chief sets down a pot of sacred embers before a valley outpost.
illustration.caption: An orc chief sets down a pot of sacred embers before a valley outpost.

title: Reedskulls
subtitle: What sleeps under the drowned mound
summary: An orc tribe expanding through the wetlands of the Southern Wilds, where it claims the crossings and takes tribute in iron.

sections.title: The drowned mound
paragraphs: The Reedskulls bind reeds around animal skulls and hang them above channels they claim. At the lowest water they wade to a drowned mound and sink an iron offering. Their elders say something underneath learned the sound of their ancestors’ names and still answers when the water is low.

sections.title: The crossings
paragraphs: The tribe has taken more crossings as its numbers have grown. Reedskull parties cut ferry ropes and carry off boats from villages that refuse their demands. They prefer tribute in nails, tools and blades, and each haul renews the dispute over how much to forge and how much to give to the thing below.

illustration.alt: Reedskull orcs carry an iron offering through mist toward a drowned mound.
illustration.caption: Reedskull orcs carry an iron offering through mist toward a drowned mound.

title: Stormchanters
subtitle: Keepers of the Five Skies sanctuary
summary: Orc keepers of a shrine to the Five Skies in the Central Heartland. Once known for their quiet island life, they are preparing for war after Lord Mortimer Vanris laid claim to their shore.

sections.title: The shrine and the prison
paragraphs: Islanders say the five weathered stones on the ridge once marked a shrine to the Five Skies. In a later age the island became a prison for orcs. Below the shrine, families still call the old foundations the prison yard, though nobody agrees on when the last guards left.

sections.title: Listening to the skies
paragraphs: Over generations, the orcs on the island developed a deep bond with the Five Skies. Their shamans keep vigil among the stones and teach children to sit through a change of wind before asking the skies for an answer. The tribe favors a quiet life of fishing, tending the shrine, and settling disputes around the hearth. Families have long formed ties with neighboring ports, and today the island is home to the largest concentration of half-orcs in Kalvatar.

sections.title: An old hatred
paragraphs: The other orc tribes despise the Stormchanters. Their war leaders say the people of the shrine have betrayed what it means to be an orc. The Stormchanters still recite their family lines through the Telling, including the names of the first prisoners. At the end of each recitation, they name the children born since the last one.

sections.title: The port Vanris wanted
paragraphs: The Stormchanters lived peacefully until Lord Mortimer Vanris decided to build a port on their island. Islanders from nearby shores opposed the plan and asked him to build on a neighboring island or negotiate with the orcs. Mortimer took the appeal as an insult. The Stormchanters have since been declared “enemies of Kalvatar.”

sections.title: The storms they called
paragraphs: The Navy made the first attacks, joined by Hunters hired for the campaign. In response, the Stormchanters called up storms powerful enough to sink ships. Their shamans and druids drew on primal powers to destroy any non-orc presence near the island. For the first time, the Stormchanters are preparing for war.
Even the neighboring islanders who spoke in their defense now find themselves turned away. Vanris’s campaign taught the Stormchanters to distrust everyone outside the tribe.

The island sits astride important trade routes in the Central Heartland. The storms now force merchant captains to wait for clear weather or take longer passages. Mortimer wanted a port on a busy route. He now has to contend with a tribe of orcs who know those waters and have chosen to fight for them.

sections.title: Rumors
paragraphs: “For the first time in seventy years, the Stormchanters are talking about joining the other orc tribes in a war.” (heard in the Central Heartland)
“A thunderbird egg rests at the very top of the Stormchanters’ shrine. They say the tribe is keeping watch over it.” (heard in the Central Heartland)

facts: An island in the Central Heartland
Shamanic devotion to the Five Skies
Largest concentration of half-orcs in Kalvatar

illustration.alt: Stormchanter defenders gather at their island shrine as a storm bears down on ships offshore.
illustration.caption: The Stormchanters call a storm over the shipping lanes.
